# Project lifeline: numerical evidence appendix

**Frozen documentary snapshot, 26 September 2026.** Read [the explanatory audit](PROJECT_LIFELINE_AUDIT.md) first. This file preserves the complete central measurement ledger before the retrospective entry, followed by numerical passages from every available phase design and handover, every current implementation plan, and the top-level vision/log records.

**This is an archive, not a list of simultaneously valid results.** Retractions, estimates, proposed targets, old scopes, superseded provider details, and obsolete commands remain visible. The narrative explains the important corrections. In particular, the old ?not a publication project? ledger introduction was superseded on 25 September, the initial 30.3% candidate leak interpretation was corrected, and the Phase 26 fixed-input ?sampling variance? explanation was withdrawn.

**Coverage rule:** the ledger snapshot is complete. For the other named sources, every non-heading Markdown block containing a digit is retained, along with its adjacent blocks for context; section headings are retained. This deliberately over-includes configuration values, years, identifiers, and test counts so that small metrics are not silently omitted. It is not an inventory of every number in raw JSON/JSONL artifacts, nor a claim that every historical observation is valid. Numbers written only in words can occur in the surrounding context but are not a separate exhaustive category.

**Provenance:** each retained block gives its original file and starting line. Source SHA-256 hashes identify the exact file state used. Historical links inside blockquoted excerpts are verbatim and can refer to paths later moved; use the source link and [STRUCTURE.md](../STRUCTURE.md) when needed. Commands inside excerpts are historical evidence, **not instructions or authorisation to run them**. Missing run IDs were not invented. No experiments were rerun to compile this appendix.

## Complete ledger snapshot, sections 1?45

The following blockquote reproduces the source text, including its old introduction, without changing its values or interpretations.

> # docs/MEASUREMENTS.md — the numeric ledger
>
> **Every number, observation and claim this project makes lives here.** Append-only, newest
> section last within each table. This project is **not** on a research-publication pathway
> (maintainer, 2026-09-23), so there is no paper to be the durable home for a figure — this file is.
>
> Rules:
>
> - A number quoted in `LOG.md`, a handover, a commit message or a chat reply **must** have a row
>   here, with the command that reproduces it and the run id that produced it. A figure without a
>   row does not count as recorded.
> - Rows are never edited or deleted. A superseded value gets a **new row** with a new date; the old
>   row stays, so the trajectory is readable.
> - "Observation" rows are as welcome as measured ones — a finding that turned out to be an artefact
>   is exactly the thing that gets rediscovered expensively later.
> - Raw artefacts (JSONL, JSON, HTML audit copies) stay where they are written; this file points at
>   them. See §5.
>
> Related: `docs/PAPERS.md` (per-paper Applied/Reference status), `docs/REFERENCES.md`
> (machine-verified citation metadata), `docs/handover/PHASE_*.md` (the narrative around a phase).
>
> ---
>
> ## 1. Extraction and evaluation quality
>
> Reproduced by: `wiki audit eval -s spice-and-wolf` (zero-cost — local/NLI only, completes with
> every API key unset; `docs/vision/PHASE_27.md`).
>
> | Date | Metric | Value | Command / run | Notes |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | 2026-09-21 | mean gold fact recall | 39.8% | `wiki audit eval -s spice-and-wolf` | Pre-Vertex baseline. |
> | 2026-09-23 | mean gold fact recall | 43.9% | same | After the Vertex flip + four defect fixes (`docs/handover/PHASE_28.md`). |
> | 2026-09-23 | mean gold fact recall | **45.9%** | same | Clean protocol re-run from a fresh gazetteer, extraction temperature pinned 0.1. Current. |
> | 2026-09-23 | fact precision, all ten gold characters | 1.0 | same | Unchanged across every run above. |
> | 2026-09-23 | fact-recall WARNs | 3 of 10 | same | `enek` 25%, `kraft-lawrence` 44%, `yarei` 0%. Left visible on purpose; causes in `docs/handover/PHASE_28.md` §8. |
> | 2026-09-23 | citation entailment, `history` | grounded (492 cited paragraphs) | same | `appearance` / `personality` read "weak overlap" on 1 and 3 cited paragraphs — a sample-size artefact, not a grounding failure. |
> | 2026-09-23 | claims, v01 / v02 | 166+20 / 270+20 | `wiki audit claims -s spice-and-wolf` | Window pass + scene pass. Was 215 / 411 on 2026-09-21. |
> | 2026-09-23 | verify flags raised | 14 across 10 of 14 characters | `wiki verify -s spice-and-wolf --upto 2` | Was 0 — `verify` had been failing open (`{"bad_facts": [...]}` validating against `flags: []`). |
>
> **Observation (2026-09-23) — floors are not ratcheted onto a single run.** A single entity's
> recall carries about ±1 fact of noise at this corpus size, so a floor in
> `docs/eval/gold/spice-and-wolf/baseline.json` is raised only from a run reproduced twice. The
> file's own `_comment` says the same thing.
>
> **Observation (2026-09-23) — `yarei` 0% recall is correct behaviour, not a regression.** The gold
> fact is "held in the barn for a week"; the corpus sentence is conditional ("Yarei *would be*
> locked in a granary … close to a week"). An extractor that declines to assert a hypothetical is
> right and gold is wrong. Fix gold, then re-record the floor — do not tune the floor to silence
> the WARN.
>

> ## 3. Wiki structure and connectivity
>
> The Phase 29 target (`CLAUDE.md` §2b): structure and connectedness that stand next to a
> professional fandom page. Measured on `dist/spice-and-wolf/wiki/v02/`.
>

> | 2026-09-23 | codex roster names rendered as links | 100% (was 0%) | same | Phase 29. Every `Members:` / `Adversaries:` entry now links; the back-edge from a codex entry to a character used to be plain text while the forward edge was a link. |
> | 2026-09-23 | character pages carrying a portrait | 11 of 14 | same | Was 14 of 14, but the v01 frontispiece was the "portrait" on Holo's, Lawrence's **and** Yarei's pages at once. See the observation below. |
> | 2026-09-23 | art plates used on more than 2 pages | 0 (was 1) | same | `_MAX_PAGES_PER_PLATE` in `site/mkdocs_wiki.py`. |
> | 2026-09-23 | `wiki audit links` | OK, 33 routes / 86 pages | `wiki audit links -s spice-and-wolf` | |
> | 2026-09-23 | audits passing | 12 of 12 | each `wiki audit <stage> -s spice-and-wolf` | `eval` OK with the 3 recall WARNs of §1. |
> | 2026-09-23 | pytest | 1028 passed | `pytest` | |
>
> **Observation (2026-09-23) — nothing in this pipeline can see what an art plate depicts.**
> `cover_image_for_entity` answers only "which plate is nearest this character's debut", which
> collides by construction: the v01 frontispiece is nearest the debut of Holo, Lawrence and Yarei
> alike, and the emitter captioned it with each of their names in turn. The fix is a cap
> (front-matter plates only for the two leads; any plate on at most two pages), not a better guess.
> A vision model reading the plates is the only thing that would actually know.
>
> **Observation (2026-09-23) — the codex `related` bucket was information-free on this corpus.**
> It is the entry's personalized-PageRank neighbours, and on a 2-volume graph every place and
> faction alike listed the same four globally-central entities (Medio / Milone / Remelio / Rowen).
> That is a property of PPR at this graph size, not a fact about any entry, so it is no longer
> rendered. It is still computed, still in the bundle and still in `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §6.1 —
> re-render it if a larger graph makes the neighbour sets actually differ per entry.
>
> **Observation (2026-09-23) — `members` and `adversaries` were not mutually exclusive.** Milone
> Company rendered "Members: Kraft Lawrence, Marheit" directly above "Adversaries: Kraft Lawrence,
> Yarei"; Remelio listed Norah Arendt in both. Each came from a real pair of intervals (an employee
> who is also betrayed by the company), but a reader sees a contradiction, not a nuance. Membership
> now wins; the betrayal is still told in prose and on the relationship page.
>

Re-run `python docs/fetch_reference_pdfs.py --check` on a day arXiv answers. |

>
> **Observation (2026-09-23) — the arXiv diagnosis in `docs/handover/PHASE_28.md` §8 needs
> refining.** That entry says arXiv returns 200 for an API URL it has already served and 406 for
> every uncached one. Today's run contradicts the first half: **all 58 tracked ids failed**,
> including ones the script had resolved successfully before. So the failure is not selective
> caching behaviour — on a bad day arXiv is simply unreachable from here for the whole batch. The
> script's "write nothing on a partial fetch" behaviour is what keeps this from corrupting the file,
> and it is the reason the gap is still open rather than half-closed.
>
> **Observation (2026-09-23) — three separate counts, all different.** 58 arXiv ids tracked by the
> script, 54 PDFs in `docs/Sample_Research_Related/`, 51 rows in `docs/REFERENCES.md`. The 58-vs-54
> gap is ids cited without a PDF kept locally; the 54-vs-51 gap is the stale regeneration above.
> `docs/PAPERS.md` is keyed on filename and is complete at 54/54. Reconcile all three the day arXiv
> answers, and record the reconciled numbers here.

> ## 2026-09-01 — Initial vision: spoiler-scoped character wiki from a novel series

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** Given a directory of EPUB volumes for a single series, produce a browsable wiki with one
> page per character containing: canonical name, age, gender, affiliations, titles, nicknames,
> relationships, background and personality. A tab at the top of the site selects "I have read up to
> Volume N" and every page re-renders to that spoiler boundary.

**Original line 16:**

> **Why:** Reading a long series (86—EIGHTY-SIX is 13 volumes / ~936k words) means forgetting who
> people are, but every existing wiki spoils the ending on page one. The volume boundary is the whole
> point of the product; without it this is just another wiki.

**Original line 20:**

> **Implies:** Facts cannot be stored as flat strings. Every fact needs the volume that revealed it,
> and rendering must filter *before* generation, not after.

**Original line 23:**

> **Status:** In progress — Phases 0–8.

**Original line 42:**

> ## Things you need to know

**Original line 44:**

> **`has_heading` must mean "any `<h1>` present," not "matches `chapter_start_selector`."** The
> series config's `chapter_start_selector` is `h1.chapter-number`, which only regular
> chapters/interludes/epilogues use. Front matter (prologue, epigraph) and back matter (afterword)
> use a *different* single heading class (`h1.preface-title`, `h1.appendix-title`, ...). Checking
> only the configured selector silently folded v01's real prologue (`preface002.xhtml`,
> "Coquelicots Blooming Across the Battlefield," ~30 paragraphs) into the epigraph chapter opened by
> `preface001.xhtml` — 16 chapters became 14 and one chapter had the wrong `chapter_kind`. Fixed by
> treating *any* `<h1>` as a new-section marker (continuation docs like `chapter010a.xhtml` reliably
> have none — that is what trap 2 actually distinguishes on), then picking the title node as
> `chapter_title_selector` if present, else the first `<h1>` that isn't the number node. If you touch
> chapter-boundary logic, `tests/test_ingest.py::test_v01_chapter_continuation_absorbs_h1_less_documents`
> guards this.

**Original line 57:**

> **`chapter_kind` is classified heading-text-first, not epub:type-first.** Across the corpus, the
> heading text itself says "PROLOGUE" / "INTERLUDE" / "EPILOGUE" far more consistently (in 8-9 of
> 13 volumes each) than `epub:type` does (`frontmatter prologue` appears in only 2 of 13 volumes'
> markup, `backmatter epilogue` in only 1). Priority: heading text → `epub:type` tokens → presence of
> a `div.epigraph` wrapper (to split "preface" into prologue vs. epigraph) → default `"chapter"`.
> See `epub._classify_kind`.

**Original line 64:**

> **Never iterate `Tag.descendants` while mutating the tree.** `substitute_and_strip_images()`
> rewrites the tree via `.replace_with()`/`.decompose()`. BeautifulSoup's `.descendants` generator
> walks live `next_element` links, so mutating mid-iteration corrupts the remaining walk in ways that
> do not raise — paragraphs after a substitution can silently go missing. `epub._extract_paragraphs`
> snapshots with `list(container.descendants)` before the loop starts. If you add another
> tree-mutating step inside that loop, keep the snapshot.

**Original line 71:**

> **`print_page` is legitimately `null` for all of v02, v03, v04, and v10, and mostly null in v01
> after the first few pages of some chapters.** Those EPUBs don't carry `<a id="page-N">` anchors in
> the body text at all (v02 has exactly one, on the title, with no number); this is a source-file
> difference, not an extraction bug — CONTRACTS section 1 already documents `print_page` as
> best-effort ("null if none seen yet").

**Original line 77:**

> **BeautifulSoup already decodes entities during parsing** (verified: `&lt;System Start&gt;` in raw
> XHTML comes back as `<System Start>` from `.get_text()`). Trap 6 ("decode entities only after tag
> stripping") is naturally satisfied by working on the parsed tree and calling `.get_text()` rather
> than doing string-level tag stripping — `normalize.normalize_paragraph_text`'s `html.unescape()`
> call is a defensive no-op for this corpus, not the actual fix.

**Original line 83:**

> **Console `�` in tool output is a Windows-terminal display artifact, not a data bug.** Verified
> by checking codepoints directly (`—` is U+2014, `É` is U+00C9 in the actual JSONL bytes). Don't
> "fix" encoding based on how text looks printed in a shell.

**Original line 87:**

> **`toc.xhtml`/`nav.xhtml`/`toc.ncx` are never parsed.** Every content document carries its own
> `<h1>` heading(s) in-body, which is a strictly more reliable source of chapter titles than the TOC
> (confirmed nav.xhtml's break in v02/v03 doesn't matter here). `epub.toc_sources` in the series
> config is unused by ingestion; it's left in place in case a future series needs it, since the
> config is meant to be series-agnostic and some series' TOCs may carry information their body text
> doesn't.

**Original line 94:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 96:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | `ebooklib` for spine/OPF/metadata, raw `BeautifulSoup` (lxml parser) per document | Spine order and metadata extraction are exactly what ebooklib is for; hand-rolling OPF parsing would just re-implement it with more bugs | Manual `zipfile` + `lxml.etree` parsing of `container.xml`/`.opf` |
> | `soup.find("h1")` (any h1) as the chapter-start signal | The only signal proven consistent across chapter, interlude, prologue, epigraph, epilogue, and afterword documents, all of which use different heading classes | `chapter_start_selector` alone — misses front/back matter, see above |
> | Heading-text-first `chapter_kind` classification | Heading text says "PROLOGUE"/"INTERLUDE"/"EPILOGUE" outright in most volumes; `epub:type` is inconsistent across the 13 volumes' toolchains | epub:type-first classification |
> | `image_page_max_words` filter applied only to headless (continuation) documents | A real chapter that happens to open with a short, image-heavy page must never be silently dropped; only pure art-plate continuations (half-title, insert pages) should be | Applying the word-count filter to every document regardless of heading |
> | No windowing/scene-segmentation logic in `segment.py` yet | Not needed until `extract/windows.py` (Phase 3) builds evidence windows; adding it now would be speculative code with no caller | Building the windowing helpers now since the file map mentions them |

> ## 2026-09-01 — Aho-Corasick as the retrieval and cost mechanism

*Non-numerical blocks omitted here; consult the linked source for uninterrupted prose.*

**Original line 34:**

> **Why:** It serves three needs at once, and it is deterministic and free. It performs the automated
> wikification the reference document calls for; it gives alias-aware mention counts for ranking
> characters by importance; and — most importantly — it is the token lever. Knowing exactly which
> paragraphs name a character means an extraction prompt never contains text irrelevant to its subject.

**Original line 39:**

> **Implies:** `entities/automaton.py` is built before any extraction runs. Extraction reads mention
> windows, never whole chapters. Alias resolution quality directly bounds recall, so Phase 2 is the
> phase to hand-audit.

**Original line 43:**

> **Status:** Planned — Phase 2.

**Original line 45:**

> ---

**Original line 48:**

> ## 2026-09-02 — EcphoryRAG evaluated and rejected; token strategy stays extraction-time

**Original line 50:**

> **What:** EcphoryRAG (arXiv 2510.08958, Oct 2025) was evaluated as a replacement for the
> Aho-Corasick + claim-extraction design and **rejected**. Its headline "94% token reduction" is an
> *offline indexing* saving obtained by storing only `(id, name, type, description, source_chunk)`
> per entity and **not extracting relations at index time at all** — edges are bare co-occurrence
> (undirected, unweighted, untyped), and relations are inferred at query time by embedding-space
> multi-hop search feeding raw chunks to a generator LLM. Its own Table 1 shows query-time cost
> *higher* than vanilla RAG (1.3M vs 848k QT tokens).

**Original line 58:**

> **Why rejected:** Three hard mismatches. (1) It has no typed predicates, so it cannot render
> Affiliations/Relationships deterministically from graph rows (rule §2). (2) It has no fact-level
> provenance or validity intervals — the paper never addresses temporal change or contradiction —
> so it cannot support `first_vol`, interval supersession, or the spoiler invariant (§1). (3) It is
> a *query-time* architecture; this project is *build-time*, emitting a static site where every page
> at every cutoff must already exist. There is no reader query to spend its "strategic query-time
> investment" on. Its savings come precisely from skipping the step that is this project's core
> deliverable.

**Original line 67:**

> **Implies:** No architecture change. `entities/automaton.py` remains the retrieval mechanism —
> for a small, closed, fully-processed corpus, exact Aho-Corasick mention indexing gives 100% recall
> at zero token cost, which embedding top-k retrieval cannot beat here.

**Original line 71:**

**Original line 46:**

> ## Things you need to know

**Original line 48:**

> **Candidate mining trades precision for recall, on purpose** (VISION.md/PROMPTS.md design
> philosophy: a wrong candidate costs one wasted classify call and is caught by classify.py or the
> human roster review; a missed candidate is invisible and never recovered). The miner finds
> maximal runs of 1-4 consecutive capitalised tokens, single-space-separated — punctuation, a
> second space, or a lowercase token breaks the run. Two things prune the obvious junk before it
> even reaches the LLM:
> - A small hand-maintained stopword set (`_GENERIC_STOPWORDS` in `candidates.py`) for common
>   pronouns/articles/conjunctions.
> - A **corpus frequency-ratio filter**: a single-token candidate is kept only if it is
>   capitalised at least 75% of the times that exact word (any case) appears anywhere in the
>   volumes being mined. Real names are almost always capitalised; ordinary words ("in", "not",
>   "don['t]") are capitalised only when they happen to open a sentence, so most of their
>   occurrences are lowercase. This is what catches sentence-initial junk a fixed stoplist can't
>   enumerate in advance — it caught things the stoplist alone missed ("In", "Not", "To", "All",
>   "Having", "Don"). Multi-word candidates skip this filter; a 2+ word capitalised run is
>   essentially never a false positive on its own.

**Original line 65:**

> **A capitalised run's regex deliberately does not swallow a trailing apostrophe.** An earlier
> version matched `Shin's`/`I'm`/`That's` as their own candidates, distinct from `Shin`/`I`/`That`
> — splitting a real name's count across two surfaces and flooding the candidate list with
> contraction junk. Dropping the apostrophe from the token pattern folds the possessive/
> contraction back into the base token for free. If you touch `_TOKEN_RE`, rerun
> `test_possessive_and_contraction_fold_into_base_token`.

**Original line 72:**

> **Honorific detection has to look in two places, not one.** A single-token honorific check
> ("does the text right before this candidate say 'Major '?") fails for the common case, because
> `Major Milizé` is itself ONE capitalised run — `Major` is inside the matched surface, not before
> it. `_preceded_by_honorific` in `candidates.py` checks both: does the surface's own first word
> match an honorific, and (for an honorific the run-regex didn't capture, e.g. `Dr. Milizé` where
> the period breaks the run) does the text immediately preceding the run match one. This was
> caught by `test_honorific_signal_detected` failing during this phase — if you touch honorific
> detection, keep that test.

**Original line 81:**

> **`entity_id` collisions are a real, not hypothetical, case.** Two different-typed clusters can
> land on the same canonical text (e.g. a faction and a piece of tech both plausibly named
> "Spearhead" in a different series) and `slugify()` would give them the same `entity_id`. Nothing
> downstream (`_apply_overrides`'s `by_id` dict, `automaton.build_automaton`'s per-entity mention
> tagging) can tolerate that silently — it was caught by
> `test_different_types_never_auto_merge_even_if_identical_text` (the *type* stayed unmerged in
> the union-find, but the two same-slug entities silently collapsed into one dict entry one step
> later). `_build_clusters` now disambiguates with a `-2`, `-3`, ... suffix. If you add another
> place that builds a lookup dict keyed by `entity_id`, assume collisions are possible, not rare.

**Original line 91:**

> **True nickname/call-sign aliases ("Shin" -> "Undertaker") are never textually similar**, so a
> fuzzy-string-only approach to picking which pairs are worth an LLM call would never even propose
> them. `alias.py`'s tier-d pair discovery adds a second, independent trigger: two candidates that
> share at least one evidence `para_id` (both were seen in at least one of the same sampled
> paragraphs) are also LLM-eligible, regardless of string similarity. This is why
> `candidates.py::_MAX_EVIDENCE_PER_CANDIDATE` was raised from 8 to 40 — co-occurrence detection
> only has as much recall as the evidence sample it's checking against. It is still best-effort,
> not exhaustive (a candidate seen hundreds of times only keeps 40 sampled paragraphs); a genuine
> miss is exactly what `entity_overrides.aliases` in the series config exists to patch by hand —
> see the worked `Baleygr` example already in `config/series.86.yaml`'s comments. When ranking
> which of the (capped at `MAX_LLM_PAIRS = 300`) eligible pairs actually get an LLM call,
> co-occurrence pairs are prioritised ahead of fuzzy-band pairs, since a fuzzy-ratio sort alone
> would push the (textually dissimilar, by definition) nickname pairs to the back of the list.

**Original line 105:**

> **`entity_overrides.split` cannot automatically decide which mention belongs to which target.**
> Given `{entity: "nouzen", into: ["shinei-nouzen", "kiriya-nouzen"]}`, there is no way for
> corpus-wide mention counts alone to know which specific occurrences of "Nouzen" refer to which
> person — that's a real coreference problem outside what this phase's evidence gives it. The
> implemented behaviour: the original merged cluster is deleted and replaced with the listed
> target ids as new, empty entities (0 mentions, no surface forms, confidence 0.5, a note pointing
> at this fact). A human then populates each target via a follow-up `entity_overrides.aliases`
> entry per target and reruns `wiki gazetteer --force`. This is a deliberate, documented gap, not
> an oversight — see `test_entity_overrides_split_creates_empty_targets`.

**Original line 115:**

> **The Aho-Corasick automaton enforces word boundaries itself.** Neither pyahocorasick nor the
> pure-Python fallback has a boundary concept, so without this "Shin" would fire inside "Shining".
> `automaton._is_boundary_match` checks the character immediately before/after each raw match
> isn't alphanumeric/apostrophe, applied identically to both backends before the longest-match-
> wins overlap resolution (`start` ascending, then longest first, greedy non-overlapping sweep).

**Original line 121:**

> **`wiki doctor` already reports which automaton backend is active** ("pyahocorasick (C
> extension)" vs "ahocorapy (pure Python, slower but correct)" per the Phase 0 handover) — this
> phase's own `pyproject.toml` fallback dependency is `ahocorapy`, but `automaton.py` does NOT
> call into it. Its API wasn't worth depending on sight-unseen; instead there's a small internal
> pure-Python fallback (linear multi-substring scan per surface, O(entities x text) instead of
> O(text) — correct, just not the fast path) that activates automatically whenever
> `import ahocorasick` fails. `MentionAutomaton.backend` reports which one is live. This machine's
> pyahocorasick import succeeded (confirmed via the smoke tests), so the fallback path is
> untested against ahocorapy specifically — only exercised by unit tests that force
> `_HAS_PYAHOCORASICK = False`... actually it isn't forced anywhere; **if you need to verify the
> fallback path, monkeypatch `automaton._HAS_PYAHOCORASICK = False` and `automaton.ahocorasick =
> None`** before building an automaton in a test. Not done in this phase — a known gap, not a
> claim of coverage that doesn't exist.

**Original line 135:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 137:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | Regex + frequency-ratio candidate mining, no NLP library | Zero dependencies, deterministic, fast enough to mine all 13 volumes in well under a second; the LLM classify stage and human roster review are the accuracy backstop by design | spaCy NER — heavier dependency, and still needs the same human-review safety net for a translated light novel's invented names |
> | Tiered clustering (free tiers a-c, LLM only for tier d) with a hard `MAX_LLM_PAIRS` cap | Bounds cost on a corpus with hundreds of candidates per volume; PROMPTS.md's own design rule is "one decision per call" plus conservative defaults | Asking the LLM about every candidate pair (O(n^2), unbounded cost) |
> | Co-occurrence as a second, independent tier-d trigger alongside fuzzy similarity | Fuzzy similarity alone structurally cannot find true nicknames/call-signs; this was found and fixed mid-phase, see notes above | Fuzzy-similarity-only pair discovery (the first draft; would have silently never merged "Shin"/"Undertaker") |
> | `entity_overrides.split` creates empty stub targets for a human to populate | Automatic per-mention disambiguation is a real coreference problem this phase's evidence can't solve; matches the project's own stated design (roster.html + config overrides as the human-in-the-loop safety net) | Attempting an automatic split heuristic (e.g. by evidence volume) — would silently misattribute facts with no way for a reviewer to notice |
> | Internal pure-Python Aho-Corasick fallback instead of depending on `ahocorapy`'s exact API | Avoids guessing at an unverified third-party API; correctness is what matters for the fallback path (rarely hit — this machine has the C extension), not speed | Wiring the declared `ahocorapy` dependency directly |

> ## 2026-09-02 — Mistral API standing in for local Ollama; testing scope capped at 1-2 volumes

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** (1) `config/models.yaml` routing for `entity_classify`, `entity_alias`, `claim_extract`,
> `codex_summary`, and `prose` now points at new `mistral_fast` / `mistral_prose` profiles
> (provider `openai`, `base_url: https://api.mistral.ai/v1`, model `mistral-small-latest`, a 24B
> model) instead of `local_fast` / `local_prose` (Ollama). `prose_polish` / `arbitrate` fall back to

> unchanged, for whenever a local server is available again. (2) Until this project reaches a phase
> where a full-corpus run is actually intended, any test, benchmark, or "real run" performed during
> implementation is scoped to volumes 1-2 only, never the full 13-volume series.

**Original line 20:**

> **Why:** No Ollama server is reachable in the current working environment (see Phase 3 gaps in

**Original line 25:**

> **Implies:** `claim_extract` no longer satisfies "Local first" (`CLAUDE.md` §2) for the current

> full-series extraction should first re-point `routing.claim_extract` back to `local_fast` once

**Original line 31:**

> **Status:** Done (config only) — 2026-09-02.

**Original line 33:**

> ---

**Original line 36:**

> ## 2026-09-02 — Token-efficiency programme (Phase 3.5), quality held constant

**Original line 38:**

> **What:** Five cost levers, ordered by expected impact, to be implemented as Phase 3.5 before any
> multi-volume extraction run. Quality is a constraint, not a variable: no lever may reduce claim
> recall, drop evidence, or weaken the verbatim-quote validation.

**Original line 42:**

> 1. **Window-major (joint multi-entity) extraction.** `extract/claims.py` currently calls the model
>    once per *(character, window)* — `extract_character_volume` builds windows per entity, and
>    line ~329 already computes the other characters in the window and then discards them. A scene
>    naming five characters is therefore sent five times. Restructure to iterate over deduplicated
>    windows and extract claims for every character mentioned in that window in one call. Saving is
>    the mean entities-per-window factor — **to be measured on v01-02, not assumed**.
> 2. **Prompt caching.** The claims system prompt (schema + closed predicate vocabulary + example)
>    is byte-identical across every call. Mistral bills cached prefix tokens at 10% of input price
>    via a stable `prompt_cache_key`; the `openai.py` adapter must pass it and the prefix must stay
>    first and unchanged.
> 3. **Batch API.** This pipeline is entirely offline — latency is irrelevant. Mistral's batch
>    endpoint is a documented 50% discount and composes with caching.
> 4. **Strict structured outputs.** Replace `response_format: json_object` with a JSON *schema*.
>    Every repair retry currently re-sends the whole window (`json_repair_attempts: 2`), and
>    `_salvage_truncated_array` exists because truncation is real; schema enforcement plus a correct
>    `max_tokens` removes that entire class of wasted call.
> 5. **Encoder-based window triage (optional, measure first).** GLiNER-Relex-style joint NER+RE runs
>    locally in one forward pass at zero API cost. Use it only to *triage* windows unlikely to carry
>    any new attribute/relation, at a deliberately permissive threshold, and only if a v01-02
>    recall check shows it drops no claims the LLM would have found. The 5070 Ti is idle now that
>    generation moved off Ollama.

**Original line 64:**

> **Explicitly rejected:** prompt/context compression (LLMLingua-style). `claims.py` drops any claim
> whose quote is not verbatim in its cited paragraph; compressing input text destroys exactly the
> fidelity that validation depends on.

**Original line 68:**

> **Why:** The bulk stage now costs real money per call (2026-09-02 Mistral entry). Lever 1 is also
> a *correctness* win — document-level joint extraction avoids the per-entity pipeline's error
> propagation, and it directly fixes Phase 3's known gap that symmetric relations are extracted twice
> from both sides and never deduplicated.

**Original line 73:**

> **Implies:** `extract/claims.py` restructured window-major (prompt rule "one subject per call" in
> `PROMPTS.md` is superseded); `llm/client.py` grows a batch submission path and cache-key support;
> `llm/providers/openai.py` passes `prompt_cache_key` and a JSON schema. Every lever is measured on
> volumes 1-2 only, per the same-dated testing-scope entry above.

**Original line 68:**

> ## Things you need to know

**Original line 70:**

> **Windows, not chapters, are the unit of extraction — and `wiki extract` calls the model once per
> window, not once per character.** PROMPTS.md says the `claim_extract` prompt "runs once per
> character per volume"; read that as naming the prompt template, not the call count. In practice a
> protagonist named 785 times in one volume (the real v01 count for Shin's surface forms) still
> produces at most `max_windows_per_entity_per_volume` (40, from `extraction.yaml`) calls, because
> `extract/windows.py` clusters nearby mentions into merged windows first and then caps the total,
> keeping the densest clusters. The smoke test's 80-call total (2 characters × 40) is the cap
> working as designed, not a bug.

**Original line 79:**

> **A claim's `object` is resolved only against entities already mentioned in the same window's
> `mentions.jsonl` records, never against the whole gazetteer.** This is deliberate, not a
> shortcut: it means the model cannot produce a relation to a name it did not actually read in the
> passage it was given — see PROMPTS.md rule 4 ("evidence is mandatory and verbatim") applied to
> entity resolution as well as quotes. `claims.py::_resolve_object` tries an exact surface match
> first, then substring containment, both case-insensitive. If a real run shows a lot of
> `unresolved_object` drops for an obviously-present name, the likely cause is the window's context
> paragraphs not including the sentence that names the object — not a resolver bug — since
> `extraction.window.context_paragraphs_before/after` bounds how far a window reaches.

**Original line 89:**

> **Repeated observations of the same fact merge by `claim_id`, not by window.** `claim_id` is
> `sha1(subject, predicate, object_norm, first_vol)[:8]` (`schema.make_claim_id`), so if two
> different windows in the same volume both support `(shinei-nouzen, AFFILIATED_WITH,
> spearhead-squadron)`, they land on the identical id and `claims.py::_merge_claim` combines their
> evidence lists and keeps the higher confidence — this is what let the smoke test's 40 separate
> `PERSONALITY` observations collapse into one claim with 40 evidence items instead of 40
> claims. A *different* value for the same `(subject, predicate, first_vol)` — e.g. two different
> ages stated in the same volume — deliberately does **not** merge, since `object_norm` differs;
> both claims are written, which is exactly the shape `graph/contradictions.py` needs in Phase 4 to
> arbitrate a same-volume conflict (CONTRACTS §4.2). Don't "fix" this by merging on
> `(subject, predicate, first_vol)` alone — that would silently pick a winner here, a full phase
> too early.

**Original line 102:**

> **Verbatim-quote checking happens twice, on purpose, and that's not redundant.**
> `claims.py::_build_claim` drops a fact immediately if its quote isn't a literal substring of the
> cited paragraph — this is the main defense against a confident 14B model inventing a plausible
> quote (PROMPTS.md rule 4), so a bad quote never reaches the claims file at all. `wiki audit
> claims` re-checks every written claim's quote against the paragraph independently, reading only
> `data/03_claims/*.jsonl` and `data/01_parsed/*.jsonl` — it would only fail if `_build_claim`'s
> check had a bug, or if a claims file were hand-edited or corrupted. Keep both: the first is a
> filter, the second is a trust-but-verify audit of the file that's actually on disk.

**Original line 111:**

> **`extraction_behaviour` is a new `Settings` property (`config.py`), not new config.** It just

*Non-numerical blocks omitted here; consult the linked source for uninterrupted prose.*

**Original line 127:**

> **Trait `max_words` (extraction.yaml) is a prompt instruction only, not a code-level filter.**
> `claims.py` does not reject a `PERSONALITY`/`SKILL`/etc. value for being a few words over its
> configured `max_words` — enforcing that in code risks discarding a genuinely good short phrase
> over a soft length heuristic. If real extraction shows traits routinely running long (a sentence
> instead of a phrase), tighten the prompt wording first before adding a code-level cutoff.

**Original line 133:**

> **Symmetric relations (`SIBLING_OF`, `FRIEND_OF`, ...) are not deduplicated across subjects at
> this phase.** Extraction asks "what do we learn about character X" independently for every
> character, so a passage naming both A and B as friends can produce both `(A, FRIEND_OF, B)` (while
> processing A) and `(B, FRIEND_OF, A)` (while processing B) as two separate claims — this is
> expected, matches "extraction = claims table verbatim," and `extraction.yaml`'s own comment
> ("`symmetric` relations are stored once and rendered from both sides") describes graph-layer
> normalization, which is Phase 4's job (`graph/temporal.py`/`edges`), not this phase's.

**Original line 141:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 143:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | One LLM call per evidence window (up to `max_windows_per_entity_per_volume` per character per volume) | Matches the token-budget design in VISION.md/PROMPTS.md exactly — a window is already capped at `max_tokens_per_request`; one call per window keeps each request small and cacheable | One call per character per volume with all windows concatenated — breaks the per-request token cap and produces one giant, harder-to-repair JSON response |
> | Resolve relation objects against the window's own `mentions.jsonl` entries only | Guarantees a claim's object was actually named in the cited passage; free (mentions are already computed by Phase 2), no fuzzy matching needed | Fuzzy-matching the model's object text against the whole gazetteer — could resolve to an entity never mentioned in the passage at all, silently inventing evidence |
> | Content-addressed `claim_id` (hash of subject/predicate/object_norm/first_vol), with evidence merged across windows on a matching id | Naturally collapses hundreds of repeat observations of the same fact into one claim with rich evidence, and keeps same-volume *conflicting* values as separate claims for Phase 4 to arbitrate | Deduplicating by `(subject, predicate)` alone — would either drop legitimate conflicting values or need a separate "pending arbitration" side table a phase early |
> | Drop a claim outright on any verbatim-quote or unresolved-object failure, rather than repairing or flagging it | PROMPTS.md rule 4: evidence is the main defense against hallucination; a claim without real evidence isn't a weaker claim, it's not a claim | Keeping the claim with a `flagged` status for a human to review — adds a review queue this phase's scope (CONTRACTS §3) doesn't call for; `wiki audit claims`' FAIL check exists for exactly this instead |
> | `extraction_behaviour` as a new `Settings` property | One property, matching the existing `client_config`/`budget_config` pattern, versus repeating `settings.extraction["extraction"][...]` at every call site | Reading the raw dict directly in `windows.py`/`claims.py` — works, but scatters the same three-level lookup across two modules |

**Original line 151:**

> ## What Phase 4 must do

**Original line 153:**

> Implement `graph/{store,temporal,contradictions}.py` and register `wiki audit contradictions`.
> Read `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §4 for the graph schema before writing anything.

**Original line 156:**

> Useful things this phase leaves behind: `data/03_claims/v{NN}.jsonl` already has same-volume
> conflicting claims as **separate, distinctly-`claim_id`'d records** (see the claim-merge note
> above) — `graph/contradictions.py` does not need to detect a conflict by comparing values across
> files, it needs to *group* claims sharing `(subject, predicate, first_vol)` and check whether their
> `object`/`value` differ. Cross-volume claims for the same `(subject, predicate)` are similarly
> already separate records (different `first_vol`, hence different `claim_id`); Phase 4 turns those
> into interval supersession per CONTRACTS §4.1. `evidence` on every claim already carries whatever
> `print_page`/`quote` the arbitration prompt (`arbitrate_conflict`, PROMPTS.md) will need to show
> the model both sides of a same-volume conflict.

**Original line 166:**

> ## Known gaps, deliberately left

**Original line 168:**

> - No real end-to-end run against Ollama happened in this phase either (same sandbox limitation as
>   Phase 2) — verified instead via unit tests plus one monkeypatched-provider smoke run against
>   real v01 text with a hand-built gazetteer fixture. **Run a real `wiki gazetteer` then a real
>   `wiki extract` before Phase 4** — this is now the single most important next action, carried
>   forward from Phase 2's own handover.

> - Trait `max_words` is prompt guidance only, not code-enforced (see notes above).
> - Symmetric relations are not deduplicated across the two subjects that both observe them — by
>   design, left for Phase 4's graph normalization (see notes above), not an oversight.
> - `extract/claims.py` calls the model once per window with no batching across windows of the same
>   character — correct and matches the token-budget design, but means a very talkative protagonist

**Original line 60:**

> ## Things you need to know

**Original line 62:**

> **Only `attributes.<PREDICATE>.single: true` (config/extraction.yaml) goes through
> tie-resolution and supersession.** Everything else — relations, non-single attributes (TITLE,
> NICKNAME, APPEARANCE), traits (PERSONALITY, BACKGROUND, ...) — is multi-valued by design: a
> character can have several friends, several nicknames, several personality traits at once, and
> none of that is a conflict. `contradictions.py::build_graph` routes single-attribute claims to
> `_resolve_single_valued`; everything else goes straight to `temporal.py::assign_multi_valued` with
> no arbitration call at all. **Do not add relation-supersession** ("stopped being friends") without
> a config flag to opt individual predicates into it — nothing in extraction.yaml currently asks for
> it, and inventing it here would be a full phase early, same caution Phase 3's handover gave for
> claim merging.

**Original line 73:**

> **Symmetric and inverse relation pairs are canonicalised to ONE storage direction, deterministically,
> by predicate name.** `_canonicalize_relation` picks whichever of `{predicate, inverse(predicate)}`
> sorts first alphabetically as the canonical predicate; for a symmetric relation it instead sorts
> `(subject, object)` lexicographically. This closes the exact gap Phase 3's handover flagged
> ("Symmetric relations are extracted independently from both sides and not deduplicated... Phase
> 4's job") — verified for real: v01-02 actually contained a `(shin, FRIEND_OF, raiden)` /
> `(raiden, FRIEND_OF, shin)` pair from independent per-character extraction, and it collapsed to one
> edge. **The canonical direction is an implementation detail, not a contract** — CONTRACTS §4 does
> not name a direction — so a query for "X's relations" must check `subject = X OR object = X` for
> predicates with an `inverse`/`symmetric` flag; `graph/ppr.py` (Phase 5) needs to know this or it
> will silently miss half the edges touching a given entity.

**Original line 85:**

> **A same-volume group with more than 2 conflicting values only arbitrates the top 2 by
> confidence.** `claim_id` merging in `extract/claims.py` already guarantees every claim in a
> `(subject, predicate, first_vol)` group has a genuinely distinct value (identical values already
> share a `claim_id`), so ">2" means 3+ actually different extracted values for one attribute in one
> volume — rare, and never occurred in the real v01-02 run. The 3rd+ entries are logged as a
> `rule:lowest_confidence_dropped` conflict without an LLM call, to avoid chaining N-1 arbitration
> calls for what is very likely one clearly-wrong outlier among the low-confidence entries. If a
> future real run on more volumes shows this happening often with a non-obvious outlier, revisit —
> right now it is an unexercised, deliberately cheap default, not a validated design.

**Original line 95:**

> **`state_at`/`history_at` return rows whose `vol_end` can be in the future relative to the query's
> `vol`.** This is correct for *which rows are true* (an interval closing at volume 8 is still true
> at a cutoff-3 read), but a row's raw `vol_end` field must never be printed verbatim by a renderer
> at a cutoff earlier than that `vol_end` — doing so tells a Volume-3 reader that this fact changes
> at Volume 8, before they have read Volume 8. **This is Phase 5's responsibility, not something
> `temporal.py` enforces** — `state_at` is documented (see its docstring) as answering "is this row
> true", not "which of this row's fields are safe to show". `synth/assemble.py` must scrub
> `vol_end`/`superseded_by` down to "changes later" (no number) rather than pass the real value
> through, or `tests/test_spoiler_leak.py`-style leakage happens one field at a time instead of one
> whole claim at a time.

**Original line 106:**

> **`quiet_change` (extraction.yaml `conflicts:` block: AGE/RANK/TITLE/OCCUPATION) is read by
> NOTHING in this phase.** Every cross-volume value change is logged as a `narrative_change`
> conflict identically regardless of predicate — the "don't show this as a flashy UI change badge"
> behavior `quiet_change` names is a rendering decision, deferred to whatever Phase 5 module builds
> the "this changed" marker; it should read `settings.conflicts_config["quiet_change"]` directly
> against an interval's `predicate` rather than expecting `contradictions.json` to carry a flag for
> it (it does not, and should not — the conflict itself is not "quiet", only its rendering is).

**Original line 114:**

> **`graph build` has no `--force` and always fully rebuilds.** Unlike `ingest`/`gazetteer`/`extract`
> (which skip a volume whose output file already exists), the graph has one combined output computed
> fresh from `data/03_claims/*.jsonl` every time — cheap (all-local except the rare `arbitrate` call,
> which is itself LLM-cached) and, critically, *must not* be incremental: a claim removed or changed
> upstream has to actually disappear from `intervals`/`edges`, which `INSERT OR REPLACE`-by-key alone
> cannot guarantee. `cli.py::graph_build` calls `store.reset(conn)` unconditionally before writing.

**Original line 121:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 123:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | Only `single: true` attributes get conflict/supersession handling | Matches extraction.yaml's own documented semantics exactly ("single: true... makes rank promotions render as history rather than a contradiction"); relations/traits/non-single attributes are legitimately multi-valued | Detecting a "conflict" whenever any two claims share `(subject, predicate, first_vol)` with different values — would misfire on every character with two friends, two nicknames, or two personality traits |
> | Canonical relation direction chosen deterministically by predicate/subject-object sort order | Fully general — one rule handles every symmetric and inverse pair in extraction.yaml with no per-predicate special-casing, and is a pure function of the config, not of extraction order | Picking canonical direction by whichever claim was extracted/written first — nondeterministic across reruns, and wrong to depend on iteration order for something that must be stable in the DB |
> | Top-2-by-confidence arbitration for a >2-way same-volume conflict, rest rule-dropped | Keeps `_resolve_pair`'s schema and prompt binary (matches PROMPTS.md's own framing: "two same-volume claims disagree"); >2 genuinely distinct values for one attribute in one volume is rare and unexercised | An N-way arbitration prompt/schema — real complexity for a case that did not occur in the actual v01-02 run; add it if a larger run shows it matters |
> | `flag`/`keep_both` on a single-valued attribute still picks a provisional value (highest confidence) for interval-building, while the conflict itself is still logged with `resolution: "flag"`/`"keep_both"` | CONTRACTS §4.2's "never silently pick a winner" is about not hiding the conflict, not about halting the whole graph build over one ambiguous attribute; the audit report surfaces every flagged item for a human | Leaving a gap in the interval sequence, or refusing to build the graph — either breaks every other subject/predicate in the same run over one ambiguous case |
> | `graph build` unconditionally resets and rebuilds; no `--force` flag | The output is one combined artifact computed fresh from claims every time, not per-volume files that are expensive to redo; `INSERT OR REPLACE` alone cannot delete a stale row for a claim that no longer exists | A `--force` flag mirroring `ingest`/`gazetteer`/`extract` — would invite a "skip if `graph.db` exists" default that goes stale the moment claims change |

**Original line 131:**

> ## What Phase 5 must do

**Original line 133:**

> Build `synth/assemble.py` (the page model, CONTRACTS §5) and `graph/ppr.py` (multi-hop evidence via
> Personalized PageRank over the volume-filtered subgraph — CLAUDE.md file map). Read
> `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §5 before writing anything.

**Original line 137:**

> Useful things this phase leaves behind: `graph/temporal.py::state_at(conn, entity_id, vol)` /

**Original line 145:**

**Original line 147:**

> - Relation intervals never close — no "the friendship/command relationship ended" modelling.

>   as a limitation anywhere else; noting it here is that.

**Original line 9:**

> ## 2026-09-02 — Page fields are generic per predicate; PPR feeds `mentions_of`; `wiki explain` ships

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** Three decisions, landed together as Phase 5: (1) `synth/assemble.py`'s page-model
> `fields` are keyed by `predicate.lower()` for every `config/extraction.yaml` attribute, not a
> hard-coded name list — CONTRACTS §5's example previously showed `titles`/`nicknames` as if those
> were special-cased. (2) `graph/ppr.py`'s Personalized PageRank output populates `mentions_of`
> directly — the multi-hop related-entity list this project's own file map already promised, now
> wired to something concrete. (3) `wiki explain "<name>" --upto N` is real, not a stub, and prints
> the assembled fields, the evidence quotes behind each one, and the PPR-ranked related entities.

**Original line 19:**

> **Why:** `config/extraction.yaml`'s own header says "Adding a predicate or attribute here is all
> that is needed — rendering is generic." Hard-coding `titles`/`nicknames` as named fields (as
> CONTRACTS' original example did) would silently drop any new attribute a future series' config
> adds — a direct violation of "series-agnostic by construction" (2026-09-01 entry above). PPR
> existed only as a file-map bullet with no consumer; `mentions_of` was an unfilled CONTRACTS field
> with no producer. Pairing them was the obvious, and only, use for either one at this phase.

**Original line 26:**

> **Implies:** A real-data run of `wiki explain shin --upto 1` surfaced a genuine spoiler leak before
> this shipped: `extract/claims.py` merges repeated observations of the same fact into one
> `claim_id`, so a claim with `first_vol = 1` can carry a `v02` quote confirming it again later.
> `first_vol <= upto_vol` clears the claim for structured rendering, but says nothing about which of
> its *individual quotes* are safe to print — the original `explain` printed all of them. Fixed by
> adding `graph/temporal.py::evidence_at(claim_ids, vol)`, which filters each quote by its own
> para_id volume; `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §4.1 and the module's own docstring now document this as a
> fifth sanctioned read, alongside `state_at`/`history_at`/`relations_at`/`all_edges_at`. Phase 6's
> `synth/prose.py`, when it cites evidence for the LLM prompt, must call `evidence_at` too — reading
> `claims.evidence_json` any other way reproduces the same bug.

**Original line 37:**

> `nx.pagerank()` needs scipy, which is not a declared dependency and was not installed; rather than
> adding a new heavy dependency for a graph of a few hundred nodes, `graph/ppr.py` hand-rolls
> personalized PageRank as a pure-Python power iteration. Revisit only if a much larger graph (a
> full 13-volume run across all characters) makes convergence speed an actual problem.

**Original line 54:**

> ## Things you need to know

**Original line 56:**

> **A claim's evidence can span multiple volumes; `first_vol` alone is not a safe filter for
> printing quotes.** `extract/claims.py` merges repeated observations of the same fact (same
> subject/predicate/object_norm/first_vol) into one `claim_id`, appending new evidence as later
> volumes confirm it again. A claim with `first_vol = 1` can genuinely carry a `v02` quote. This is
> correct and fine for the STRUCTURED value (the fact really was known since v01) — but the first
> version of `wiki explain` in this session printed every quote attached to a claim regardless of
> `--upto`, which leaked v02 dialogue into a `--upto 1` run. Found by running it against real data
> and grepping the output for `v02`, not by inspection. Fixed by
> `graph/temporal.py::evidence_at(claim_ids, vol)`, which checks each quote's own `para_id` volume.
> **Phase 6's `synth/prose.py` must call `evidence_at`, not read `claims.evidence_json` directly**,
> or it reproduces the exact same leak when building its prompt — this is the single most important
> thing to carry into Phase 6.

**Original line 69:**

> **Page-model field keys are `predicate.lower()`, not a hard-coded name table.** CONTRACTS §5's
> original example showed `"titles"`/`"nicknames"` as if TITLE/NICKNAME were special-cased; they
> render generically like every other attribute (`fields["title"]`, `fields["nickname"]`).
> `config/extraction.yaml`'s own header says "Adding a predicate or attribute here is all that is
> needed — rendering is generic," which is the literal justification. The ONE exception is relations:
> `AFFILIATED_WITH` (identified by predicate name, not a config flag) renders into
> `fields["affiliations"]`; every other relation predicate renders into one `fields["relationships"]`
> list (each entry carries its own `predicate`, so nothing is lost by not having one list per
> predicate). If a future series' config adds a new attribute, it needs zero code changes to appear
> on a page; if it adds a new *relation* predicate that deserves its own field the way
> `AFFILIATED_WITH` does, that DOES need a code change here — there was no time pressure to
> generalize that one exception, and CONTRACTS/CLAUDE.md both call out exactly two relation-driven
> field names, so it stayed as the two-bucket split rather than inventing a config flag nothing asks
> for yet.

**Original line 84:**

> **A currently-open interval's real `vol_end`/`superseded_by` must never reach the page JSON when
> it's still in the future relative to the cutoff.** `assemble.py` exposes this as a boolean instead:
> a scalar attribute field gets `changes_later: true/false`; an affiliation gets `current: true/false`
> plus a `vols` pair whose second element is `null` until the close is actually revealed. This was
> Phase 4's handover's explicit instruction (`state_at`'s own docstring: "That scrub is
> synth/assemble.py's job") and is covered by
> `test_synth_assemble.py::test_scalar_field_scrubs_future_vol_end_and_reports_changes_later`, which
> asserts the real number (`"5"`) does not appear anywhere in the field's repr at all, not just that
> `changes_later` is set correctly.

**Original line 94:**

> **`nx.pagerank()` needs scipy, which is not installed and not a declared dependency.** Discovered
> by running `wiki explain` for real, not by reading networkx's docs — the installed networkx (>=3.2)
> only ships the scipy-backed implementation of `pagerank()`. Rather than adding a new dependency for
> a graph of a few hundred nodes at most, `graph/ppr.py::_personalized_pagerank_scores` is a
> hand-rolled pure-Python power iteration (standard formulation: restart to the seed on every jump,
> alpha=0.85, L1-convergence at 1e-10 or 100 iterations). If a much larger run ever makes this slow,
> either add scipy properly (pyproject.toml + `wiki doctor`) or vectorize with numpy (already an
> indirect dependency, per the traceback that surfaced this) — do not silently start calling
> `nx.pagerank()` again, it will break the same way.

**Original line 104:**

> **`assemble_page()` does not write anything to disk.** It is a pure function returning a dict.
> `data/05_pages/` still does not exist — `wiki explain` uses the dict in memory for display only.
> Phase 6's `wiki synthesize` is what calls `assemble_page()`, adds prose, checks `claim_set_hash`
> against whatever the previous cutoff wrote, and actually writes `data/05_pages/<id>/v<NN>.json`/
> `.md`.

**Original line 110:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 112:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | Field keys are `predicate.lower()`, generic over `config/extraction.yaml` | That file's own header says rendering is generic; a hard-coded name table breaks the moment a new series' config adds an attribute (series-agnostic requirement) | A fixed name table matching CONTRACTS' old example (`titles`, `nicknames`, ...) — matches the illustrative doc exactly but silently drops any attribute not in the table |
> | `AFFILIATED_WITH` is the one relation predicate identified by name, not by a config flag | CONTRACTS/CLAUDE.md both name exactly two relation-driven fields (`affiliations`, `relationships`); no config flag exists to generalize this, and inventing one nothing asks for is exactly the premature-abstraction Phase 3/4's handovers already cautioned against | A generic `relations.<PRED>.field: affiliations` config flag — real complexity for a two-item split |
> | `mentions_of` is populated directly from `graph/ppr.py`'s ranked output | PPR existed only as an unused file-map bullet; `mentions_of` was an unfilled CONTRACTS field; pairing them is the only concrete use either one has at this phase | Leaving `mentions_of` empty until Phase 7's wikifier can scan generated prose — defers a decision Phase 5 can make cleanly now, and Phase 7 can still layer wikified-prose mentions on top later without conflict (this list is additive, not exclusive) |
> | PageRank hand-rolled as pure-Python power iteration | `nx.pagerank()` requires scipy, not installed/declared; graphs here are a few hundred nodes at most — a new heavy dependency is not worth it for this scale | Adding scipy to pyproject.toml + wiki doctor — legitimate if this ever becomes a bottleneck, not needed now |
> | `evidence_at` filters each quote by its own para_id volume, added as a fifth sanctioned `graph/temporal.py` read | Found a real leak this way; centralizing it (rather than fixing it inline in `cli.py::explain`) means Phase 6's prose stage gets the fix for free instead of reintroducing the same bug independently | Fixing the filter only inside `cli.py::explain`'s closure — would have "worked" for this phase and quietly broken again in Phase 6 |

**Original line 120:**

> ## Known gaps, deliberately left

**Original line 122:**

> - Relation intervals still never close (Phase 4's known gap, unchanged) — `relations_at`'s scrub
>   logic for a closed-but-not-yet-revealed relation is written and tested
>   (`test_synth_assemble.py`), but nothing in real data exercises it yet.
> - `assemble_page()`'s `fields` ordering follows `settings.attributes` iteration order (a Python
>   dict, so config file order) for attributes, and interval `vol_start` order within a list field —
>   not alphabetical. Not a contract violation (CONTRACTS §5 doesn't mandate an order), just worth
>   knowing if a future diff looks like fields "moved" for no code reason after an extraction.yaml
>   edit.
> - `wiki explain`'s "~N evidence tokens" estimate is `len(quote_chars) / 4`, a rough heuristic, not
>   a real tokenizer call — good enough for "does this look too big before Phase 6 spends real
>   tokens," not for budget accounting (that's `llm/budget.py`'s job once Phase 6 actually calls a
>   model).
> - No `wiki audit pages` yet — `paths.STAGE_DIRS["pages"]` and `wiki status`'s "pages" row already
>   exist from earlier phases, but there is still nothing to audit until Phase 6 writes files there.
> - **`quiet_change` (extraction.yaml `conflicts:` block) is still read by nothing.** Phase 4's
>   handover flagged this as "Phase 5's rendering layer" work. It is deliberately still not read
>   here: CONTRACTS §5 defines no "this field just changed" marker for `assemble_page()` to set —
>   the closest thing, `changes_later`, means "will change in the future relative to this cutoff,"
>   the opposite direction from `quiet_change` ("a change that already happened, don't badge it").
>   Whatever actually renders a "changed!" badge is a Phase 7 SPA concern, and it can read
>   `quiet_change` directly against a field's predicate name (trivially: field key `"rank"` ->
>   `"RANK"` -> `settings.conflicts_config["quiet_change"]`) without needing it echoed into the page
>   JSON at all — so this is deferred to Phase 7, not forgotten. Reconsider only if Phase 6/7 turns
>   out to need it earlier than expected.

> ## 2026-09-01 — Short, non-contradictory prose

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** `background` and `personality` are 2–4 sentences each, generated only from the
> volume-filtered claim set, with evidence references retained.

**Original line 14:**

> **Why:** The user asked for short descriptions for anything not expressible in a word or a sentence.
> Long generated prose is also where hallucination and spoiler leakage hide.

**Original line 17:**

> **Implies:** Structured fields are rendered from graph rows with no LLM involvement at all. Prose

> to audit.

**Original line 21:**

> **Status:** Planned — Phase 6.

**Original line 23:**

> ---

**Original line 26:**

> ## 2026-09-02 — Prose is generated from TRAIT claims only, never from structured fields

**Original line 28:**

> **What:** `synth/prose.py` (Phase 6) builds `background` from BACKGROUND trait claims and
> `personality` from PERSONALITY/MOTIVATION/SKILL/FEAR trait claims — never from the scalar
> attribute/relation fields `synth/assemble.py` renders (age, status, rank, affiliations,
> relationships, ...). A field is `null`, with no LLM call made, when the character has zero trait
> claims of that kind visible at the cutoff. `evidence` on the returned page is not something the
> model reports back; it is the exact `para_id` set the prompt was built from.

**Original line 35:**

> **Why:** `docs/PROMPTS.md`'s existing split — `personality_prose` "from trait claims only" — was
> already the design; this makes `background_prose` match it exactly rather than inventing a wider
> "biography context" pull from structured fields, which CONTRACTS/PROMPTS never specified and would
> have needed new evidence-fetching plumbing duplicating `synth/assemble.py`'s. It also keeps
> CLAUDE.md §2 ("structured fields are never LLM-generated") unambiguous: the model never sees a
> field it might restate as if it were the generated prose. Skipping the LLM call entirely when there
> is no trait evidence avoids the exact hallucination risk CLAUDE.md §1 exists to prevent, and costs
> zero tokens for the (common, at early cutoffs) case of a minor character with no traits yet.

**Original line 44:**

> **Implies:** A character can legitimately reach `--upto N` with populated structured fields
> (status, affiliations, relationships from attribute/relation claims) and still have `prose: {
> "background": null, "personality": null }` if no trait claims exist yet — this is correct, not a
> bug, and `wiki audit pages` reports it as "zero structured fields" only when `fields` itself is
> empty, a different condition.

**Original line 50:**

> **Status:** Done (Phase 6) — see the Phase 6 LOG.md entry and `docs/handover/PHASE_6.md`.

**Original line 52:**

> ---

**Original line 55:**

> ## 2026-09-02 — `wiki synthesize` caching compares cutoff N to cutoff N-1, not to its own last write

**Original line 57:**

> **What:** `synth/cache.py::previous_page(entity_id, upto_vol)` walks downward from `upto_vol - 1`
> to the nearest cutoff with a file already on disk, and `unchanged(prev, claim_set_hash)` decides
> whether the current cutoff needs writing. This correctly collapses a long run of adjacent,
> factually-identical cutoffs (CONTRACTS §5.1's "13x multiplier"), including across a resumed
> `--upto` invocation with gaps already on disk. It does **not** make a full command re-run a no-op
> at the file-write layer: cutoff N is always compared to cutoff N-1's content, not to cutoff N's own
> previous run, so re-running `wiki synthesize --upto 2` twice in a row rewrites both files both
> times.

**Original line 66:**

> **Why:** This is the literal reading of CONTRACTS §5.1 ("If it is unchanged from cutoff N-1...").
> A same-cutoff idempotency check (comparing this run's output to the last time *this exact cutoff*
> was written) is a different, stronger guarantee nothing in CONTRACTS asks for, and would need a
> second comparison path alongside the one §5.1 actually specifies — not worth the complexity when
> the expensive resource (LLM spend) is already protected: `llm/cache.py` caches on the exact
> request, so a byte-identical prompt on a rewritten cutoff costs nothing.

**Original line 73:**

> **Status:** Done (Phase 6) — verified by re-running `wiki synthesize --upto 2 --entities shin
> --polish` twice against real data; the second run rewrote both files but made no new network call
> (same `generated_by`/prose text both times).

**Original line 77:**

> ---

**Original line 80:**

> ## 2026-09-02 — `config/models.yaml`: `prose`/`codex_summary` had no reachable fallback

**Original line 82:**

> **What:** `prose` and `codex_summary` routed to `mistral_prose` with no `fallback` entry at all,
> unlike every other API-routed stage (`prose_polish`, `arbitrate`). `Settings.resolve_role` only
> substitutes the fallback role when the primary profile's API key is *absent* from the environment
> — not when the key is present but rejected by the provider (expired, revoked, out of quota). Both
> now declare `fallback: google_fast`.

**Original line 88:**

> **Why:** Found during Phase 6 real-data testing: `MISTRAL_API_KEY` in this environment expired on
> 2026-09-02 (the provider returned a 401 saying so), which `resolve_role` cannot detect ahead of a
> real call, so `prose` dead-ended with no fallback path even though a working Google key was
> present. This does not fully fix the underlying limitation (`resolve_role` still cannot react to a
> mid-call auth failure and switch profiles automatically), but at least gives these two stages the
> same static-fallback safety net every other API-routed stage already has.

**Original line 95:**

> **Implies:** If `MISTRAL_API_KEY` is renewed, `prose`/`codex_summary` still try it first — this is
> a fallback, not a repoint. `google_fast` (`gemini-flash-lite-latest`) is a free-tier profile with a
> low daily request quota (20/day was hit during Phase 6 testing); a real multi-character run relying
> on this fallback should expect to be rate-limited and may need `GOOGLE_API_KEY` upgraded off the
> free tier, or `MISTRAL_API_KEY` renewed, before running at scale.

**Original line 79:**

> ## Things you need to know

**Original line 81:**

> **`synth/prose.py` reads TRAIT claims only — never a structured `fields` value.** This was a
> deliberate narrowing of "background... from the volume-filtered claim set" (docs/PROMPTS.md's
> original planning-stage wording): BACKGROUND trait claims already ARE members of that set, and
> pulling in status/rank/affiliation history as extra "biography context" would need new
> evidence-fetching plumbing nothing in CONTRACTS specifies, while blurring CLAUDE.md §2's
> "structured fields are never LLM-generated" (the model would see content it could restate as if it
> were the generated prose). If a future request wants background prose to also draw on structured
> fields, that is a real CONTRACTS §5 change, not a bug fix — flag it explicitly rather than quietly
> widening the prompt's input.

**Original line 91:**

> **A `null` prose field with no LLM call is intentional, not a gap.** `_generate_one` in
> `synth/prose.py` returns `None` immediately, before touching the client, when there are no fact
> lines to hand it. This is why v01's page above has both fields `null`: Shin has no BACKGROUND
> trait claim by volume 1 in the real corpus. Do not "fix" this by asking the model to write
> something from nothing — that is the exact hallucination risk CLAUDE.md §1 exists to prevent.

**Original line 97:**

> **`evidence` in the prose dict is not a citation the model produces — it is what we fed it.**
> `_gather_facts` collects every `para_id` from `evidence_at(claim_ids, upto_vol)` calls made while
> building the prompt, and that list (deduped, sorted) becomes `evidence` regardless of what the
> model's response text actually says. This makes the field impossible for the model to falsify by
> paraphrasing a quote instead of citing it, at the cost of it being "everything shown", not
> "everything used" — a model that ignores one of five facts still gets all five listed as evidence.
> This was a deliberate simplicity-over-precision call; revisit only if `wiki audit pages` ever needs
> finer-grained citation accuracy than it currently checks (it currently only checks sentence-count
> bounds, not grounding).

**Original line 107:**

> **`synth/cache.py`'s skip is about ADJACENT cutoffs within one logical build, not about rerun
> idempotency.** `previous_page(id, N)` finds the nearest EXISTING file below N and compares hashes.
> On a totally fresh multi-volume run (`--upto 13` from nothing) this is exactly CONTRACTS §5.1's
> "13x collapse": a character whose facts do not change between v5 and v6 gets no v06 file at all,
> and Phase 7's bundle step is expected to resolve cutoff 6 to the v05 file it finds on disk. But
> re-running `wiki synthesize --upto 2` a SECOND time over the SAME already-populated data rewrites
> both v01 and v02 again, every time — because v02's hash is being compared to v01's hash (which is
> almost always different; that is real narrative content, not staleness), never to v02's own
> previously-written copy. This is deliberate (see VISION.md 2026-09-02 entry) and safe: the
> expensive resource, LLM spend, is still protected by `llm/cache.py`'s exact-request cache, which
> returns free and instant on a byte-identical prompt. If a future need genuinely requires
> same-cutoff rerun idempotency at the file layer too, that's a second comparison
> (`prev_at_this_exact_vol.claim_set_hash == claim_set_hash`) layered on top of what exists — not
> a replacement for the N-vs-N-1 check CONTRACTS §5.1 actually specifies.

**Original line 122:**

> **`wiki audit pages`'s cache-reuse number is reconstructed, not recorded.** There is no manifest
> file listing which cutoffs were attempted vs skipped — the report infers skips from GAPS in each
> entity's on-disk `v{NN}.json` sequence (e.g. v01 and v03 exist, v02 doesn't -> assume v02 was
> skipped). This is a heuristic that assumes every cutoff in an entity's written range was actually
> attempted in some run; it will misreport if pages were manually deleted or `--entities` filtered
> runs left irregular gaps for reasons other than caching. Good enough for an audit sanity check,
> not a source of truth — if this ever matters more precisely, the real fix is a manifest written by
> `synth/cache.py` itself, not smarter gap inference.

**Original line 131:**

> **`config/models.yaml`: `prose`/`codex_summary` had no reachable fallback, discovered by a real
> 401.** `Settings.resolve_role` only substitutes `fallback` when the primary profile's API key is
> *absent* from the environment (`profile.api_key` is falsy) — it has no way to react to a key that
> is *present but rejected* by the provider (expired, revoked, quota-exhausted) without actually
> attempting the call. `MISTRAL_API_KEY` in this environment expired on 2026-09-02 itself (the
> provider's own error said so), and `prose`/`codex_summary` were the only two API-routed stages
> with no `fallback:` entry at all — every other stage (`entity_classify`, `entity_alias`,
> `claim_extract`, `arbitrate`, `prose_polish`) already had one. Both now fall back to `google_fast`.
> This does not fix `resolve_role`'s inability to detect a bad-but-present key ahead of time — that
> would need either a health-check call before every stage (real cost) or a runtime provider-swap on
> auth failure inside `llm/client.py::_call` (a real architecture change, out of scope for a
> one-stage prose bug) — it just gives these two stages the same static safety net the others have.

**Original line 144:**

> **`GOOGLE_API_KEY`'s free tier has a 20-request/day quota per model, hit mid-session.** Real

> Gaps. A future session picking this phase back up (or starting Phase 7's real-data checks) should

**Original line 150:**

> **`--polish` routing is importance-percentile, computed over the FULL character roster, not the

> `--entities` filter applied to the actual run — so `wiki synthesize --entities lena --polish`
> still asks "is Lena above the 85th importance percentile of the WHOLE cast", not "of just Lena",
> which is the only sensible reading (a filter for testing convenience should not change who counts
> as "major"). Verified in the real run: Shin (importance 1.0, clearly major) got `prose_polish` and
> `generated_by: "google:gemini-flash-latest"`.

**Original line 159:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 161:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | Prose input is TRAIT claims only, never structured `fields` | Matches docs/PROMPTS.md's existing `personality_prose` design exactly; avoids new evidence plumbing and keeps CLAUDE.md §2's "never LLM-generated" boundary unambiguous | Also feeding scalar attribute history ("biography context") for `background` — broader reading of "volume-filtered claim set" nothing in CONTRACTS actually requires |
> | `evidence` = para_ids fed to the prompt, not model-cited | Deterministic, cannot be falsified by paraphrase; simpler than parsing/validating a model citation list | Asking the model to return which facts it used — adds a schema field and a validation failure mode for marginal precision gain |
> | No LLM call when zero trait evidence exists | Zero-evidence generation is exactly CLAUDE.md §1's hallucination risk; also free | Always calling the model with an empty fact list and hoping `forbid_uncited_specifics` holds — real risk, no upside |
> | Cache compares cutoff N to cutoff N-1's file, not to N's own last run | The literal CONTRACTS §5.1 mechanism; the expensive resource (LLM spend) is already protected by llm/cache.py regardless | A second same-cutoff idempotency layer — real complexity for a guarantee nothing currently asks for |
> | `categories` = affiliation entity_ids; `Appearances` = every vol named in `fields` | Both undefined by CONTRACTS §5.2; this derives them from the page dict alone with no new evidence read, keeping site/okf.py a pure function like synth/assemble.py | Reading mention_counts from graph.db for `Appearances` — a new read path this module didn't otherwise need |
> | `prose`/`codex_summary` get `fallback: google_fast` | Every other API-routed stage already has a fallback; found the gap via a real 401, not inspection | Rewriting `Settings.resolve_role` to retry-and-swap on a runtime auth failure — real architecture change, out of scope here |
> | `wiki audit pages` reuse count is inferred from on-disk gaps | No manifest exists and adding one only to serve an audit report is premature | A dedicated cache-skip manifest written by synth/cache.py — legitimate if precision ever actually matters |

**Original line 171:**

**Original line 173:**

> - Non-major (`prose`, not `prose_polish`) generation was not real-run-verified this session —

>   tests (stage-forwarding is asserted directly), just not against a live API.
> - Cache-skip (`synth/cache.py::unchanged` returning `True` in a real run) was not observed on real

>   an exact count.
> - No `wiki budget` persistence — `client.budget` accumulates in memory during `synthesize` but

> ## 2026-09-02 — Site bundle: sparse multi-cutoff shape, extended `links.json`, and a minimal static viewer instead of `web/`

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** Three decisions, landed together as Phase 7 (`site/wikify.py`, `site/bundle.py`,
> `site/static_site.py`). (1) `data/06_bundle/pages/{id}.json` and `data/06_bundle/codex/*.json`
> are both SPARSE multi-cutoff maps — `{"cutoffs": {"<vol>": {...}}}` — carrying only the cutoffs at
> which something actually changed; a client resolves a selected volume to the nearest cutoff key
> `<=` it, the same walk `synth/cache.py::previous_page` already does on disk. (2) `links.json`'s
> value per `entity_id` is `{"route", "canonical", "type"}`, not a bare route string, so a client
> can render an affiliation/relationship/PPR-neighbour/codex-member reference's display name without
> a second lookup file. (3) `web/` (the planned Vite + React + TS SPA) has no scaffold yet, and
> building one is a substantially larger effort than the rest of this phase — asked the user
> directly rather than guessing; they chose a dependency-free HTML/CSS/JS viewer
> (`site/templates/`) written straight into `dist/site/` by `site/static_site.py`, with no Node/npm
> build step, over scaffolding the real SPA this session.

**Original line 24:**

> **Why:** (1) mirrors CONTRACTS §5.1's "generated once per cutoff at which the claim set changes"
> cache rule at the bundle-file layer, not just at the LLM-call layer — without it, either every
> cutoff 1..N would need its own bundle entry (defeating the whole point of the collapse) or the
> bundle would silently go stale between characters' actual cutoffs. (2) a compact combined map
> costs little and saves the reference viewer (and any future SPA) a second network round trip per
> rendered link. (3) `site/bundle.py`'s data contract is independent of what renders it — the bundle
> is portable to a real SPA later with zero changes to the Python side, so shipping a working
> `wiki site build`/`wiki serve` today was judged more valuable than a half-built React app this
> session would not have had time to finish or test properly.

**Original line 34:**

> in the bundle resolves against `links.json`. Building the real `web/` SPA later needs no change to
> `site/bundle.py` — only to what writes `dist/site/`; see `docs/handover/PHASE_7.md`.
