**Original line 113:**

> ## Things you need to know

**Original line 115:**

> **The sparse multi-cutoff shape is the single most important idea in this phase — get it wrong
> and every downstream reader is subtly broken, not obviously broken.** `data/05_pages/<id>/
> v{NN}.json` files already only exist at cutoffs where something changed (Phase 6's "13x
> collapse"). `build_pages_bundle` does NOT try to fill the gaps — it copies exactly the keys that
> exist on disk (`{"cutoffs": {"1": {...}, "3": {...}}}`, no `"2"` key). `build_codex_bundles` does
> the analogous thing but has to COMPUTE its own sparseness, since there is no per-cutoff codex file
> on disk to mirror — that is what `_state_hash` is for. **Every reader of a multi-cutoff bundle
> file — the reference viewer's `nearestCutoff()` in `app.js`, `wiki audit links`, any future
> consumer — MUST resolve a selected volume to `max(key for key in cutoffs if key <= selected)`,
> never assume the key for the selected volume exists.** Getting this wrong doesn't crash anything;
> it just silently shows `undefined`/nothing for a legitimate cutoff, which is a much worse bug to
> chase later than a crash would be.

**Original line 128:**

> **`_state_hash` covers evidence AND `members`/`related`, not evidence alone — this is a real
> divergence from `synth/cache.py`'s single-hash `unchanged()`, made deliberately, not by
> oversight.** A codex entry's summary sentence can stay byte-identical across two cutoffs while its
> member list changes (a character newly affiliates). If the cache key were evidence-only, that
> cutoff would be skipped — no new `cutoffs["<N>"]` key — and a client resolving "nearest cutoff <=
> N" would keep showing the STALE member list at N, forever, until the summary text itself happened
> to change for unrelated reasons. `test_codex_bundle_skips_unchanged_cutoff_but_writes_on_
> membership_change` in `tests/test_site_bundle.py` is the worked example — read it before touching
> `_state_hash` or `_members_and_related`.

**Original line 138:**

> **`codex_summary`'s prompt needed a literal JSON example, not just a field description — and this
> is a real, general lesson, not a one-off.** `_system_prompt` originally read like `synth/prose.py`'s
> own system prompts (a paragraph of instructions, no literal JSON shown). Against
> `gemini-flash-lite-latest` (`google_fast`, reached via `codex_summary`'s `fallback:` when
> `MISTRAL_API_KEY` is absent — it had also independently expired again this session; see `wiki
> doctor`'s "key present" check only verifies the key is non-empty, not that the provider still
> accepts it, same known gap Phase 6 documented), a prompt whose FIRST LINE was `"Location: Sixth
> Sector"` reliably primed the model to invent its own JSON shape — `{"location": "...",
> "definition": "..."}` — instead of the `{"text": "..."}` the `CodexSummary` schema actually
> requires, and `llm/client.py::complete_json`'s 3-attempt repair-retry loop never recovered it
> (reproduced 4/4 times across two entities and two cutoffs before the fix, 0/4 times after adding
> one line: `` Respond with JSON only: {"text": "..."} ``, matching the pattern
> `entities/classify.py` already used). Google's `json_mode` (`response_mime_type: application/
> json`) only enforces *valid JSON*, never a specific *shape* — there is no `response_schema`
> constraint wired up in `llm/providers/google.py`. `docs/PROMPTS.md` rule #3 now states this as a
> hard rule for every future `complete_json` prompt. `synth/prose.py`'s prompts have the same latent
> gap (no literal example) and were NOT observed to fail in Phase 6's real testing, but that may
> just mean nobody has hit the right/wrong priming context yet — worth a real repro before "fixing"
> something not shown to be broken.

**Original line 158:**

> **`members`/`related` on a codex entry come from the graph, not from evidence text.** `members` is
> every CHARACTER entity with a visible relation TO this codex entity (`graph/temporal.py::
> relations_at` — extraction only ever produces a relation with a character as `subject`, since
> `extract/claims.py` is a per-character driver, so the "other side" of any relation touching a
> codex entity is always a character; `_members_and_related` filters by type anyway rather than
> assuming, matching this codebase's usual "guard, don't trust the shape" style). `related` is this
> entity's own `graph/ppr.py::personalized_pagerank` neighbours, restricted to OTHER non-character
> entities, capped at 5 — the multi-hop "what else is this connected to" CONTRACTS §6.1's original
> (illustrative, not literal) example showed. Both are graph-cutoff-filtered the same way every
> other reader of `graph.db` is (`relations_at`/`all_edges_at` both filter `vol_start <= vol` before
> anything else) — no new spoiler-filtering discipline was invented here, just applied to entity
> types that had not needed it before.

**Original line 171:**

> **`links.json`'s value is `{"route", "canonical", "type"}`, not a bare string — CONTRACTS §6 only
> ever said "entity_id → route."** This is a deliberate extension (documented in CONTRACTS §6.3),
> not an accidental schema drift: without `canonical`, the reference viewer (or any future SPA)
> would need a second lookup — realistically `index.json`'s character roster plus three separate
> codex files merged client-side — just to print a relationship target's name. `route` alone is
> still a strict subset of the object, so nothing that only ever read `.route` breaks.

**Original line 178:**

> pages/index/links/search are always built for the full roster regardless of the flag — they are

**Original line 85:**

> ## Things you need to know

*Non-numerical blocks omitted here; consult the linked source for uninterrupted prose.*

**Original line 92:**

> **An override does not fall back on a missing key — this is deliberate, and matches an existing
> pattern rather than inventing a new one.** The *ordinary* (non-override) path already returns a
> keyless profile as-is when no `fallback` is declared for that stage; it does not raise early. An
> override just extends that same behaviour by skipping the fallback substitution too. The actual
> failure, if the key really is missing, happens naturally at call time as a `ProviderError` ->
> `LLMError`, with the same "run `wiki doctor`" hint every other LLM failure gets. Do not add an
> early `ConfigError` for a missing key on an override — it would special-case overrides for no
> functional benefit over what already happens at call time.

**Original line 101:**

> **The Groq model trap.** `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` — the obvious model id to reach for — 404s on
> a real key today; Groq's available model list rotates. Worse, several of what IS available
> (`openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `-120b`, `-safeguard-20b`) are reasoning models: they spend `max_tokens` on
> a hidden `reasoning` field before ever writing to `content`, and `llm/providers/openai.py` only
> ever reads `content` (`data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or ""`). This project's per-stage
> token budgets are all tight (512-1536), so a reasoning model under this adapter silently returns
> an empty string instead of erroring — the same failure *shape* as the `codex_summary`/Gemini
> JSON-shape bug from Phase 7 (VISION.md 2026-09-02), just a different mechanism (hidden reasoning
> tokens vs. an unconstrained JSON shape). `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` was verified live (plain text and
> `response_format: json_object`) to write directly to `content` with no reasoning field, so that is
> what `groq_fast`/`groq_prose` use. If another Groq-hosted reasoning model is ever added as a
> profile, either raise `max_tokens` enough to cover its reasoning budget, or forward a
> `reasoning_effort: "none"`/`"low"` request option once `llm/providers/openai.py` supports passing
> it through — it does not today; only `temperature`/`max_tokens`/`response_format` are forwarded.

**Original line 139:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 141:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | Role-name overrides as the primary form; ad-hoc `provider:model` as a secondary, warned form | A role carries pricing/api_key_env/base_url/option-shape with it; a bare model id carries none of that (confirmed via `llm/cache.py`/`llm/providers/*.py` exploration) | Accepting only raw model ids — simpler flag, but every override would need its options/pricing guessed, and budget tracking would misreport cost |
> | A per-command `--model` option, no `@app.callback`, threaded explicitly through `run-all` | `cli.py` has no callback today, and `run-all` already calls the other commands as plain Python functions (not subprocess dispatch) — matching that existing pattern needed no new plumbing | A `typer.Context.obj`-based global option — would need a callback added to `app` for the first time, more invasive for the same result |
> | Override bypasses key-absent fallback | The caller named a specific model; silently substituting a different one on a missing key is a worse surprise than a clear, familiar `LLMError` at call time | Falling back the same way the ordinary routing table does — would make `--model prose=anthropic_best` with no Anthropic key silently run Mistral instead, defeating the point of asking for it explicitly |
> | Ad-hoc profile clone order: stage's own current profile -> first same-provider profile -> `default_role` | Prefers the option/pricing shape most likely to match the model actually being tried, cheapest lookup first | Always cloning the first same-provider profile regardless of stage — simpler, but wrong when the stage's own current role already uses the right provider with different (often cheaper) options |
> | `groq_fast`/`groq_prose` point at `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, verified live | The obvious id (`llama-3.3-70b-versatile`) 404s on this key; reasoning models on this same provider have a silent-empty-output trap under this project's tight token budgets | Picking a model id from Groq's docs without a live round-trip call — exactly what caused the `codex_summary` Gemini bug this project already hit once |
> | Reinstall the editable package rather than editing/removing the stale worktree | The install pointing at the wrong path was the actual bug; the worktree's unmerged content is not this phase's to judge or discard | Leaving the broken install in place and just noting it — would leave every future `wiki` invocation in this environment silently wrong |

> had no reachable fallback" entry's own caveat is still true and now bit `claim_extract` too:
> `Settings.resolve_role` only substitutes a stage's `fallback` when the primary key is *absent* from
> the environment, never when it's present-but-rejected by the provider — so an expired key dead-ends
> every routed-to-it stage exactly the way a missing key would NOT. `claim_extract` has no fallback
> declared at all (unlike its siblings), so it had no path forward except an explicit `--model`

**Original line 82:**

> **Two free-tier rate limits, both hit for real and both structural, not transient:**
> - **Groq (`groq_fast`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`) has an 8,000 TPM cap on this key's tier.** 20 consecutive
>   attempts (65s apart, well past any single retry's backoff) all failed at the same point with the
>   same `429 rate_limit_exceeded` — this is not "wait a bit and it clears," the per-character
>   extraction prompt is simply too large relative to the cap for more than a couple of characters to
>   fit in one rolling minute. Abandoned Groq for this stage; switched to `--model
>   claim_extract=google_fast` instead, which completed (partially rate-limited, see below, but not
>   structurally blocked).
> - **Google AI Studio's free tier (`google_fast`/`google_best`, both models) caps at 15
>   requests/minute.** Every stage that fans out one call per character/entity in a tight loop with no
>   inter-call pacing (`claim_extract`, `prose`, `codex_summary`) hit this at least once across the
>   run (`extract`: 12/14 characters then `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`; `site build`'s codex-summary step:
>   the same, twice). Recovery pattern that worked every time: just retry the same command after the
>   API's own `retryDelay` (~50-60s) — `llm/client.py`'s disk cache means a retry only re-attempts the
>   items that didn't finish, so each retry is strictly incremental, never a restart from zero.
>   `llm/client.py`'s own retry/backoff (`max_retries=3`, `2/4/8s` exponential = 14s total) is too
>   short for either failure mode — both need a caller-level retry loop, not a client-level one.

**Original line 107:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 109:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | Default series (`86`) keeps the original, unsegmented `data/`/`dist/` layout | The real, already-built 86 corpus must never be silently moved or orphaned by adding series support | Segmenting every series including the default under `data/<id>/` — simpler code, but would silently relocate the existing corpus's output on next run |
> | `data/cache/llm/` never segmented | Cache keys are content-addressed (provider+model+prompt+options) — a cached answer for a given prompt is valid no matter which series asked it, so segmenting would just duplicate cost for no correctness benefit | Segmenting the cache per series "for consistency" — would double-pay for any prompt structurally shared across series (none currently, but no reason to foreclose it) |
> | `set_active_series` mutates module globals, called once at startup | Every module in this codebase already imports `PARSED_DIR`/`PAGES_DIR`/etc. as bare attributes; re-threading a `series_id` parameter through every function that touches a path would touch far more files for the same result | A `series_id` argument threaded through every path-consuming function — more "correct" in isolation, but a much larger, riskier diff for Phase 9's actual goal |
> | `require_para_raid` opt-in per series, not inferred | The pipeline cannot distinguish "this series has no radio-comms channel" from "the CSS-class pattern regressed and is silently missing everything" by inspection alone — the review's own listed root cause. An explicit, human-set flag is the only reliable signal | Inferring "expected" from whether the pattern matches anything on a first pass — indistinguishable from the exact silent-failure mode this check exists to catch |
> | Spice and Wolf source EPUBs read from `"All novels/<title>/"` rather than moved into `raw/` | `raw/` was implicitly 86-only in every existing series config's mental model; moving files was judged out of scope for a config-only phase | Moving/copying the EPUBs into `raw/spice-and-wolf/` to match 86's layout — arguably cleaner, but a filesystem change beyond what this phase needed, and not yet decided as the long-term multi-series convention |
> | Continuing the calibration run on `google_fast` rather than stopping for `MISTRAL_API_KEY` to be renewed | The key's expiry is an external account/billing action outside this session's control; `--model ...=google_fast` is an existing, already-verified (Phase 4) escape hatch, cheap, and reversible (a CLI flag, not a config rewrite) | Blocking and waiting for the user to renew the key — would have stalled a already-scoped, low-cost, resumable run for no correctness benefit |
> | `synth/prose.py`'s prompt fixed with a literal JSON example, matching `codex_summary`'s already-applied fix | Same root cause (Gemini `json_mode` enforces valid JSON, never a specific shape, without one), same fix, already precedented — CLAUDE.md/docs/PROMPTS.md rule #3 says every `complete_json` prompt needs this | Leaving it as a documented-but-unfixed "worth watching" gap now that a real repro exists — the fix is a two-line, zero-risk change |
> | `claim_extract` given a `fallback: google_fast` even though it won't auto-recover today's specific failure (key present-but-expired, not absent) | Matches the precedent already set for `prose`/`codex_summary` (2026-09-02 entry); helps once the key is fully unset rather than merely expired, and documents the real constraint (15 req/min) for the next person who reads `models.yaml` | Leaving `claim_extract` without a fallback since it wouldn't have prevented today's failure anyway — true, but inconsistent with its siblings and loses the chance to record the rate-limit finding where a future reader will actually see it |

> step` loop, **12** HTML audit reports + `wiki trace`, **13** planned page outline (closed section
> vocabulary, replacing the two hand-synced hardcoded templates in `okf.py`/`app.js`), **14**

**Original line 32:**

> **Why:** The review memo's three symptoms (thin pages, false claims, broken links) map cleanly onto
> STORM's own expert-editor findings once you read the two together — this project already exhibits
> "source bias transfer" (uncounted evaluative language) and "over-association" (relation pairs
> asserted without a stated predicate, worse than plain hallucination per STORM's editors) as
> concretely observable defects, not hypothetical risks. Separately, none of the user's four new
> operating rules have any supporting infrastructure today: no run/snapshot concept exists in
> `paths.py`; `llm/cache.py` stores the response only (`{text, in_tokens, out_tokens}`), never the
> prompt, system prompt, or a timestamp, so a cached answer cannot be traced back to what was asked;
> `Budget.save()` has no production caller so `wiki budget` always reports nothing recorded; chapter
> identity exists inside every paragraph record (`ingest/segment.py:25`'s `para_id`) but no CLI flag
> or path function can address one; and `wiki audit links` prints FAIL but exits 0, so a broken build
> ships silently.

> **A real bug found and fixed during implementation, not just planned:** the first version of
> `snapshot_before` hardlinked instead of copying (cheaper on the same volume). Every stage in this
> codebase writes its output via `path.open("w")`, which truncates the existing file **in place**
> rather than writing a new file and renaming over it — so a hardlinked "snapshot" shares the live
> file's inode, and the stage's own next write silently corrupts the snapshot too. Caught by
> `tests/test_provenance.py::test_snapshot_before_and_restore_round_trip` before this ever ran
> against real data; `_copy_tree` now always does a real copy, documented at the point of the fix so
> the next person does not reintroduce it for the same "hardlinks are cheaper" reason.

> shared across series on purpose — it backs the content-addressed LLM cache, not cost accounting).

**Original line 113:**

> ## A real bug found and fixed during this phase

**Original line 115:**

> The first version of `provenance._copy_tree` tried `os.link` (hardlink) before falling back to
> `shutil.copy2`. **This silently corrupted every snapshot.** Every stage in this codebase writes
> its output via `path.open("w")` / `path.write_text(...)`, which truncates the *existing* file in
> place rather than writing a new file and renaming over it. A hardlinked "snapshot" shares the live
> file's inode — so the very next time the stage wrote to that path, the snapshot was overwritten
> too, with nothing left to roll back to.

**Original line 122:**

> Caught by `tests/test_provenance.py::test_snapshot_before_and_restore_round_trip` before this ever
> ran against real data. Fixed: `_copy_tree` always does a real copy now, with the reasoning
> documented at the point of the fix (`provenance.py`) so it doesn't get "optimized" back to a
> hardlink later for the plausible-sounding reason that started this bug.

**Original line 168:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 170:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | Log every call (hit AND miss) to `calls.jsonl` | A cache hit is the proof a question was already answered — exactly what "search before re-asking" (rule 2) needs to be checkable | Logging only real (uncached) calls — cheaper, but would make `wiki calls` blind to the very repeats it exists to catch |
> | Frontier interlock checked only on a cache miss | A hit costs no money and reveals no new spend; blocking it would make a previously-legitimate, already-cached answer unreadable later for no safety benefit | Checking on every call regardless of cache state — simpler code, but punishes cheap/free repeats for no reason |
> | `RunContext.finish()` is idempotent (first call wins) | Every existing command body has multiple `raise typer.Exit` points; calling `finish()` at each one (rather than reindenting the whole body under one `try/finally`) needed idempotency to be safe from double-counting the budget | A single try/finally wrapping each entire command body — more "correct"-looking, but a much larger, riskier reindentation of five already-working command functions for the same result |
> | Snapshot at the whole-stage-directory granularity (`paths.STAGE_DIRS` keys), not per-file | Every command already writes to exactly one (or two, for site build) stage directories; matching that grain needed no new bookkeeping of "which files did this write" | Tracking exact written files — more precise, but needs instrumenting every writer in `ingest/`, `extract/`, `graph/`, `synth/`, `site/`, none of which currently reports what it wrote |
> | Cumulative `wiki budget` total moved to `data/<series>/budget.json`, series-scoped | `llm/budget.py`'s own default (`data/cache/llm/budget.json`) is deliberately shared across every series (it backs the content-addressed LLM cache) — reusing it for cost totals would silently mix two series' spend into one number | Leaving the default as `llm/budget.py`'s own path — simpler, but wrong the moment a second series is in active use, which is already true (Spice and Wolf) |
> | `doctor` never starts a run | It only calls `client.health()`/`health_profile()`, which hit providers' health/list endpoints directly, never `LLMClient._call` — there is nothing to log | Wrapping doctor in a run "for consistency" — would create an empty run directory on every single `wiki doctor` invocation, which is run constantly, for no benefit |

**Original line 9:**

> ## 2026-09-04 — Phase 11 built: chapter granularity, `wiki step`, and demoting `run-all`

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** The rest of the user's rule 3 (see the 2026-09-03 "Six-phase redesign" entry) — strictly
> iterative, one-chapter-at-a-time processing with a mandatory pause for manual audit. `--chapters`
> (`'1-4'`, `'2,5'`, `'3'`, parsed by a new `config.py::parse_chapter_range` sharing its body with
> `parse_volume_range`) on `ingest` and `extract`, requiring `--volumes` to name exactly one volume.
> Both commands now **merge, not overwrite**, when writing chapter-scoped output — a new
> `cli.py::_merge_by_chapter` keeps every existing paragraph record / claim whose `chapter_idx` is
> outside the requested set and replaces only the rest, so a volume's `v{NN}.jsonl` accumulates one
> chapter at a time across repeated calls instead of being clobbered. Skip-if-exists became
> per-chapter on both commands. New `wiki step` command: resolves the next unprocessed
> `(volume, chapter)` from a new small state file (`data/<series>/_runs/step_progress.json`, via new
> `provenance.load_step_progress`/`save_step_progress`), runs
> `ingest -> extract --chapters -> graph build -> synthesize -> site build` for that one chapter,
> prints the affected character page(s)' real, working local URL
> (`http://127.0.0.1:8080/#/character/<id>`, confirmed against `site/templates/app.js`'s hash
> router), runs the existing terminal `claims`/`contradictions` audit reports, and only then saves
> progress. `wiki step` (bare) does the very first chapter; advancing past an already-completed
> increment always requires `--continue` or `--redo` explicitly — a bare repeat is refused
> (`StepBlocked`) rather than silently no-oping, which is what makes "pause for manual audit" real
> instead of a comment. `run-all` is demoted: it now refuses a `--volumes` scope resolving to more
> than one volume unless `--i-accept-unaudited` is passed, pointing at `wiki step` as the default.

**Original line 32:**

> **Why:** Confirmed by direct code reading (not assumed from the handover doc) that every on-disk
> artifact was volume-granular with no chapter concept anywhere, `graph build`/`synthesize`/
> `site build` had no `--volumes` at all, and `run_all` called the other five stage commands
> in-process with nothing stopping an unattended 13-volume run. `graph build`'s claim-file glob
> (`sorted(paths.CLAIMS_DIR.glob("v*.jsonl"))`) already only reads whatever volume files exist, so
> Phase 11's "scope graph build's inputs to whatever claims files exist" needed no code change there
> — confirmed, not re-implemented.

**Original line 40:**

> **Implies:** `graph build`, `synthesize`, `site build` deliberately get NO chapter selector —
> spoiler safety (`CLAUDE.md` §1) is defined at `first_vol`, i.e. volume granularity, by invariant;
> synthesizing/building the site "at `--upto <volume>`" while only some of that volume's chapters
> are extracted is still spoiler-safe (nothing from unextracted chapters or later volumes can leak,
> it's just incomplete until the rest is stepped through). A chapter that legitimately produces zero
> claims (a short interlude, no character evidence) is indistinguishable on disk from one never
> attempted, so it is silently re-attempted by a later `--chapters`/`wiki step` call touching it —
> deliberate, and free, since `llm/cache.py` makes the repeat cost no tokens. `claim_id` has no
> chapter component (`make_claim_id(subject, predicate, object, vol)`), so the same claim asserted
> in two different chapters of one volume processed by two different `wiki step` calls is not
> merged the way a single whole-volume `extract` call already merges it via `_merge_claim` — a known,
> accepted gap, not fixed in this phase (see `docs/handover/PHASE_11.md`).

**Original line 98:**

> ### Resolution algorithm (`_resolve_step_target`)

**Original line 100:**

> 1. No volumes discovered at all -> `None` (nothing to do).
> 2. No progress yet -> `(lowest volume, 0)`. Chapter 0 always exists once a volume's spine has been
>    walked at all, by construction (`ingest/epub.py` assigns `chapter_idx=len(chapters)` at append
>    time, so indices are always contiguous from 0 with no gaps) -- no need to have ingested the
>    volume yet to know this.
> 3. `--redo` -> repeat exactly `progress`, regardless of `--continue`. Works even if the target
>    volume's parsed file is missing (it isn't, in practice -- see point 2's guarantee once a step
>    has actually completed).
> 4. Progress exists, neither flag given -> raise `StepBlocked`. This is what makes "pause for
>    manual audit" real: advancing always requires a deliberate flag, every time.
> 5. `--continue` -> read `_chapter_count(progress["vol"])` (requires that volume's
>    `data/01_parsed/v{NN}.jsonl` to exist -- guaranteed, since a completed step for that volume
>    means `step()` already called `ingest()` for it). If `progress["chapter_idx"] + 1` is still
>    within range, advance within the volume; otherwise advance to chapter 0 of the next volume in
>    `settings.discover_volumes()` order, or `None` if there is no next volume.

> and `step_progress.json` was confirmed unchanged (`{"vol": 1, "chapter_idx": 1}`, exactly as
> before the failed call) — not corrupted, not advanced. This is exactly the behavior the design
> relies on (§4's point 10 in the original plan), demonstrated with a real failure rather than a
> simulated one. No code change resulted; recorded here because it's the kind of thing that's easy
> to get wrong silently.

**Original line 159:**

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 161:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | `--chapters` requires `--volumes` to resolve to exactly one volume | Chapters are numbered per-volume; applying one chapter spec across several differently-sized volumes has no sensible meaning | Applying the same chapter range to every selected volume — silently wrong the moment volumes have different chapter counts |
> | Merge-not-overwrite (`_merge_by_chapter`) instead of a hard `--force`-required error when a chapter's already done | This is what makes incremental accumulation across repeated `wiki step`/`extract --chapters` calls actually work — the file grows one chapter at a time instead of needing `--force` (which would also blow away every OTHER already-extracted chapter under the old whole-file overwrite) | A hard error requiring `--force` whenever any requested chapter already exists — safer-looking, but `--force` under the OLD (pre-Phase-11) semantics meant "redo the whole volume," which would silently discard every other already-extracted chapter |
> | A chapter with zero claims is always re-attempted on a later call (no "attempted but empty" marker) | Idempotent and free (`llm/cache.py` makes the repeat cost nothing); building a separate "attempted" tracker is real complexity for a purely cosmetic inefficiency | A `chapters_attempted` field alongside claims — correct, but the codebase's existing whole-volume flow never needed this concept either, and it would need its own merge/rollback semantics |
> | Step-progress lives in its own small file (`step_progress.json`), not inside the run manifest schema | The manifest's `volumes`/`volume_scope` fields are already meaningfully volume-grained (used by the frontier interlock, `wiki runs`); overloading them with a chapter dimension for one command's internal bookkeeping would complicate every OTHER reader of a manifest for no shared benefit | Adding a `chapter_scope` field to every manifest — touches Phase 10's schema and every existing manifest consumer for a concern only `wiki step` has |
> | `step_progress.json` is NOT touched by `snapshot_before`/`restore` | Rolling back one run's output and then continuing the step loop from the same position is the correct combination — `wiki rollback` undoes what a run WROTE, not where the step loop IS | Snapshotting it alongside stage dirs — would silently rewind or fast-forward the step loop as a side effect of an unrelated rollback, surprising and undocumented |
> | `wiki step` delegates to the five existing stage commands in-process (same pattern `run_all` already used) rather than building its own extract/synthesize/site-build logic | Reuses every existing skip-if-exists, provenance, and error-handling behavior for free; `run_all`'s own propagation of `typer.Exit` on failure already does exactly what "a failed step must not advance progress" needs | A parallel, step-specific implementation of the four stages — real duplication for no behavioral difference |
> | `graph build`/`synthesize`/`site build` get no chapter selector | Spoiler safety (`CLAUDE.md` §1) is defined at `first_vol`, i.e. volume granularity, by invariant — there is no "chapter cutoff" concept to add without touching that invariant | Adding a parallel chapter-level cutoff to synth/site — a materially larger, riskier change touching the one invariant this project cannot regress, for a benefit `wiki step`'s existing `--upto <volume>` calls already get safely (see below) |
> | No dedicated automated test for "`graph build` reads only the claim files present" | The behavior needed zero code change (confirmed by reading `cli.py::graph_build`'s existing glob before touching anything) and was exercised for real by every `wiki step`/`run-all` verification run above, which always ran with only 2 of 13 volumes' claims on disk | A heavy CliRunner-style integration test standing up a full Settings/gazetteer/LLMClient fixture just to re-confirm an unchanged `Path.glob` call |

**Original line 172:**

> ## Known gaps, deliberately left for later phases

**Original line 174:**

> - **No cross-chapter `claim_id` merge.** `make_claim_id(subject, predicate, object, vol)` has no
>   chapter component. A whole-volume `extract` call already merges duplicate claim_ids across
>   chapters within that one call (`extract/claims.py::_merge_claim`, combining evidence). Two
>   SEPARATE `wiki step`/`extract --chapters` calls (different chapters, same volume) that both
>   produce the same claim_id will NOT be merged — both land in the file. Rare in practice (the same
>   exact subject/predicate/object asserted independently in two different chapters of one volume),
>   and downstream `graph/contradictions.py` already reconciles same-subject/predicate/object claims
>   ACROSS volumes; extending that reconciliation to same-volume-different-chapter duplicates was
>   judged out of scope here — not fixed, not silently swept under "merge-not-overwrite."
> - **No chapter-level HTML audit report.** `wiki step` runs the existing terminal `claims`/
>   `contradictions` reports (Phase 4's `audit/reports.py`, unchanged). Self-contained HTML reports
>   a non-coder can open from disk, plus `wiki trace`, are Phase 12.
> - **`run-all` still has no `--chapters`.** It was never meant to — it's the "unattended, one
>   volume at a time" path now; `wiki step` is the chapter-granular one.
> - **No `wiki step --status`/`wiki step --reset`.** Inspecting or clearing
>   `step_progress.json` today means reading/deleting the file directly (documented in
>   `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §7.5). Not asked for; add if it comes up.
> - Phase 9's still-open finding (Holo's Appearance field near-duplicates) and Phase 10's
>   Vertex-frontier-profile-still-commented-out gap are both untouched — unrelated to this phase.

> ## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

**Original line 138:**

> | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
> |---|---|---|
> | `wiki audit run <run_id>` reuses the existing flat `wiki audit <stage>` command (stage="run" plus a second positional `run_id`) rather than a new Typer sub-app | `CLAUDE.md` §6 documents `audit <stage>` as a stable CLI shape; Typer requires every sub-app command to be explicitly named (no positional dispatch with 2+ commands), so a sub-app would have forced `wiki audit report <stage>` or similar, breaking every existing doc/muscle-memory reference to `wiki audit <stage>` | A `graph_app`/`site_app`-style Typer sub-app for `audit` |
> | `_audit_report` builds ONE `Console(record=True)` and passes it to `reports.run` instead of calling the report function once for the terminal and once (recording) for HTML | `rich.Console(record=True)` prints live to `sys.stdout` AND records for later export from the SAME call — confirmed empirically before writing any code. Calling twice would double every side effect a report has (`_gazetteer_report` re-writing `roster.html`, wasted LLM-free but real disk I/O) for identical output | Two separate console objects / two calls to `reports.run` |
> | `wiki audit <stage>` always targets `provenance.latest_run_id()`, no `--run` option | Keeps the common case (`wiki audit claims` right after `wiki extract`) a single unadorned command; the run that JUST finished is almost always the one you want the HTML attached to. A user who wants a specific older run's HTML can re-run the stage command to make it latest again, or read `wiki runs` and know which run's `audit/` dir corresponds to which invocation | A `--run <id>` option on `wiki audit <stage>` — real but not asked for, and the common path already works without it |
> | Every report's FAIL now exits `wiki audit <stage>` non-zero, not just `links` | The handover only named `links` explicitly, but all six reports already had the identical FAIL/OK branch shape, and `_audit_report`'s check is one `if ok is False` regardless of which stage — leaving the other five at "prints FAIL, exits 0" would have been an inconsistent, arbitrary carve-out for no stated reason | Scoping the fix to `links` only, per the letter of the original ask |
> | `wiki step`'s own run passes NO `stage_keys` to `provenance.start_run`, so `snapshotted_stages` stays absent and `wiki rollback <step run id>` has nothing to restore | `step()` itself never writes to a stage directory directly — every delegated command (`ingest`/`extract`/`graph_build`/`synthesize`/`site_build`) already snapshots its OWN stage dir before writing. A step-level snapshot would be a redundant second copy of the exact same pre-run state, and `wiki rollback` on the step run would restore nothing new since the delegated runs' own snapshots are the real rollback points | Also snapshotting at the step level "for completeness" — real disk cost, zero behavioral benefit |
> | `wiki trace` reads RAW claims directly from `data/03_claims/v*.jsonl` (every claim regardless of `first_vol` cutoff), not through `graph/temporal.py`'s `state_at`/`history_at` | `wiki explain <name> --upto N` already exists and does exactly the assembled, cutoff-filtered view — duplicating that here would make `trace` redundant with it. `trace`'s stated job (`docs/handover/PHASE_11.md`'s Phase 12 item 4, "does not exist yet... traceable end to end by a non-coder") is provenance: the full raw history AND the run/call chain that produced each piece, which is specifically the thing `explain` cannot show (it never touches `_runs/`) | Reimplementing `explain`'s cutoff-filtered view a second time under a new command name |
> | `provenance.search_calls_all_runs` is a thin loop over `list_runs()` + the existing `read_calls(..., grep=...)`, not a new index/cache | `calls.jsonl` files are small (this project's testing cap is 1-2 volumes; `CLAUDE.md` §0) and `wiki trace` is an occasional inspection command, not a hot path — a per-run linear scan costs nothing worth optimizing for | A merged/indexed cross-run call log maintained incrementally |

> ## Known gaps, deliberately left for later phases

**Original line 150:**

> - **`wiki audit <stage>`'s HTML always targets the LATEST run for the series, even if that run's
>   command has nothing to do with the stage being audited** (e.g. running `wiki audit links` right
>   after an unrelated `wiki gazetteer` call attaches `links.html` to the gazetteer run). Harmless
>   (the HTML is still correct; it's just filed under a run whose command name doesn't match the
>   stage), and the common case (`wiki audit <stage>` right after the command that produces that
>   stage's input) always gets the intuitively-right run. Not fixed — would need a `--run` option
>   (rejected above) or per-stage "most relevant run" heuristics that are more complexity than the
>   problem has warranted so far.
> - **No HTML export for `wiki explain`/`wiki trace` themselves** — both remain terminal-only, like
>   `wiki calls`. Only `audit/reports.py`'s six registered reports get the HTML treatment, since
>   those are the ones the original ask (`docs/handover/PHASE_11.md`) named.
> - **`wiki trace`'s cross-run call search is a substring match on the canonical name only** — it
>   does not also search for the entity's aliases or `entity_id`. A call that referred to a
>   character only by an alias/nickname (not yet resolved to canonical at prompt-construction time)
>   would be missed. Not observed in practice against Spice-and-Wolf (prompts consistently use the
>   canonical name), and adding multi-term OR search is a small, well-scoped follow-up if it comes
>   up on `86`'s larger cast.
> - Phase 9's still-open finding (Holo's Appearance field near-duplicates), Phase 10's
>   Vertex-frontier-profile-still-commented-out gap, and Phase 11's cross-chapter `claim_id` merge
>   gap are all untouched — unrelated to this phase.

> ## 2026-09-04 — Config-driven page outline (closed section vocabulary)

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** The six-phase redesign plan (`docs/vision/PHASE_10.md`, 2026-09-03) named Phase 13
> next: replace the two hand-synced hardcoded section templates — `site/okf.py`'s `render_markdown`
> (fixed Python calls: Overview, Affiliations, Relationships, Background, Personality, Appearances,
> in that literal order) and `site/templates/app.js`'s `renderCharacter` (the same sections as
> separately hand-written HTML string literals) — with one declared, closed vocabulary both read.
> A new `page_outline` block in `config/extraction.yaml`, dict-of-dicts shaped like `attributes`/
> `relations`/`traits` (so the existing per-series `_deep_merge` overlay already handles it), names
> every CHARACTER page section: `order`, `kind` (`fields` | `affiliations` | `relationships` |
> `prose` | `derived`), `title`, and — for `kind: prose` — `traits`/`min_sentences`/`max_sentences`/
> `subject`/`source`. `Settings.page_outline` (new property) exposes it sorted by `order`.

**Original line 22:**

> **Why:** Today a person adding or reordering a page section has to edit both files by hand with
> nothing enforcing that they still match — and in fact they already didn't: `app.js`'s body order
> (Background, Personality, Relationships) had drifted from `okf.py`'s (Relationships, Background,
> Personality) with no test catching it. This also directly unblocks the depth programme recorded
> in `docs/vision/PHASE_17.md`: Phase 20 (outline-driven multi-section pages) and the per-series
> schema overlay's "no series concept in `src/`" rule both assume the section list already lives in
> config, not in either renderer.

**Original line 30:**

> **Implies:** `synth/prose.py` is folded into this phase even though the six-phase paragraph names
> only `assemble.py`/`okf.py`/`app.js` — `assemble.py`'s prose-dict keys and `prose.py`'s generation
> loop are the same contract, and generalizing one without the other would leave any future
> config-declared section permanently `null`. `synth/assemble.py`'s `"prose": {"background": None,
> "personality": None}` literal becomes one `None` per configured `kind: prose` section key.
> `site/bundle.py`'s `index.json` gains a `sections` key (mirroring the existing `field_labels`) so
> `app.js` never hard-codes a section title either. `cli.py`'s `step()`/`synthesize()` prose-written
> check and `audit/reports.py`'s `_pages_report`/`_links_report` hardcoded `("background",
> "personality")` tuples are generalized to the same config-driven list, so a future series-specific
> prose section is audited and link-checked automatically. Scope explicitly excludes Phase 20's
> per-section graph retrieval and evidence-scaled length budgets — this phase keeps today's
> trait-predicate-grouping retrieval and fixed sentence bounds, only declaring the section *list*
> itself in config.

> ## Why this phase exists

**Original line 12:**

> The six-phase redesign plan (`docs/vision/PHASE_10.md`, 2026-09-03) named Phase 13 next: replace
> the two hand-synced hardcoded section templates — `site/okf.py`'s `render_markdown` (fixed Python
> calls: Overview, Affiliations, Relationships, Background, Personality, Appearances) and
> `site/templates/app.js`'s `renderCharacter` (the same sections as separately hand-written HTML
> string literals) — with one declared, closed vocabulary both read. This was worth doing now, not
> later, because it turned out the two files had **already** drifted apart: `app.js`'s body order
> was Background → Personality → Relationships while `okf.py`'s was Relationships → Background →
> Personality, and nothing caught it. It also directly unblocks the depth programme
> (`docs/vision/PHASE_17.md`): Phase 20 (outline-driven multi-section pages) and the per-series
> schema overlay rule ("no series concept in `src/`") both assume the section list already lives in
> config.

> ## What exists now

**Original line 26:**

> ```
> config/extraction.yaml
>   New `page_outline` block, dict-of-dicts keyed by section (same shape as `attributes`/
>   `relations`/`traits`, so the existing per-series `_deep_merge` overlay handles it for free --
>   add, override, or `null`-delete one section without repeating the rest). Base taxonomy declares
>   six: overview (kind: fields), affiliations (kind: affiliations), relationships (kind:
>   relationships), background (kind: prose, traits: [BACKGROUND]), personality (kind: prose,
>   traits: [PERSONALITY, MOTIVATION, SKILL, FEAR]), appearances (kind: derived). Each entry has
>   `order` (explicit sequencing -- not dict-insertion-order, so a series overlay adding one section
>   doesn't depend on where the base dict happens to place it) and `title`. `prose:` block trimmed
>   to just `codex_summary`/`forbid_uncited_specifics` -- `background`/`personality`'s sentence
>   bounds moved into their `page_outline` entries.
>
> src/narrativewiki/config.py
>   Settings.page_outline (new property)  -> list[dict], each entry with its own `key`, sorted by
>     `order`. Pattern: `prose_config` (same file). No CLI override exists for this yet, unlike
>     `--attr`/`--trait`/`--relation` (Phase 17's schema-tuning work) -- out of scope, not asked for.
>
> src/narrativewiki/synth/assemble.py
>   assemble_page()'s `"prose": {"background": None, "personality": None}` literal is now
>   `{s["key"]: None for s in settings.page_outline if s["kind"] == "prose"}`. Nothing else changed
>   -- fields/affiliations/relationships were already generic.
>
> src/narrativewiki/synth/prose.py
>   generate_prose() loops `settings.page_outline` filtered to `kind == "prose"` instead of two
>   hardcoded calls; `_PERSONALITY_PREDICATES` constant deleted (the predicate list now lives only
>   in config, as each section's own `traits` key). `_system_prompt`/`_generate_one` take the
>   section dict instead of a `kind: str`, reading `subject`/`source`/`min_sentences`/
>   `max_sentences` from it -- falls back to `f"a short {title.lower()} summary"` / `"facts"` if a
>   future section omits `subject`/`source`, so a minimal overlay entry still works without a
>   prompt-writing exercise.
>
> src/narrativewiki/site/okf.py
>   render_markdown()'s five hardcoded `parts.append(...)` calls became one loop over
>   `settings.page_outline`, dispatching on `kind` via new `_section_body()` to the same
>   `_overview_lines`/`_affiliation_lines`/`_relationship_lines`/prose-lookup/`_appearances` helpers
>   (all kept, just called generically). Each section renders as `## {title}` + its content, in
>   declared order.
>
> src/narrativewiki/site/bundle.py
>   build_pages_bundle()'s `for kind in ("background", "personality")` wikify loop now iterates
>   `settings.page_outline` filtered to `kind == "prose"`. build_index()'s `field_labels` dict
>   gained a sibling `"sections"` key: `[{"key", "kind", "title"} for s in settings.page_outline]`
>   -- CONTRACTS §6 documents it. This is what lets `app.js` stay generic without a build-time
>   template step.
>
> src/narrativewiki/site/templates/app.js
>   renderCharacter() iterates `state.index.sections` (falls back to a hardcoded `DEFAULT_SECTIONS`
>   matching the base six, for a bundle built by an older `wiki site build` with no `sections` key
>   yet -- the same forward-compat concern `field_labels` already has). `kind: fields` and
>   `kind: affiliations` render into the existing infobox aside (fields bare, affiliations under an
>   `infobox-section` title div -- preserved exactly from the old hardcoded version, including
>   fields having NO visible "Overview" label, which was already true before this phase);
>   `relationships`, `prose`, and `derived` render into the body, each under an `<h2>{title}</h2>`,
>   in declared order. New `appearancesOf(page)` helper mirrors `okf.py::_appearances`'s
>   since_vol/vols/history walk client-side. This is what fixed the body-order drift noted above,
>   and it also adds an Appearances section to the HTML view for the first time -- previously only
>   `okf.py`'s Markdown rendered it. Verified live with a real headless-Edge screenshot (see below),
>   not just by reading the diff.
>
> src/narrativewiki/cli.py
>   synthesize()'s `if prose["background"] or prose["personality"]:` (the "did this cutoff actually
>   generate anything" check, used by both `wiki synthesize` and the `wiki step` it's delegated
>   from) is now `if any(prose.values()):`.
>
> src/narrativewiki/audit/reports.py

> tests/test_synth_assemble.py, tests/test_synth_prose.py, tests/test_site_okf.py,

> | Infobox-vs-body placement (`fields`/`affiliations` -> aside; everything else -> body) stays a fixed rule in `app.js`, not a new config field | The six-phase ask was a closed **section** vocabulary, not a full layout DSL; the aside/body split is a page-chrome decision, not part of "what sections exist and what feeds them" | A `placement: infobox\|body` key on every `page_outline` entry |
> | No `--attr`-style CLI override for `page_outline` | Not asked for by the six-phase entry; the per-series overlay (already built, Phase 17) covers the actual use case ("Overlord needs an Abilities section") without extra CLI surface | `--section`/`--only-section` flags mirroring `--attr`/`--only` |

**Original line 9:**

> ## 2026-09-04 — Fandom-grade depth: the ceiling is the ontology, not the model (Phases 17-21)

**Original line 11:**

> **What:** Raise generated pages from their current ~8-sentences-plus-a-bullet-list shape to the
> depth of a mature Fandom wiki (the *Overlord* wiki was named as the target). Five phases, in
> dependency order: **17** value canonicalization + relation arbitration, **18** chapter-major
> extraction as a second pass + epithet aliases, **19** an event/narrative layer in the graph,
> **20** outline-driven multi-section page planning, **21** cross-entity pages + an evaluation
> harness. This supersedes nothing; it is the depth axis the six-phase redesign (2026-09-03) did not
> cover, and Phases 14/15 of that plan are absorbed into 17 and 21 respectively.

**Original line 19:**

> **Why — measured, not assumed.** Four numbers taken from the real Spice and Wolf v01-v02 output
> and from running `extract/windows.py` against the live mention index:

**Original line 22:**

> 1. **Extraction yield:** two entire novels produce 255 claims / 573 evidence quotes across 26
>    predicate types. Holo, a co-lead, has 91 claims total. A Fandom character page carries on the
>    order of 500-2000 discrete assertions for *one* character.
> 2. **Coverage:** for Holo in v01, 517 paragraphs contain a mention and cluster into 135 windows;
>    `max_windows_per_entity_per_volume: 40` sends 40 of them. The extractor reads **33.6%** of the
>    volume's 2,587 paragraphs about its own main character (62.8% if uncapped). Lawrence: 56.6%
>    sent, 87.5% available. Discarded windows are chosen by mention count, so the quiet
>    character-development scenes are exactly the ones dropped. This is on top of the pronoun- and
>    epithet-only scenes Aho-Corasick cannot see at all.
> 3. **Predicate mass:** 60 of 255 claims are APPEARANCE and 26 are FRIEND_OF. The schema's weight
>    sits on timeless entity properties.
> 4. **Schema shape:** `config/extraction.yaml` is 9 attributes + 5 traits + 22 relations. Every one
>    is a property of an *entity*. None is a property of *something that happened*.

**Original line 36:**

> A mature Fandom page spends most of its bytes on event-level narrative — Chronology (per-volume
> plot from that character's vantage), Abilities with mechanics, a multi-paragraph Relationships
> essay per person, Quotes, Trivia, per-chapter Appearances. **The data model has no slot for any of
> it.** `EVENT` exists as a gazetteer *entity type* (a battle with a proper name — 86's whole
> gazetteer found 2 of them among 163 entities), not as a narrative unit with participants, causality
> and time. There are no scene records, no beat summaries, no per-chapter plot, no quote records, no
> state-change events.

**Original line 44:**

> This is why a stronger model does not fix it, and this is the decision being recorded: **model
> capability is ranked fourth of five causes, and finetuning is rejected outright.** Point a frontier
> model at this pipeline and it fills the same 26 slots with better sentences. The unit of extraction
> (a +/-2-paragraph mention window) is also *smaller than the unit of the fact* — a plot arc, a
> motive, a consequence spans a chapter, so no window-scoped call emits one at any model size. Second
> confirmation from this project's own output: Holo's ~40 near-duplicate APPEARANCE fragments and her
> simultaneous `Enek — Friend of` / `Enek — Enemy of` rows are missing *stages*, not missing
> intelligence.

**Original line 53:**

> **Finetuning is rejected**, for the record, so it is not re-proposed: (a) it needs thousands of
> (passage -> claim) pairs from this corpus that do not exist and would cost more to build than the
> project; (b) the failure modes are structural — no slot, no coverage, no dedup — and weights fix
> none of them; (c) a finetuned 14B's literary-synthesis ceiling still sits below a frontier model's
> zero-shot; (d) decisively, it fights CLAUDE.md §1 — finetuning moves knowledge *into weights*,
> where it carries no `first_vol` and cannot be spoiler-scoped. The one defensible future use is
> distilling frontier claim-extraction into a local model to cut bulk cost: a cost optimization,
> never a quality one.

**Original line 62:**

> **Implies:**

**Original line 64:**

> - **Phase 17 — canonicalization first, because depth multiplies duplicates.** Embed all values for
>   one `(subject, predicate)` with `bge-m3` locally (`llm/providers/ollama.py` still needs the
>   `/api/embed` path noted on 2026-09-03), cluster, elect one canonical surface form, keep the rest
>   as `variants` carrying their own evidence rather than as sibling bullets. Route contradicting
>   relations on the same pair through `arbitrate` as either a temporal transition or an extraction
>   error. Zero API cost. Do this before anything else so later changes can be judged.
> - **Phase 18 — chapter-major extraction as a SECOND pass, not a replacement.** Read every chapter
>   end to end in overlapping ~4k-token spans, emitting scene records: participants, location, beat
>   summary, state changes, attributed quotes. Coverage becomes 100% by construction and the pronoun
>   problem largely dissolves without a coreference model, because a whole-chapter span carries its
>   own antecedents. The existing mention-major pass stays for precise slot-filling. The 40-window
>   cap is then replaced by a per-chapter budget, which is naturally bounded. Also: mine epithet
>   aliases ("the wisewolf", "the merchant") into the gazetteer so the automaton sees them. Bulk
>   cost is ~1.6M input tokens for 13 volumes — free on Ollama, a few GPU-hours.
> - **Phase 19 — the event layer.** A narrative node anchored to `(vol, chapter_idx, para span)` with
>   participants and roles; new claim kinds `event`, `state_change` (X->Y *at event E*), `quote`
>   (speaker, addressee, para_id), `mechanic`. Intervals anchor to `event_id`, not only
>   `vol_start`/`vol_end`. Note that claims **already carry `chapter_idx`** (see any row of
>   `data/*/03_claims/v01.jsonl`) and `graph/temporal.py` discards it at the interval layer — the key
>   chronology needs is being thrown away today.
> - **Phase 20 — outline-driven pages, retiring the six hardcoded sections in `site/okf.py`.** Each
>   section is a separate generation with its own graph retrieval query, its own evidence set, and
>   its own length budget scaled to evidence volume, replacing the global 2-4 sentence cap in
>   `extraction.yaml`'s `prose:` block. **CLAUDE.md §1 survives unchanged and is not weakened:** every
>   section is still generated from an already-cutoff-filtered set; the invariant simply applies per
>   section instead of per page. This is what turns 8 sentences into a full page without raising
>   hallucination risk.
> - **Phase 21 — cross-entity pages + evaluation.** Relationship pages (pair-scoped subgraph + shared
>   scenes), faction pages, per-volume timeline pages; `graph/ppr.py` currently feeds only
>   `mentions_of` and gets repointed at per-section retrieval. Evaluation is not optional — depth and
>   hallucination are indistinguishable from the inside: hand-transcribe the fact list and outline
>   from three real Fandom pages, then measure heading recall, fact recall, and citation entailment.
> - **Routing:** chapter-major pass local; section synthesis frontier-tier, cached on a *section*-
>   evidence hash (a far better hit rate than the current page-level `claim_set_hash`, where one new
>   fact invalidates a whole page). Phase 10's frontier interlock bounds dev spend.

**Original line 100:**

> **A limit to state plainly, so it is not rediscovered as a failure:** the Overlord wiki cannot be
> equalled from EPUBs alone. A large share of it is out-of-band — author interviews, anime-adaptation
> differences, release dates, image galleries, community trivia. The reachable target is *parity with
> its novel-derived content*, which is still a 10-20x depth increase over today's output.

> ## 2026-09-04 — Per-series extraction schemas and CLI schema tuning; depth must never become series-specific

**Original line 112:**

> **What:** The depth programme above must not buy richness by hard-coding one series' concepts.
> Two mechanisms, and one standing rule.

**Original line 115:**

> 1. **Per-series schema overlay.** `config/extraction.yaml` stays the universal base (the concepts
>    every narrative has: age, gender, status, kinship, affiliation). A new optional
>    `config/extraction.<series>.yaml` is deep-merged over it, holding only what that series needs —
>    `KARMA: { single: true, format: short_text, display: "Karma" }` for Overlord, a magic-system
>    attribute for another series, `RACE`/`LEVEL`/`JOB_CLASS` and so on.
>    `paths.extraction_config()` takes a series id; `load_settings(series_id)` merges base + overlay.
> 2. **CLI schema tuning**, so a run can be narrowed or widened without editing config at all — the
>    same ergonomics as the existing `--model` override (Phase 8): repeatable
>    `--attr KARMA=short_text:"Karma"` / `--trait` / `--relation` to add a predicate ad hoc, and
>    `--only`/`--skip` (repeatable, accepting predicate names or the kinds `attribute`/`relation`/
>    `trait`) to restrict what a given run extracts. Combined with the existing `--volumes` and the
>    Phase 11 `--chapters` selector, this is what makes "volume 9 introduces a stat block, extract it
>    only there" a command line rather than a code change.
> 3. **The standing rule:** no Phase 17-21 deliverable may name a series concept in `src/`. Every new
>    section, predicate, or page kind is declared in config and rendered generically, exactly as
>    attributes already are.

**Original line 132:**

> **Why:** The requirement is that the wiki adapt to whatever a series actually tracks — Overlord
> characters need a Karma level rendered next to Gender and Affiliations — while the code stays
> series-agnostic (2026-09-01 "Series-agnostic by construction"). Verified before writing this that
> the attribute axis is **already** generic end to end, so this is a scoping problem, not a rewrite:
> `extract/claims.py::_vocab_lines(settings.attributes)` builds the extraction prompt from config;
> `_predicate_spec` validates against config; `synth/assemble.py::_build_attribute_fields` keys
> fields by `predicate.lower()` for every configured attribute (the 2026-09-02 generic-fields entry);
> `site/okf.py::_overview_lines` iterates `attributes_cfg`; and `site/bundle.py` ships a

> `KARMA` to `extraction.yaml` today would already reach the rendered page with no code change.

**Original line 143:**

> ## 2026-09-04 — Relation staleness when a mid-volume transition is never re-extracted

**Original line 177:**

> **What:** User-raised scenario, recorded as a second confirming data point for Phase 19's design
> rather than a new deliverable. Phase 17's relation-conflict arbitration only closes a
> `FRIEND_OF`/`ENEMY_OF` interval when BOTH predicates are independently extracted as claims
> somewhere in the claim set (same-volume arbitration, or cross-volume supersession once the second
> claim appears). If a friend turns enemy mid-volume and the passage that shows it is never sampled
> into an extraction window at all — the mention-window cap already measured to discard exactly the
> "quiet" low-mention-count scenes, per the coverage numbers in the entry above — no conflicting
> `ENEMY_OF` claim ever enters the graph. Nothing to arbitrate against means the `FRIEND_OF` interval
> stays open forever, and every later cutoff (volume N+1, N+2, ... even if the enmity is never
> restated on-page again) renders the stale, backdated relation.

**Original line 188:**

> **Why:** This is a coverage/recall gap, not an arbitration gap. Phase 17 already handles "both
> sides got extracted, which one wins." This is "only one side was ever extracted" — structurally
> the same "missing stages, not missing intelligence" diagnosis made above for the near-duplicate
> APPEARANCE/simultaneous-FRIEND_OF-ENEMY_OF findings, just for the opposite failure direction (an
> edge that should have closed and didn't, instead of two edges open at once).

**Original line 194:**

> **Implies:** No new phase opened — this reinforces the two mitigations already planned, so it's
> recorded here rather than as a new item:
> - **Phase 18** (chapter-major extraction) directly raises the odds the transition passage is
>   sampled at all: 100% coverage by construction vs. today's measured ~34% (Holo, v01) mention-window
>   coverage under the 40-window cap.
> - **Phase 19** (event layer) is the structural fix, already named as the target home for "a general
>   relation-edge-closing redesign" in `docs/handover/PHASE_17.md`'s Known Gaps. A `state_change`
>   claim (`FRIEND_OF -> ENEMY_OF` *at event E*) is a single explicit assertion of the transition
>   itself — it closes the old interval unconditionally at extraction time and does not depend on a
>   second, independently-extracted conflicting relation claim ever showing up later.
> - **Residual ceiling Phase 19 cannot remove:** a transition that is genuinely never stated in the
>   text (it happens off-page, between volumes) cannot be recovered by any extraction design. This is
>   a corpus-coverage limit, not a pipeline bug — Phase 21's evaluation harness should name it as such
>   rather than treat every stale relation it finds as a defect to chase.

**Original line 209:**

> **Status:** Noted. No code changes from this entry — folded into Phase 18/19 scope, which already
> plan to address it.

**Original line 217:**

> **What:** Both deliverables from the "Fandom-grade depth" entry above, implemented, scoped

> `graph/store.py`'s schema, `synth/`, or `site/`, since canonicalization reduces the *input* to the
> existing `assign_multi_valued` merge rather than adding a new output shape.

**Original line 222:**

> 1. **Embedding infra**, the prerequisite the `embed` profile's own comment named as missing:
>    `llm/providers/base.py::Embedding`, `llm/providers/ollama.py::embed()` (`/api/embed`, one
>    batched HTTP call per group), `LLMClient.embed(stage, texts)` — per-text disk-cached via the
>    existing `LLMCache`/`make_key` (an embedding's vector is just `json.dumps`'d into the same
>    `CachedResponse.text` field a completion's answer would use), no budget/frontier-scope check
>    (the only role ever routed to `embed` is local/free by construction), one compact run-log line
>    per batch call rather than one per text. `config/models.yaml` gained a `canonicalize -> embed`
>    routing entry — `wiki doctor` health-checks it for free via its existing generic `for stage in
>    routing` loop, no doctor code change needed.
> 2. **`graph/canonicalize.py`** (new module): pure-Python cosine similarity + greedy single-pass
>    clustering (no numpy/sklearn dependency exists in this project, and group sizes are small
>    enough that O(n²) is fine). Buckets by `temporal.normalize_value` first — exact case/whitespace
>    duplicates merge at zero embed cost — then embeds one representative per bucket only when
>    `min_group_size` is met and an embed model is reachable; degrades to normalize-value-only
>    bucketing otherwise (never crashes a `graph build`, never drops a value). Canonical form =
>    highest-confidence, earliest-`first_vol` member of each cluster.
> 3. **Canonicalization wired into `build_graph`**: every multi-valued attribute/trait `(subject,
>    predicate)` group is clustered and remapped to its cluster's canonical value *before*
>    `assign_multi_valued` is called — that function's own exact-string dedup then does the actual
>    merge, unchanged. Merge decisions are recorded in a new `contradictions.json["canonicalization"]`
>    key (CONTRACTS §4.2) for provenance/audit, printed by an extended `wiki audit contradictions`.
> 4. **Relation-conflict arbitration**: `config/extraction.yaml` `relations.*.conflicts_with`
>    (declared symmetrically, `FRIEND_OF`↔`ENEMY_OF` only — deliberately not `RIVAL_OF`, see the
>    config comment on why a bigger fictional taxonomy than the corpus evidence justifies was
>    rejected). A `(subject, object)` pair with claims under ≥2 of a conflict group's predicates
>    routes through the new `_resolve_relation_group` — same-volume ties reuse `_resolve_pair`
>    unchanged via a pseudo `{"value": predicate, ...}` dict (no new arbitrate prompt needed);
>    cross-volume predicate changes supersede via the new `temporal.py::assign_relation_supersession`
>    (structurally `assign_single_valued` with `predicate` varying per entry instead of fixed) —
>    this is the one exception to "relation edges never close" (CONTRACTS §4.1), scoped to
>    conflict-group members only.

**Original line 300:**

> **What:** Both mechanisms from the entry above, implemented as planned:

>    `--attr NAME=format:"Display"[:multi]`, `--trait NAME="Display"[:max_words]`, `--relation
>    NAME="Display"[:symmetric|:inverse=OTHER]` (all additive, parsed by `config.py::

**Original line 10:**

> ## Why this phase exists

**Original line 12:**

> `docs/vision/PHASE_17.md`'s "Fandom-grade depth" entry (2026-09-04) named Phase 17 first among
> five depth phases (17-21), specifically **before** any of them add more extraction volume:
> "depth multiplies duplicates." Two problems, measured against this project's own real output
> (Holo, Spice and Wolf v01-v02): ~40 near-duplicate APPEARANCE fragments for one character, and a
> simultaneous `FRIEND_OF`/`ENEMY_OF` pair on the same relationship. Neither is fixed by a bigger
> model — the unit of extraction (a ±2-paragraph window) means the same fact gets rephrased across
> many windows, and nothing before this phase ever compared two DIFFERENT relation predicates
> against each other for the same pair. Two deliverables:

**Original line 21:**

> 1. **Value canonicalization** — cluster near-duplicate free-text values (multi-valued attributes
>    + traits) via local bge-m3 embeddings, elect one canonical form, merge before rendering.
> 2. **Relation-conflict arbitration** — config-declared mutually-exclusive relation predicates
>    (`FRIEND_OF`/`ENEMY_OF`) arbitrate same-volume, supersede cross-volume — closing the
>    "relation edges never close" gap for exactly this case.

**Original line 27:**

> ```
> config/models.yaml
>   New `canonicalize -> embed` entry under `routing:`. The `embed` profile (bge-m3) already
>   existed (added 2026-09-03) but nothing could call it -- this wires it up. No fallback: embed

> src/narrativewiki/llm/providers/base.py

>   `/api/embed` -- one HTTP call for a whole batch. Same error-handling shape as `complete`
>   (ConnectError/ReadTimeout/404/>=400/`"error"` key -> ProviderError with an actionable message).
>
> src/narrativewiki/llm/client.py
>   New `LLMClient.embed(stage, texts) -> list[list[float]]`. Per-TEXT disk caching (reuses the
>   existing `LLMCache`/`make_key` machinery unchanged -- one input text is the "prompt", the key
>   gains `{"_embed": True}` in its options so an embed cache entry can never collide with a real
>   completion's cache entry for the same text): every miss is batched into ONE provider call. No
>   budget/frontier-scope check (the only role ever routed to `embed` is local/free by
>   construction -- unlike `complete`/`complete_json`, which any stage could in principle route to
>   a paid tier). If `self.run` is set, ONE compact `calls.jsonl` line per `embed()` call (text
>   count + cache-hit count), not one per text -- keeps the run log light for what could be a
>   hundred-plus small groups in a real build. A provider with no `embed` attribute (every provider
>   except ollama today) raises `LLMError` naming the stage, never a silent empty-vector return.
>
> src/narrativewiki/graph/canonicalize.py  (NEW)
>   `cosine(a, b) -> float` (pure Python, no numpy dependency exists in this project and group
>   sizes are small enough O(n^2) is fine) and `cluster_values(entries, embed_fn, threshold,
>   min_group_size) -> list[Cluster]`. Buckets by `temporal.normalize_value` first (exact
>   case/whitespace duplicates merge at zero embed cost, matching the merge rule
>   `assign_multi_valued` already documents but does not itself apply). Below `min_group_size`
>   distinct values, OR `embed_fn is None` (embed model unreachable): returns one cluster per
>   distinct normalized value, no embedding call made -- canonicalization degrades to a no-op, a
>   `graph build` never crashes or drops a value for lack of a pulled bge-m3. Otherwise: one greedy
>   pass over values sorted (confidence desc, first_vol asc) -- each value joins the first existing
>   cluster whose representative cosine similarity crosses `threshold`, else starts a new cluster.
>   `Cluster.canonical` = `members[0]["value"]` (the sort makes this the highest-priority member).
>
> src/narrativewiki/graph/temporal.py
>   New `assign_relation_supersession(subject, obj, ordered_predicates) -> list[interval]` --
>   structurally `assign_single_valued` with `predicate` varying per entry instead of fixed,
>   `object` fixed, `value` staying null (the existing relation-interval convention). The one
>   exception to "relation intervals never close," scoped to conflict-group members only.
>
> src/narrativewiki/graph/contradictions.py
>   `build_graph()` gained two new code paths, both additive to the existing structure --
>   single-valued attribute handling is completely untouched.
>   (1) Canonicalization: for every non-single-attribute/trait `(subject, predicate)` group
>       (`other_claims`, same grouping as before), a new `_run_canonicalization()` clusters the
>       group's values via `canonicalize.cluster_values` (embed_fn wraps `client.embed`, or `None`
>       if `client` is `None`/lacks `.embed`) and returns a `claim_id -> canonical value` remap,
>       applied to each observation's `value_or_object` BEFORE `assign_multi_valued` is called.
>       That function's own exact-string dedup then does the actual interval merge, completely
>       unchanged. Non-singleton merges are recorded into a new `canonicalization_merges` list,
>       which becomes `contradictions_doc["canonicalization"]`.
>   (2) Relation arbitration: `_relation_conflict_groups(relations_cfg)` computes predicate ->
>       conflict-group-members once (union-find over `conflicts_with`, requiring both sides
>       declared). Relation claims are partitioned: a `(subject, object)` pair with claims under
>       >=2 of a conflict group's predicates goes to `pair_claims`, routed through the new
>       `_resolve_relation_group` (arbitrates same-volume ties by reusing `_resolve_pair` UNCHANGED
>       via a pseudo `{"value": predicate, "confidence", "evidence", "claim_id"}` dict -- no new
>       arbitrate prompt was written; the existing one already asks "which fact is correct" and a
>       relation choice fits the same shape); cross-volume predicate changes supersede via
>       `temporal.assign_relation_supersession`. A pair with only ONE conflict-group predicate ever
>       present falls through to the ordinary `assign_multi_valued` path unchanged -- nothing to
>       arbitrate. Everything else (the overwhelming majority of relation claims) is completely
>       unaffected -- `conflict_groups` is empty unless a series' config declares `conflicts_with`.
>   New `_relation_conflict_record()` mirrors `_conflict_record()`'s shape but with a joined
>   `"predicate": "A|B"` and each side carrying its own `predicate` (plus a `value` alias so the

>   `build_graph()`'s module docstring rewritten to describe both new paths.
>
> docs/CONTRACTS.md

**Original line 150:**

> **Two real bugs were caught and fixed by this live run, not by the unit tests** (both fixtures
> were too clean to reproduce them):
> 1. `LLMClient.embed()` did not translate a provider's `ProviderError` into `LLMError` the way
>    `_call` does — an unreachable Ollama crashed `graph build` outright instead of degrading.
>    Fixed: `embed()` now does the same `ProviderError -> LLMError` translation, and
>    `graph/contradictions.py::_run_canonicalization` catches it, falling back to exact-match-only
>    canonicalization for the REST of the run too (a sticky `embed_state["unavailable"]` flag,
>    shared across every `(subject, predicate)` group in one `build_graph()` call) — so one dead
>    connection doesn't retry hundreds of times across a real build.
> 2. `_resolve_relation_group`'s per-volume logic compared the top-two claims BY CONFIDENCE ALONE
>    without first collapsing same-predicate claims — real data had Holo/Liebert's ENEMY_OF
>    extracted independently from both directions (two claim_ids, same canonical predicate, same
>    volume) alongside a genuine FRIEND_OF claim, and confidence ranking could put two ENEMY_OF
>    claims in the top two, producing a nonsensical `"ENEMY_OF|ENEMY_OF"` "conflict" and silently
>    dropping the real FRIEND_OF claim as a lowest-confidence outlier. Fixed: claims are now
>    collapsed to one representative PER PREDICATE per volume first (merging claim_ids, exactly
>    mirroring how `assign_multi_valued` already merges same-predicate relation claims on the
>    ordinary path) — only genuinely different predicates are ever compared. Confirmed by rerunning
>    against real data: the spurious `ENEMY_OF|ENEMY_OF` row disappeared, conflict count dropped
>    from 29 to 23 (the correct count), interval/edge counts unchanged.

**Original line 12:**

**Original line 14:**

> Two measured gaps from this project's own output (Spice and Wolf v01-v02):

**Original line 16:**

> 1. **The mention-window cap discards exactly the scenes that matter.** At 40 windows/character,
>    Holo's v01 pass saw 33.6% of the volume's paragraphs; 62.8% were available. The windows are
>    chosen by mention count, so the quiet character-development scenes — which carry status changes,
>    relationship transitions, and character-revealing dialogue — are exactly what gets dropped.
>    A friend who becomes an enemy mid-volume and is never re-extracted is a fact the graph can never
>    see and therefore can never close the interval for.

**Original line 23:**

> 2. **Pronoun-and-epithet blindness.** Aho-Corasick cannot match “the wisewolf” until that surface
>    form is in the gazetteer. Before this phase, epithets were never mined. A chapter where Holo is
>    only referred to as “the wisewolf” produced zero extraction windows and zero claims, even though
>    the chapter existed and was ingested.

**Original line 28:**

> The fix is a second pass that reads **every paragraph in every chapter** — not just paragraphs
> that contain a known entity mention — in overlapping ~4k-token spans. Coverage becomes 100% by
> construction, and the whole-chapter context carries its own antecedents, so the pronoun problem
> largely dissolves without a coreference model.

> mining+classification+clustering pipeline). It is: (1) local and free -- no LLM call, just a
> surface-form write and automaton rebuild; (2) idempotent -- re-running it over the same epithet
> file produces the same gazetteer; (3) narrowly scoped -- it only touches the surface_forms for
> entities the epithet records mention, not the full entity list.

> ## What Phase 20 added

**Original line 10:**

> `docs/vision/PHASE_17.md`'s Phase 20 entry called for two things: each prose section's length
> scaling with its own evidence volume instead of a global fixed cap, and a deterministic Quotes
> section sourced from the event layer Phase 19 built.

**Original line 14:**

> ### 1. Adaptive sentence budgets

**Original line 16:**

> `config/extraction.yaml`'s `page_outline` sections may now declare `sentences_per_evidence`
> (`chronology`: 0.4, `background`/`personality`: 0.5). `synth/prose.py::_adaptive_bounds(section,
> evidence_count)` computes the actual `(min_s, max_s)` sent to the LLM system prompt:

**Original line 20:**

> ```
> raw   = evidence_count * sentences_per_evidence
> min_s = clamp(round(raw * 0.5), floor, ceil)
> max_s = clamp(max(min_s + 1, ceil(raw)), floor, ceil)
> ```

**Original line 26:**

> `min_sentences`/`max_sentences` become the floor/ceiling instead of the fixed bounds. A section
> without `sentences_per_evidence` is unaffected (`_adaptive_bounds` returns the fixed pair
> unchanged) — this is how `chronology`'s `traits: []` sentinel section and any future
> non-adaptive section stay backward compatible.

**Original line 31:**

> ### 2. Quotes section

**Original line 33:**

> New `kind: quotes` in `page_outline` (config carries `max_quotes` instead of `traits`/sentence
> bounds). `synth/assemble.py::build_quotes_section(events_conn, entity_id, upto_vol, section)` is
> deterministic — no LLM call: it reads `character_events_at`/`event_claims_at` (Phase 19,
> `kind="quote"`), matches `speaker` against the entity's `entity_id` OR (if the caller sets
> `section["_entity_canonical"]`) its canonical name — scene extraction sometimes records the
> surface form rather than the resolved id — sorts by `confidence` descending, deduplicates by the
> quote's first 60 characters, and takes the top N. `cli.py::synthesize` calls it unconditionally
> after assembling each page (not gated by `claim_set_hash`, since it's cheap and its source,
> events.db, is a separate cache domain from graph.db — see Known gaps #1).

**Original line 43:**

> ### 3. `wiki audit outline`
