**Original line 52:**

> ## Bugs found and fixed this session

**Original line 54:**

> The prior session left Phase 20 code-complete but with 2 failing unit tests and had not run it
> against real data. Both were real bugs, not test-fixture issues:

**Original line 57:**

> 1. **`_adaptive_bounds` didn't clamp `min_s` to the ceiling.** With `evidence_count=100,
>    sentences_per_evidence=0.5, max_sentences=6`, `min_s` computed to 25 before ever being
>    compared against `ceil_s` — `tests/test_synth_prose.py::test_adaptive_bounds_clamps_to_ceiling`
>    caught it. Fixed: `min_s = min(ceil_s, max(floor_s, round(raw * 0.5)))` (`prose.py`).

**Original line 62:**

> 2. **`build_quotes_section` only matched `speaker == entity_id`, not the canonical-name
>    fallback its own docstring promised.** `character_events_at` (which gates which events are
>    even considered) was called with `entity_id` alone, so an event whose `participants_json` only
>    contains the surface form/canonical name (not the resolved id) was invisible before the speaker
>    match ever ran. Fixed: `build_quotes_section` now also queries `character_events_at` with
>    `section["_entity_canonical"]` when set, unions the results (`synth/assemble.py`).

**Original line 69:**

> 3. **Found during the live run, not by unit tests:** `ProseText.text`'s `max_length=900` was
>    tuned for the pre-Phase-20 fixed 2-6 sentence range. `chronology`'s new ceiling of 10 sentences
>    let the local `qwen2.5:14b` model legitimately need more room — Kraft Lawrence's Chronology
>    section (53 events at v1) failed validation 3x in a row against the live corpus before this fix
>    landed. Fixed: `prose.py::_prose_schema_for(max_s)` returns the static `ProseText` for
>    `max_s <= 6` (every pre-Phase-20 call site, byte-identical behaviour) and a dynamically
>    constructed schema (`max_length = max_s * 200`) above that. Both `_generate_one` and
>    `generate_chronology` now request the schema sized for their own `max_s`, not a shared constant.

> ## Known gaps (for Phase 21+)

**Original line 136:**

> 1. **Quotes section is not `claim_set_hash`-gated, but the whole cutoff still is.**
>    `cli.py::synthesize` calls `build_quotes_section` only for a cutoff that was NOT skipped by
>    `page_cache.unchanged()` — which checks `graph.db`'s claim set, a completely separate database
>    from `events.db`. If `wiki events-build` is re-run with new data but no trait claim changed,
>    the cutoff is skipped before `build_quotes_section` is ever called, so stale/missing quotes
>    persist until something else invalidates the cutoff. Not hit by the normal pipeline order
>    (`events-build` always runs before `synthesize`, per `wiki step`/`run-all`), but a manual
>    `wiki events-build --force` followed by `wiki synthesize` (no `--force`) would miss it. A full
>    fix needs an `events_hash` folded into the skip decision — deliberately deferred (see the
>    original Phase 20 implementation plan's "Open Questions" section, which made the same call for
>    different reasons: quotes generation is cheap, so the original plan dropped `synth/cache.py`
>    changes entirely; this note is the one place that simplification has a real, if narrow, edge).
> 2. **Local `qwen2.5:14b` does not reliably obey the adaptive sentence-count instruction.**
>    The live run's Chronology section for a well-attested character came back at 12-14 sentences
>    against a computed ceiling of 10 — `wiki audit pages`'s existing "outside configured sentence
>    bounds" check caught this correctly (it already existed pre-Phase-20; nothing new needed
>    there), but the model itself is not compliant. `_prose_schema_for`'s widened `max_length` (see
>    Bugs fixed #3) prevents this from being a hard validation failure, but does not make the model
>    follow the count. Worth a prompt-tuning pass in a future phase if Chronology's local-model
>    accuracy matters more than it did for this verification.
> 3. **`_outline_report`'s prose-section WARN branch is a no-op.** The audit report's own docstring
>    says it should "WARN if the section is None and the character has >0 visible trait claims" but
>    the implementation (inherited from the prior session, `audit/reports.py` around line 580) just
>    computes and discards the check — it never actually opens `graph.db` to look up trait claims,
>    so no WARN is ever emitted. Not a FAIL-class bug (the report still correctly FAILs on the
>    `quotes` over-`max_quotes` case, which is the one hard invariant Phase 20 needed), but the
>    docstring overstates what the check does. Left as-is this session given the live run above
>    didn't surface a real case it would have caught; a future pass should either implement the real
>    check or shrink the docstring to match.
> 4. **OpenRouter free-tier routing is unresolved**, not a Phase 20 defect but blocking anyone who
>    wants API-quality prose without local Ollama running — see the routing section above.

> itself multiple independent deliverables large enough to span several sessions.

**Original line 13:**

> ---

**Original line 15:**

> ## 2026-09-08 — Relationship pages: scope and design decisions (part 1 of 4)

**Original line 17:**

> **What:** Implemented the first of Phase 21's four deliverables: pair-scoped relationship pages
> for CHARACTER-CHARACTER pairs. Full implementation details in `LOG.md`'s 2026-09-08 entry and
> `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §6.4.

**Original line 21:**

> **Why these specific scope cuts (recorded here because they are judgment calls a future session
> should not silently re-litigate):**

**Original line 24:**

> - **Deterministic v1, no LLM summary.** The vision entry says "relationship pages," not
>   "relationship summaries." Phase 20 already established two patterns for a new page surface —
>   `build_quotes_section` (deterministic, no LLM) and `_generate_codex_summary` (LLM, gated on
>   evidence). Relationship pages follow the first: relation history + shared scenes are exactly
>   what `graph.db`/`events.db` already contain, with no need for a model to paraphrase anything.
>   An LLM-generated one-sentence relationship summary (mirroring `codex_summary`) is a clean,
>   separately-scoped follow-up if a future session wants it — not bundled in here.
> - **Population is "pairs with a relation edge," not every possible pair.** A relationship page
>   for two characters who are merely co-mentioned but never assigned a relation predicate would be
>   indistinguishable from a random pairing. `site/bundle.py::_relationship_pairs` derives the
>   population directly from `graph.db`'s `intervals` table (`object IS NOT NULL`), the same
>   ground truth `relations_at` already uses for a character's own Relationships field.
> - **No per-viewer label flip.** `synth/assemble.py::_relationship_entries` flips a non-symmetric

**Original line 53:**

> ## 2026-09-08 — Faction codex enrichment: scope and design decisions (part 2 of 4)

**Original line 55:**

> **What:** Implemented the second of Phase 21's four deliverables: a FACTION codex entry
> (`codex/factions.json`) gains `key_events` — scenes where two or more of the entry's current
> `members` co-appear. Full implementation details in `LOG.md`'s 2026-09-08 entry and
> `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §6.1.

**Original line 60:**

> **Why these specific scope cuts:**

**Original line 62:**

> - **"Faction pages" reads as "richer faction codex entries", not a new unique page type.**
>   `config/extraction.yaml` already declares FACTION as `page: codex` (CLAUDE.md §2 — only
>   CHARACTER gets a unique page); nothing in the original vision entry asked to change that. The
>   gap this part closes is that a codex entry only ever had a one-sentence `summary` +
>   `members`/`related` — no sense of what the group actually DID together, which is exactly what
>   Phase 20's `quotes` and Phase 21 part 1's `shared_scenes` gave characters and pairs.
> - **Co-presence of >= 2 current members, not "any event touching one member."** A well-attested
>   faction's roster can rack up dozens of events through a single popular member — that list would
>   say nothing about the faction as a group. Requiring 2+ members co-present (mirroring part 1's
>   own pair-based `shared_events_at`, generalized) keeps the field meaningfully about the faction
>   acting together. `graph/events.py::group_events_at` is the new sanctioned reader for this.
> - **Config-gated per codex `kind`, never hard-coded to the string "factions".** `codex_pages.
>   <kind>.max_key_events` — present only under `factions` in the shipped config — is what
>   `build_codex_bundles` branches on, not the kind name. A LOCATION/EVENT codex entry (`places`)
>   already IS the event/place (its own evidence covers "what happened here"); a TECH entry isn't a
>   group of co-present people. Neither gains anything from this field, and because `_state_hash`
>   only folds `key_events` into its payload when the kind's config declares `max_key_events`, their
>   hash values — and therefore their `codex_summary` LLM-call cadence — stay byte-identical to
>   before this part existed. A future series or codex kind that DOES want this just adds the config
>   key; no code branch needed.
> - **No faction-to-faction relations added.** Investigated `config/extraction.yaml`'s `relations`
>   block: `AFFILIATED_WITH` is the only relation with `object_types: [FACTION]`, and it is
>   CHARACTER-subject only (extraction is a per-character driver, `extract/claims.py`). A "rival
>   factions" or "allied factions" enrichment would need a genuinely new relation predicate (and
>   probably a new extraction pass, since no existing claim ever has a FACTION subject) — a bigger,
>   separately-scoped change than this part's evidence-surfacing goal, not attempted here.
> - **No roster history (join/leave over time).** `graph/temporal.py::relations_at`'s own docstring
>   already documents the gap this would need closed: relation intervals never close except for a
>   `conflicts_with` group (Phase 17), and `AFFILIATED_WITH` isn't one — so there is no way today to
>   know a character LEFT a faction, only that they were ever affiliated. The existing sparse-cutoff
>   mechanism already reflects membership GROWTH correctly (a new cutoff is written the moment
>   `members` changes, per `_state_hash`); modeling departure is a graph-level change, not a codex
>   one, and out of scope here.

**Original line 101:**

> ## 2026-09-08 — Per-volume timeline pages: scope and design decisions (part 3 of 4)

**Original line 103:**

> **What:** Implemented the third of Phase 21's four deliverables: `data/06_bundle/timeline/
> v{NN}.json`, a chapter-by-chapter recap of one volume's own events, plus `/timeline` and
> `/timeline/<vol>` routes in the viewer. Full implementation details in `LOG.md`'s 2026-09-08 entry
> and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §6.5.

**Original line 108:**

> **Why these specific scope cuts:**

**Original line 110:**

> - **One volume's own events, not a cumulative "story so far."** `graph/events.py::events_at`
>   already gives "everything visible through cutoff V" (used by `character_events_at`/Chronology
>   prose); a timeline page's job is different — "what happened IN volume V specifically," so a
>   reader can walk the story chapter by chapter one volume at a time. This needed a new reader
>   (`events_in_volume`, `WHERE vol = ?` rather than `WHERE vol_start <= ?`) rather than reusing or
>   generalizing an existing one — the semantics genuinely differ, generalizing them into one
>   function would have made both call sites pass a flag to pick a filter mode for no real gain.
> - **No sparse-multi-cutoff shape, unlike every other §6 file.** `events.vol_start` always equals
>   `vol` (CONTRACTS §4b.1 — an event is anchored to its own volume, never forward-dated), so a
>   timeline file's content is permanently fixed the moment `wiki events-build` runs; there is
>   nothing for a later `--upto` rebuild to change. Giving it the same cutoffs/state-hash machinery
>   `build_codex_bundles`/`build_relationship_bundles` need would have been complexity with no
>   payoff — the simplest correct shape here really is "one stable file per volume, present or not."
> - **Deterministic v1, no LLM narrative.** Consistent with every other Phase 20/21 evidence surface
>   (`quotes`, `shared_scenes`, `key_events`) before it — the underlying `beat_summary`/`note` text
>   already reads as prose (LLM-paraphrased at scene-extraction time), so a second LLM pass to
>   narrate "volume 1's story" would be re-paraphrasing an already-paraphrased summary for
>   questionable gain. An LLM-narrated volume recap is a clean, separately-scoped follow-up.
> - **The volume picker gates on the READER's own slider position, not the build's `--upto`.**
>   `renderTimelineIndex` loops `1..state.vol`, not `1..state.index.upto_vol` — a bundle built at
>   `--upto 5` still must not let a reader who has only moved their slider to volume 2 see a
>   "Volume 3 Timeline" link. This mirrors every other per-volume-gated UI element in the viewer
>   (the character roster, codex entries); verified live in the DOM-stub check (see LOG.md).
> - **`state_changes` gets its first-ever renderer here**, not in Phase 19/20. Chronology prose
>   already consumes `event_claims` state_change rows (folded into paraphrased prose), but nothing
>   before this rendered one directly. A timeline page is exactly the surface where showing the raw
>   `note` text (rather than an LLM's re-paraphrase of it) earns its place — it is already a
>   paraphrase once, at scene-extraction time, and showing it verbatim here costs no LLM call.
> - **A real, pre-existing bug found (not introduced) by this part's own live-UI check, fixed in
>   passing:** `app.js::nameFor(null)` rendered the literal text "null" for a quote whose speaker
>   scene extraction never resolved. This was already reachable through `renderSceneCard`'s two
>   earlier callers (relationship shared_scenes, faction key_events) before this part existed;
>   the timeline page's DOM-stub check just happened to be the first time this session's live
>   verification hit a real unresolved-speaker quote. Fixed by making `nameFor` fall back to
>   "Unknown" — a one-line, self-contained fix, not a scope expansion of this part's actual work.

**Original line 150:**

> ## 2026-09-08 — Evaluation harness: scope and design decisions (part 4 of 4, Phase 21 complete)

**Original line 152:**

> **What:** Implemented the fourth and final deliverable of Phase 21: `wiki audit eval`, computing
> heading recall, fact recall, and citation entailment against hand-transcribed gold data from three
> real Spice & Wolf Fandom wiki pages (Holo, Kraft Lawrence, Norah Arendt — the three well-attested
> characters within the project's own volumes 1-2 testing scope). Full implementation details in
> `LOG.md`'s 2026-09-08 entry and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` §8.

**Original line 158:**

> **Why these specific scope cuts:**

**Original line 160:**

> - **`in_scope: true/false` per gold fact, not a flat fact list.** The vision entry's own framing —
>   "depth and hallucination are indistinguishable from the inside" — assumes the comparison is
>   fair. A real Fandom page describes the character across the WHOLE series; this wiki at
>   `eval_vol` 2 is CORRECTLY supposed to omit anything revealed later (CLAUDE.md #1). Scoring recall
>   against those facts would have measured spoiler-safety compliance as a defect. Concretely: Holo
>   and Lawrence's eventual marriage and bathhouse in Nyohhira (the sequel series' setting) is
>   excluded; Lawrence being "respected by Eve and Eringin" is excluded because neither appears in
>   the extracted v1-2 roster at all — cross-checking a candidate gold fact's named entities against
>   the project's OWN roster turned out to be a genuinely useful, cheap sanity signal for "is this
>   even in scope," used throughout the transcription.
> - **Uncertain-provenance facts excluded conservatively, not guessed.** A few real facts (e.g.
>   "Holo is willing to reveal her true wolf form to protect Lawrence") are plausible by volume 2 but
>   not something transcription could confidently place to a specific volume from memory alone —
>   marked `in_scope: false` with a note, rather than asserted. Wrong gold data would be worse than
>   incomplete gold data: it would blame the pipeline for not recalling something never actually
>   guaranteed to be there yet.
> - **WebFetch of fandom.com returned HTTP 402 in this sandbox** (a bot/paywall gate, not a project
>   decision) — transcription used several targeted WebSearch queries against the same
>   `spiceandwolf.fandom.com` pages instead of one full-page fetch. Documented in each gold file's
>   header comment as a real, non-hidden constraint on completeness, not silently worked around.
> - **Both recall metrics are lexical keyword-overlap heuristics, not an LLM judge.** Consistent
>   with CLAUDE.md §2's "local first," no-wasted-call discipline extended to evaluation itself — an
>   LLM-as-judge pass over 3 characters' worth of facts was a real option, deliberately not taken, in
>   favor of a deterministic, free, immediately-rerunnable check. The tradeoff surfaced live: real
>   facts already present in the generated pages (Norah's tailor dream, her sheepdog Enek, her Church
>   background — all confirmed present by directly reading `data/05_pages/norah-arendt/v02.json`)
>   scored as "not recalled" because the exact wording differed enough that keyword overlap fell
>   under the found-threshold. This is a real, known limitation of a lexical heuristic, not a defect
>   in the actual generated wiki content — `_eval_report`'s own docstring and CONTRACTS §8 call this
>   out explicitly, and the report always prints the per-fact miss list specifically so a human
>   reviewer catches false negatives like this one by eye rather than trusting the number alone.
> - **Citation entailment needs no gold data — it self-checks the page's own citations** (does the
>   cited paragraph exist, does the prose share vocabulary with it), rather than trying to verify
>   facts against an external source, which a lexical heuristic cannot do reliably. Live run finding:
>   `chronology` sections scored "weak overlap" for all three characters (Norah's had zero cited
>   paragraphs at all) — traced to `generate_chronology`'s `evidence` list only collecting
>   `event_claims` para_ids as a bonus, not the underlying `beat_summary` paraphrases the prose is
>   actually built from (Phase 19 design, CONTRACTS §4b.2's "the one un-gated field"); the citation
>   entailment check does not currently look at `beat_summary` provenance at all. Left as a
>   documented known gap rather than fixed here — fixing it is a Phase 19/`eval/gold.py` design
>   question of its own, out of this part's scope.
> - **No new top-level CLI command.** `wiki audit eval` reuses the existing `audit/reports.py`
>   registry (`@register("eval", "wiki synthesize")`) exactly like every other phase's report,
>   inheriting `wiki audit run`'s HTML export for free — consistent with "every phase has one"
>   (CLAUDE.md file map) rather than inventing a parallel `wiki eval` surface.
> - **Descriptive, not a spoiler-safety gate.** `_eval_report` FAILs only on a structural problem (a
>   gold `entity_id` with no generated page at all) — never on a low recall/entailment score. Depth
>   and hallucination-avoidance quality are a continuum for a human to read and judge from the
>   report's printed detail; CLAUDE.md #1's one hard boolean invariant stays `test_spoiler_leak.py`'s
>   job, not this one's.

**Original line 211:**

> **Status:** Done (Phase 21, part 4 of 4). **Phase 21 is now complete** — all four deliverables
> (relationship pages, faction codex enrichment, per-volume timelines, evaluation harness) shipped.

**Original line 214:**

> ## 2026-09-08 — Closing the "chronology citation entailment" known gap: eval-only, not page-widening

**Original line 216:**

> **What:** Fixed the first known gap listed above and in `docs/handover/PHASE_21.md`: a chronology
> section with no `event_claims` (state_change/quote) scored "0 cited paragraphs" / "weak overlap"
> even when well-grounded, because `synth/prose.py::generate_chronology`'s stored `evidence` never
> included each event's own `core_para_ids` (`graph/events.py`) — the paragraphs `beat_summary` was
> actually paraphrased from.

**Original line 222:**

> **Why this specific fix, over the alternative already named in the known-gap text:** The known gap
> named two options — widen what `generate_chronology` records as `evidence`, or teach
> `score_citation_entailment` to check `core_para_ids` separately. The first was tried and reverted
> in this same session: `core_para_ids` is chapter-span-scale (12-158 paragraphs per scene in the
> live spice-and-wolf v1-2 corpus, not a handful), so folding it into a character's stored page
> evidence made Holo's `evidence` list balloon to **5103** entries and her `v02.json` grow from
> 10KB to 142KB — for a character present in most scenes, "evidence" degenerated into "somewhere in
> most of the corpus," which is technically defensible (beat_summary genuinely was paraphrased from
> that whole span) but useless as a citation and a real regression against CLAUDE.md §2's token/data
> discipline once run across a full 13-volume corpus. **Chose the second option instead**: `graph/
> events.py`'s `events` table gained a `core_para_ids_json` column (additive, harmless — exposes an
> event's true grounding to anyone who queries it, e.g. a future `wiki explain`-style tool), but
> `generate_chronology`'s own `evidence` stays event_claims-only, exactly as before. `eval/gold.py::
> score_citation_entailment` gained optional `events_conn`/`entity_id`/`vol`/`events_source_keys`
> kwargs: for a `source: "events"`-configured section only (chronology, identified generically via
> `page_outline`, never hard-coded by key name), it ALSO checks vocabulary overlap against the union
> of that character's events' `core_para_ids` — on demand, printed only in the eval report, never
> written to `data/05_pages/`. Live re-run confirmed the fix: Norah Arendt's chronology now reports
> `grounded (0 cited paragraph(s); beat_summary check: grounded (966 paragraph(s)))` instead of the
> previous `weak overlap` — while her page's own stored `evidence` count stays 0, unchanged.

> ## 2026-09-09 — Audit of the shipped Spice & Wolf v1-2 bundle, and the plan it produced

**Original line 9:**

> **What:** An independent audit measured `dist/spice-and-wolf/site` and `data/spice-and-wolf/`
> directly rather than reading the audit reports (which disagree with the data). Verdict: the site
> renders, link integrity is perfect (100 links, 0 broken), ingest is clean, the timeline pages are
> the best writing on the site, and **the spoiler invariant holds — zero leaks across every V1
> cutoff**. Underneath, 127,155 words produced **255 claims**, 5 of 14 character pages have no facts,
> 24% of the graph is APPEARANCE noise, and 56 scenes produced 0 state changes and 0 locations.

**Original line 16:**

> Eight defects were filed (S1-S8), and the user reported seven more from reading the site (U1-U7).
> Every one was re-verified against data on disk before planning.

**Original line 19:**

> **Why it matters more than the numbers suggest — three findings that reframe the work:**

**Original line 21:**

> 1. **A crashed run is still feeding the pipeline.** `_runs/20260904T133513-extract-v1-1/manifest.json`
>    records `"outcome": "failed"` (`Cannot reach Ollama`), yet its partial `03_claims/v01.jsonl`
>    (77 claims, 2 of the volume's 7 mentioned characters) is what every later stage read. Nothing
>    checks upstream outcome: `provenance.py` writes `outcome`, and only `wiki runs` / `calls` /
>    `rollback` / `audit run` ever read it. Stage gating is file-existence only. Volume 2, extracted
>    by a run that finished, handles comparable minor characters fine — so the five empty pages are
>    not an extraction-difficulty signal, they are the crash.
> 2. **The routing on disk pointed at a dead model.** `claim_extract`/`scene_extract` routed to
>    `local_fast` -> `ollama qwen2.5:14b`, and `canonicalize` -> `embed` -> `ollama bge-m3`. Ollama is
>    not running here. The V2 claims say `google:gemini-flash-lite-latest` — an ad-hoc `-m` override
>    never written back, so the config disagreed with what actually ran. Consequence: **Phase 17's
>    embedding-based value canonicalization has been silently no-op'ing**, degrading to exact-string
>    bucketing (`contradictions.json`: only 10 variants absorbed across the whole graph). That is a
>    large part of why the APPEARANCE noise never collapsed.
> 3. **Most of what the user asked for already exists and is simply not wired up.** `polarity:
>    [asserted, denied, presumed]` is extracted (4 claims carry `presumed`) and rendered by nothing.
>    `attributes.*.format`, `confidence.min_for_structured_field` and `conflicts.quiet_change` all
>    have **no consumer anywhere in `src/`**. `graph/canonicalize.py` exists but skips every
>    `single: true` attribute by design.

**Original line 41:**

> **The user's seven issues, with their verified causes:**

**Original line 43:**

> - **U1 — pronouns lose information.** No coreference anywhere in `src/`. The prompt never tells the
>   model that a fact stated about the subject under a pronoun still counts, so it skips those
>   sentences. Decision: fix at the **prompt level only** — no coref model, no new pass, no new calls.
>   `docs/handover/PHASE_18.md` already argued whole-chapter spans dissolve most of this; the missing
>   piece is telling the model so.
> - **U2 — "25 years" (v1) vs "twenty-five years" (v2).** Lawrence has *four* AGE claims: `'25'`,
>   `'twenty-five'`, `'twenty-five years old'` (v1) and `'twenty-five years'` (v2). `AGE` is
>   `single: true`, which `canonicalize` explicitly skips; the only comparison in the graph is
>   `temporal.normalize_value` = `.strip().casefold()`. So the v2 rephrasing reads as a genuine
>   narrative change — it is the single `narrative_change` in `contradictions.json`.
> - **U3 — unwanted "(since v1)".** Emitted unconditionally by `okf.py:72,79,87,96` and
>   `app.js:236,239,281,291`. Compounded by `conflicts.quiet_change` having no consumer: Lawrence's
>   `age.changes_later` is correctly `false`, yet `previously: 25 (v1-1)` still prints.
>   Decision: show a volume marker **only where a value actually changed**; stable facts render bare;
>   spans stay inside history/expandables.
> - **U4 — cryptic relationship tags.** `synth/assemble.py:173` is `row["qualifier"] or display`,
>   letting unvalidated free text *replace* the config display label. Lawrence's page carries 20 rows
>   for 9 people, with four Holo badges reading `Comrade of` / `Friend of` /
>   `wife (false identity claimed)` / `fake`, and a Jakob pair reading `Child of` +
>   `acquaintance / former master`. `okf.py::_relationship_lines` doesn't even group by person.
> - **U5 — "also connected to" with no explanation.** `assemble.py:225` `mentions_of` is raw
>   `ppr.personalized_pagerank(top_k=8)` with no type filter; 6 of Lawrence's 8 chips are entities
>   already rendered above in Relationships/Affiliations. Unexplained *and* duplicative.
> - **U6 — status is null.** Zero STATUS claims exist for Lawrence or Holo. The field is **absent
>   entirely** from the page dict (`_build_attribute_fields` skips predicates with no rows), so no
>   Status row renders at all.
> - **U7 — "dead" vs "presumed dead".** `polarity` is extracted, stored, and read into the page model
>   by `_scalar_field` — then rendered by nothing. "presumed dead" is currently indistinguishable
>   from "dead", exactly the collapse `config/extraction.yaml`'s own `polarity:` block says must
>   never happen.

**Original line 74:**

> **Implies (the plan, in three call-neutral-or-negative phases):**

**Original line 76:**

> - **Phase A — recover what has already been paid for.** Quarantine failed runs and add a claim-file
>   completeness assertion; format-aware value normalization + deterministic appearance subsumption
>   (works with or without a reachable embed model); membership-predicate filtering for factions;
>   wikify every `beat_summary`; and a deterministic page-model/rendering pass covering U3-U7, a lead
>   sentence, section reorder, and a page-existence gate. One re-extraction, then zero new calls.
> - **Phase B — reallocate the calls already being made.** Split the scene call in two (a 14B model
>   handed a six-field schema over a 4k-token span degrades to the easiest field — 56/56 empty
>   `state_changes` is what that looks like); prompt-level coreference hardening + the phantom-entity
>   fix; replace the flat 40-window cap with a sqrt(mentions) budget; cap codex evidence.
> - **Phase C — invert the two passes.** Make the chapter-span pass primary (it already reads 100% of
>   paragraphs for a fifth of the cost), demote mention windows to a targeted top-up, add a
>   verification pass rather than a bigger extraction pass, and grow the gold set to ten characters
>   and gate on it.

**Original line 90:**

> **Decisions taken and NOT taken:**

**Original line 92:**

> - **Rejected: adding a coreference model.** It would be a new dependency and a new pass for a
>   problem the span pass plus two prompt rules should largely absorb. Revisit only if measurement
>   after Phase B still shows pronoun-driven loss.
> - **Rejected: synthesizing a default STATUS as a graph interval.** That would fabricate a claim with
>   no evidence (violating CLAUDE.md §2) and silently change `claim_set_hash`. The default belongs in
>   `config/extraction.yaml` as an `attributes.*.default` key, materialized at
>   `synth/assemble.py::_build_attribute_fields` and marked `inferred: true` — spoiler-safe by
>   construction, since "alive" is the reader's default at any cutoff and a later death is a claim
>   that only appears once the reader reaches it.
> - **Rejected: special-casing any predicate by name.** Every new behaviour is driven by a new config
>   key, preserving the "rendering is generic" invariant `config/extraction.yaml` opens with.
> - **Kept: `canonicalize` still routed at the local `embed` profile.** Phase A's subsumption is
>   deterministic and degrades gracefully, so there is no reason to spend API budget on embeddings.

**Original line 467:**

> **B2 — coreference hardening (U1) + the phantom-entity fix (S3).** Three independent fixes:
> (1) `claims.py::_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE` gained two rules: a fact about the subject stated through a
> pronoun or epithet still counts when the passage makes the antecedent unambiguous (the recall
> half), paired with an explicit "omit rather than guess" rule for the genuinely ambiguous case —
> so recall doesn't just trade for a new hallucination mode. (2) Both drivers' user prompts now
> list other named entities grouped by entity_id (`resolve.py::group_known_entities`, new) as
> `"Kraft Lawrence (also: Lawrence, Kraft)"` instead of a flat set of raw surfaces
> (`{m["surface"] for m in mentions}`) — this is the actual, confirmed cause of a beat_summary
> hallucinating "Lawrence sells furs to Kraft Lawrence": two aliases of one person read to the
> model as two different people with nothing tying them together, and `beat_summary` is never
> resolved against entities, so no resolution rule downstream could have fixed it. (3)
> `resolve.py::resolve_surface`'s fallback replaced raw bidirectional substring containment (which
> could misresolve a fragment sharing no whole word with a candidate, e.g. "man" inside "Norman")
> with a whole-word name-part rule — a bare "Kraft" now resolves to a "Kraft Lawrence" candidate via
> token-set containment, and when more than one candidate qualifies the longest (most specific)
> surface wins, not the first one in list order. While in `schema.py`: `_is_usable_fact` compared
> `kind` against `_VALID_KINDS` case-sensitively, so a model emitting `"kind": "RELATION"` (rather
> than lowercase) silently lost the fact before `claims.py::_lookup_predicate` ever got a chance to
> re-derive the true kind from config — fixed by lowercasing `kind` before that check
> (`_normalize_kind`). Client-side, `app.js::renderSceneCard` now filters out any quote whose
> speaker didn't resolve instead of rendering it with a "— Unknown" byline (a placeholder that reads
> as a real, if anonymous, attribution to a reader).

> gets passed through as) and an optional `drops: Counter[str]` that records `window_cap_truncated`

> per-character mention counts once and calls `allocate_window_caps` before its character loop,
> threading each entity's share through `extract_character_volume` into `build_windows`; the existing

> `window_cap_truncated`, so `wiki extract`'s dropped-reasons line reports it with no CLI change

> uncapped windows) and `_cap_codex_evidence` (caps a windows pool by BOTH `max_windows` (5) AND a new
> total-token budget, `window.codex_max_evidence_tokens`, default 2000 — a window-count cap alone let
> merged windows for a corpus-wide entity like "the Legion" total ~30k tokens for a one-sentence

> accumulates one volume's windows per iteration (`raw_windows = raw_windows + _codex_windows_for_volume(...)`)
> instead of re-scanning volume 1..vol from scratch on every cutoff — O(upto_vol) window builds
> instead of O(upto_vol^2). (3) The LLM-call decision is now decoupled from the cutoff-entry-write

> evidence-only hash changed; a membership-only change (e.g. a character newly joining a faction with
> no new evidence) reuses the previous cutoff's summary text/evidence instead of re-paying for an
> identical prompt.

>    `cli.py`'s `synthesize` command's A5 minimum-evidence gate (`has_min_evidence`) skips writing a

>    "note"}]` dicts) — crashing `_links_report`'s `TypeError: string indices must be integers, not
>    'str'`. Same bug, same fix, in `cli.py`'s `site_build`: the character-page-bundle,
>    codex-bundle, and relationship-bundle writers each only ever WRITE what the current run

> — current state only (`state_at`/`relations_at`, not `history_at`, since a superseded value isn't
> what the live page asserts today), each fact paired with up to 2 evidence quotes via

> `assemble_page()`'s rendered dict, which deliberately drops `claim_ids`/evidence entirely.
> `graph/verify.py::verify_character()` makes the one call per character (`VerificationResult` ->
> `flags: [{fact_index, rationale}]`, resolved back against the numbered fact list the prompt showed
> it) and, mirroring `graph/contradictions.py`'s own `client=None`/empty-input handling, degrades to
> "skipped, zero flags" rather than a fabricated verdict whenever there is nothing to check or no
> model reachable.

>       which is why 9 `speaker: null` quotes shipped unnoticed.

> - [x] **B1. Split the scene call in two.** Done 2026-09-10 — see the dated entry above. Original

### docs/handover/PHASE_22.md

Source: [PHASE_22.md](handover/PHASE_22.md). SHA-256: `0cf4f3d735d730b8591b0c46e8189fe4cc179f35f42a2cc6ebe28dc897c51894`.

**Original line 1:**

> # Phase 22 Handover — Output quality: from a crashed-run audit to a verified, gated harness (COMPLETE)

**Original line 3:**

> **Status:** All of A1-A6, B1-B4, and C1-C4 shipped and verified. Full test suite: 615 tests, all
> green. One real corpus run happened mid-phase (`Re-extract V1+V2`, local Ollama, $0 spend); every
> other sub-item was verified against scripted fake LLM clients only, per this project's
> "budget real spend deliberately" discipline — see "Known gaps" below for what that means for
> anyone about to spend real money on this series.

**Original line 9:**

> Phase 22 began as a single independent audit (`docs/vision/PHASE_22.md`'s 2026-09-09 entry) of the
> shipped Spice & Wolf v1-2 bundle, which found the graph nearly empty (255 claims, 5 of 14 character
> pages with zero facts) and traced it to three root causes: a crashed extraction run silently
> feeding every later stage, routing pointed at a dead local model, and several already-extracted
> fields (`polarity`, `conflicts.quiet_change`, format-aware normalization) with zero consumers
> anywhere in `src/`. That audit produced a three-track plan (A: recover what's already paid for: B:
> reallocate calls already being made; C: invert the two extraction passes) — this handover covers
> all three tracks end to end so a cold contributor never has to reconstruct the arc from `LOG.md`
> scrollback or `docs/vision/PHASE_22.md`'s ~900 lines of dated entries.

**Original line 19:**

> ---

**Original line 21:**

> ## What exists now

**Original line 23:**

> ### Track A — recover what was already paid for

**Original line 25:**

> - **A1 — failed-run quarantine + claims-completeness gate.** `provenance.py::COMMAND_STAGE_KEYS`,
>   `last_run_for_stage`, `failed_stage_artifacts`; `cli.py::_guard_upstream_failures`, called first
>   thing in `extract`/`scenes`/`graph build`/`synthesize`/`site build`/`verify` — aborts with the
>   crashed run's id and the `wiki rollback` command unless `--allow-partial`. `graph build` also
>   gets `_incomplete_claim_volumes`: a volume's claims file must carry every mentioned CHARACTER as
>   a claim subject or the build stops naming exactly who's missing. This is the check that would
>   have caught the original crash. CONTRACTS §7.7.
> - **A2 — format-aware value normalization + subsumption.** `temporal.normalize_value(value, fmt)`
>   (`attributes.*.format`, e.g. AGE's `number_or_range` folding `'twenty-five'`/`'25'`/etc. to one
>   value); `contradictions.py::_collapse_same_normalized_value` (same-volume phrasings never reach
>   arbitration as a fake tie); `canonicalize.py::subsume_values()` (deterministic, no embed call —
>   token-subset and lone-noun pruning, gated on `attributes.*.subsume: true`, APPEARANCE only);
>   `conflicts.quiet_change` finally has a consumer (`synth/assemble.py`). CONTRACTS §4.2.
> - **A3 — faction membership + key-event participation.** `relations.*.membership: true`
>   (AFFILIATED_WITH/SERVES_UNDER/COMMANDS + ORIGIN_FROM/PARTICIPATED_IN/PILOTS) filters
>   `site/bundle.py::_members_and_related`'s `members` list; ENEMY_OF/RIVAL_OF routes to a separate
>   `adversaries` bucket. `_faction_key_events` now also requires the faction itself to be a
>   participant or the scene's location, fixing two factions sharing most of their roster from
>   rendering byte-identical key-event lists. CONTRACTS §4.3 (bundle), `app.js` Adversaries row.
> - **A4 — every `beat_summary` wikified.** Faction `key_events`, relationship `shared_scenes`, and
>   timeline events all hyperlink entity mentions now, via the same `site/wikify.py` pass prose
>   already got; `_links_report` validates those links too. Timeline `chapter_idx` fixed from 0- to
>   1-based.
> - **A5 — page model + rendering (U3-U7, S5, S6).** `attributes.*.default` materializes an
>   `inferred: true` scalar field with no backing claim (STATUS defaults to "alive"); `_claim_polarity`
>   reads the most-recent VISIBLE claim, not `claim_ids[0]` (closes a real spoiler gap);
>   `polarity_prefixed()` renders "presumed X"/"not X"; a relationship's `label` is always the config
>   display text (qualifier demotes to `note`/`blurb`), and `relationships` entries finally carry
>   `current`/`vol_end` the way `affiliations` always did; `show_vol` gates every "(since vN)" marker
>   to genuine reveals; `mentions_of` deduplicates against what's already shown and gets an
>   annotation; `page["lead"]` is a new one-line "status · affiliation" summary;
>   `has_min_evidence()`/`find_name_collisions()` gate a page from being written with zero real
>   evidence and flag same-name-different-type collisions (Saint Ruvinheigen: character vs. city).
>   CONTRACTS §5/§5.1.
> - **A6 — yield assertions.** `_claims_report`/`_scenes_report` now hard-FAIL on their OWN stage's
>   crashed-run outcome (closing the gap that A1's guard only covers downstream commands, not
>   reports); roster yield and APPEARANCE-share numbers print on every run; `_outline_report`'s dead
>   prose-completeness branch now actually warns; `_links_report` FAILs on a `speaker: null` quote
>   anywhere in the bundle. CONTRACTS §7.8.

**Original line 65:**

> ### Track B — reallocate the calls already being made

**Original line 67:**

> - **B1 — the scene call split in two.** `extract/scenes.py` makes a beat call
>   (participants/location/beat_summary) and a detail call (state_changes/quotes/epithets), sharing
>   one cached prompt prefix — 56 → 112 calls/volume, same cost tier, much better per-field recall
>   (the old combined prompt's one worked example never demonstrated a non-empty state_change).
> - **B2 — coreference hardening + phantom-entity fix.** Two new prompt rules (a pronoun/epithet
>   referring to the subject still counts when unambiguous; omit rather than guess when ambiguous);
>   known entities now listed grouped by entity_id (`"Kraft Lawrence (also: Lawrence, Kraft)"`,
>   `resolve.py::group_known_entities`) instead of a flat surface set — the confirmed cause of a
>   "Lawrence sells furs to Kraft Lawrence" hallucination; `resolve_surface`'s containment fallback
>   is now whole-word, longest-match-wins. Quote cards with an unresolved speaker are suppressed
>   client-side rather than rendered "— Unknown".
> - **B3 — proportional window budget.** `extract/windows.py::allocate_window_caps` replaces the flat
>   per-character window cap with a shared per-volume pool split by `sqrt(mention_count)`, floored at
>   `min_windows_per_entity_per_volume` so a low-mention character isn't squeezed to nothing next to
>   a protagonist.
> - **B4 — capped, cheaper codex evidence.** `site/bundle.py::_cap_codex_evidence` caps by BOTH
>   window count and a token budget (`window.codex_max_evidence_tokens`); the cutoff loop now
>   accumulates windows incrementally (O(upto_vol), was O(upto_vol²)); the LLM call is now decoupled
>   from the cutoff-entry-write decision, so a membership-only change reuses the previous summary
>   instead of re-paying for an identical prompt.
> - **Re-extract V1+V2 — the one real corpus run this phase.** Ran the full pipeline against
>   `--series spice-and-wolf` on LOCAL OLLAMA (not the API the TODO anticipated — `GOOGLE_API_KEY`
>   was unset, so it silently fell back; $0 spend, not apples-to-apples with the Gemini-produced
>   baseline). Every graph-cleanliness metric improved (roster yield 9/14 → 12/14, APPEARANCE share
>   24% → 12%, conflicts 23 → 3); gold-eval fact recall was a mixed bag (two characters up, one flat,
>   one to zero) — most plausibly a local-model capability gap, not a regression from these fixes.
>   Two real bugs found and fixed here, both invisible until a live run finally exercised the code
>   path: stale page/bundle files never cleaned up when an entity/cutoff falls out of scope
>   (`synthesize`/`site_build` now delete what the current run doesn't produce); unresolved-speaker
>   quotes reaching the bundle JSON despite the client already hiding them (`_shared_scenes_between`/
>   `_faction_key_events`/`_event_claims_split` now filter on `speaker` server-side too).

**Original line 99:**

> ### Track C — invert the two extraction passes

**Original line 101:**

> - **C1 — the chapter-span pass becomes primary.** `wiki scenes`'s detail call gains
>   `participant_facts` — attribute/relation/trait facts per participant, reusing
>   `claim_extract`'s exact vocabulary/validation (`schema.ExtractedFact`) — folded into the
>   EXISTING detail call, zero extra calls per span. Written to a new file,
>   `data/03_claims/scene_v{NN}.jsonl`, leaving `wiki extract`'s own file untouched; `wiki graph
>   build` globs both and merges by `claim_id`. This is now the primary facts source (100% paragraph
>   coverage at a fifth of the per-span cost of the mention-window pass).
> - **C2 — `wiki extract --entities` becomes a targeted top-up.** The old "skip if the volume's
>   claim file exists" guard no longer fires when `--entities` is given — it re-extracts only the
>   named character(s) and merges the result in (`cli.py::_merge_by_entity`, keyed on claim
>   `subject`), leaving everyone else's claims untouched. `wiki audit eval` prints the exact top-up
>   command for any gold character under 50% fact recall.
> - **C3 — a verification pass, not a bigger extraction pass.** New `wiki verify --upto N`: one
>   `verify`-role LLM call per CHARACTER entity (skipped when there's nothing to check), asking
>   whether each currently-visible fact is actually supported by its own cited evidence
>   (`synth/assemble.py::fact_set_for_verification`, `graph/verify.py::verify_character`). Never
>   mutates a claim/interval/page — a flagged fact is only logged to the new
>   `data/04_graph/verification.json`, surfaced via `wiki audit verify`. Wired into `run-all`, NOT
>   into `wiki step` (would raise its per-chapter cost). CONTRACTS §4.3.
> - **C4 — gold set grown to ten characters, regression gate added.** Six new hand-transcribed gold
>   files (`docs/eval/gold/spice-and-wolf/*.yaml`, now 10 of 14 gazetteer characters). New
>   `docs/eval/gold/<series>/baseline.json` (hand-maintained, `{entity_id: fact_recall}`, recorded
>   from a real `wiki audit eval` run against the data already on disk) — `_eval_report` now FAILs
>   when a character WITH a recorded baseline drops below it, while staying purely advisory for any
>   character with none. CONTRACTS §8.

> 1. **Only one real corpus run happened this whole phase** (`Re-extract V1+V2`, local Ollama, $0).

>    live run (`wiki scenes --force && wiki extract --force && wiki graph build && wiki verify --upto
>    2 && wiki synthesize --force --upto 2 && wiki site build --force`) is the first chance to see
>    C1's `participant_facts`, C2's top-up path, and C3's verification prompt behave against real
>    model output, not just a scripted one — budget accordingly before running it (C3 alone is ~14
>    calls at `--upto 2`; C1 folds into the existing scene call at no extra cost).
> 2. **`baseline.json`'s ten numbers reflect a pre-Phase-22-C1/C2/C3 extraction state.** They were
>    recorded from whatever pages already existed on disk (post `Re-extract V1+V2`, before C1's
>    `participant_facts` or C3's verification had ever actually run against real data) — not a
>    fresh re-run incorporating this phase's own facts-quality changes. The next real
>    `wiki graph build && wiki synthesize --force --upto 2` is likely to move these numbers
>    (hopefully up, given C1 makes the chapter-span pass primary); update `baseline.json` by hand
>    once that run's numbers are trustworthy, rather than leaving stale pre-C1 numbers as the floor.
> 3. **`enek.yaml` (new in C4) documents a live, real extraction bug**: `enek/v02.json` currently
>    renders `RELATIVE_OF Holo` and `FRIEND_OF Lawrence` relationship rows nothing in the real
>    character's story supports. Not fixed in this phase (C4's scope was gold-data coverage, not
>    extraction correctness) — a good first target for the next real `wiki verify` run to confirm it
>    actually catches, and for a human to look at afterward regardless.
> 4. **`saint-ruvinheigen` still has no generated page at all** (the A5 name-collision finding —
>    character vs. the city he's named after) and was deliberately left out of the C4 gold-set
>    expansion for that reason (a permanent FAIL with nothing to measure). `weiz`/`count-ehrendott`/
>    `saint-metrogius` also remain gold-uncovered — the 10-character TODO target was met without
>    them, but nothing stops extending further.
> 5. **No automatic "sweep only where scenes came up short" mode.** `wiki extract` with no

>    printed top-up suggestion and run it.
> 6. **`arbitrate`'s `local_best` role has no working fallback for "Ollama unreachable"** (only for
>    "API key missing") — flagged since A1, never picked up; `wiki graph build --allow-partial` gets
>    past both stage guards and then still dies at the first contradiction needing arbitration if
>    Ollama is down. The same gap now also exists for `verify` (C3's new role, same fallback shape).

### docs/vision/PHASE_23.md

Source: [PHASE_23.md](vision/PHASE_23.md). SHA-256: `2acb73ab780f0002a4d369c94c989ca98c3d26cda0901fb80729e0224075a599`.

**Original line 1:**

> # Phase 23 — Precision, Grounding, and Fandom-Grade Pages

**Original line 3:**

> ## 2026-09-10 — Scope and design decisions

**Original line 5:**

> **Trigger:** user audit of the live Spice and Wolf v1-2 site. `/#/relationships/marheit/kraft-lawrence`
> renders "Kraft Lawrence — Spouse of — Marheit," which is false. Investigation (three parallel
> Explore passes over the graph DB, the extraction pipeline, and the rendered bundle/site) found this
> is not an isolated bug but the normal output quality of the pipeline as it stands after Phase 22:

**Original line 10:**

> - Root cause of the spouse claim: a 5-paragraph evidence window (`context_paragraphs_before/after:
>   2`) that excludes the actual referent of "partner" (Holo, named 3 paragraphs past the window
>   edge); a prompt that forces an attribution to the one subject in scope even when the passage
>   isn't about them; `SPOUSE_OF` carrying no guardrail `note:` (unlike `RELATIVE_OF`/`COMMANDS`,
>   which do); and `extract/resolve.py::resolve_surface` binding the relation's object to a string
>   the model echoed from the prompt's own `group_known_entities()` label
>   (`"Lawrence Kraft (also: Lawrence)"`) rather than a name from the passage — confirmed systemic:
>   194 of 621 extraction calls in the live run returned an object of this shape.
> - Graph-wide: 29 of 47 relation claims cite evidence that does not name both endpoints; 15 name
>   neither. `RELATIVE_OF` (14 intervals, second most common predicate) is essentially all wrong.
>   `CHILD_OF` fired in both directions off one sarcastic line. A captive renders as a company
>   "member." Four unrelated `FRIEND_OF` edges all cite the same two-word quote, `"Fall back."`
> - No layer in the pipeline checks a fact against its own evidence and can act on the result.
>   `wiki verify` (Phase 22 C3) is the only evidence-grounded check, has never run on this series
>   (`verification.json` absent), is advisory-only by explicit design ("never mutates a claim,
>   interval, or page"), and is misrouted to an unreachable local model with no working fallback.
>   `intervals`/`edges` carry no confidence column, so no downstream filter is even expressible.
> - No precision metric exists anywhere. `eval/gold.py` measures recall and self-consistency only;
>   its `_page_text()` flattens predicate names into the keyword bag, so a false relation can only
>   *raise* the recall score. Zero of ~615 tests assert an extracted relation is correct.
> - Presentation gap vs the Fandom reference (via the repo's own hand-transcribed gold data, since
>   live WebFetch of fandom.com returned HTTP 402): target shape is Appearance/Personality/
>   History/Relationships/Trivia as narrative prose with volume citations; current pages are
>   infobox fragments plus contradictory predicate-badge pills, `aliases` dropped from the page
>   model entirely, evidence never rendered, 5 of 13 pages with zero prose sections, mean gold fact
>   recall 0.19. Also found: the chapter-span scene pass (documented as "the primary facts source")
>   emitted zero `participant_facts` across 25 scenes — likely an output-token cap mismatch between
>   `scenes.py`'s request and the `google_fast` model profile — leaving 100% of relations sourced
>   from the narrow window pass that produced the spouse bug.

**Original line 40:**

> **Decisions** (confirmed with the user):
> 1. A fact whose own cited evidence does not support it is **withheld entirely** from rendered
>    pages, not hedged or merely logged — nothing ships that the pipeline cannot defend.
> 2. Both correctness AND presentation are in scope for this phase — fixing extraction alone would
>    leave true facts in an amateur-looking infobox/badge layout; restyling alone would polish wrong
>    facts.
> 3. V1-V2 will be fully re-extracted after the code lands (cache goes cold — prompts and gates
>    change), with before/after precision and recall recorded in the handover as proof.

**Original line 49:**

> **Scope, six parts** (full rationale and file-by-file plan in the approved plan file; mirrored here
> per the append-only rule so the decision trail survives independent of that file):
> - **A — extraction-side precision gates:** fix `resolve_surface` (reject echoed prompt labels,
>   require passage-occurrence, return `None` on ambiguity instead of silently picking one); a new
>   evidence-adequacy gate (`requires_both_endpoints`, `min_quote_words`, `subject_must_be_named`)
>   for family/command predicates; guardrail `note:`s for every relation that lacks one; relation
>   `conflicts_with` groups plus rejection of mutual same-predicate edges; wire the already-declared
>   but dead `min_for_structured_field: 0.7`.
> - **B — make verification binding:** add `confidence`/`evidence_count` to `intervals` and a new
>   `verdicts` table; withhold `unsupported`-verdict or sub-threshold facts at assembly (reversible —
>   nothing is deleted, `wiki explain`/`trace` still see everything); fix `wiki verify`'s routing/
>   fallback and give it full evidence instead of a 2-quote cap; run it inside `graph build` so it
>   cannot be skipped, and make `wiki audit verify` FAIL rather than only report.
> - **C — measure precision:** a real `score_fact_precision` in `eval/gold.py`; fix `_page_text`'s
>   leak; add `negative_facts` to the gold schema (assertions the wiki must NOT make) seeded from
>   this audit's findings; gate `wiki audit eval` on negative facts and precision regression; tests
>   that assert a relation is wrong — the first such tests in the repo.
> - **D — recall defects:** fix the scene pass's zero-output bug (checked first — likely recovers
>   most missing recall on its own); widen evidence windows now that A's gates prevent a wider
>   window from becoming a wider hallucination surface; diagnose the epithet miner's zero output.
> - **E — Fandom-grade pages:** restructure `page_outline` to Appearance/Personality/History/
>   Relationships/Trivia; make Appearance prose-generated instead of an infobox fragment list;

>   6 — kills a two-word quote outright), `subject_must_be_named` (subject's name must be in the
>   CITED PARAGRAPH, not just the window), `requires_both_endpoints` (new per-predicate flag on

> **A second, unplanned discovery: `wiki audit eval` itself had a real bug, found via this session's
> first eval run against the fixed data.** 17 negative-fact violations came back where only 2 should
> have. Traced to `eval/gold.py::score_fact_precision`'s original majority-keyword-overlap matcher:
> every one of this project's `negative_facts` reads "X is not a RELATIONSHIP-WORD of Y", and the two
> proper-noun keywords (X, Y) alone clear a 50% threshold whenever X and Y are related through ANY
> OTHER real predicate — which is common and correct (e.g. Enek and Lawrence never interact at all,
> but "Enek is not a friend of Kraft Lawrence" still needs checking against a real relationship
> elsewhere on the page). Two straight fix attempts both failed before landing on the right one:
> 1. Full keyword coverage (`fact_kw <= page_kw`) against the pooled page text: fixed all 15 false
>    positives but introduced FALSE NEGATIVES — a real relationship entry's `label`/`blurb` never
>    repeats the OTHER party's name (`synth/assemble.py::_relationship_entries` only puts it in
>    `entity_id`, which C2 deliberately excludes from matching), so Y's name only appeared by prose-
>    mention luck. Missed both real violations entirely.
> 2. Adding the page's own `canonical` to `_page_text` (a real, kept fix — a page's own name should
>    count as its own content) closed some of that gap, but a coincidental UNRELATED use of the word
>    "relative" in Lawrence's own Background prose ("apprenticing under a relative" — someone else
>    entirely) then falsely tripped EVERY "is not a relative of anyone-Lawrence-has-any-relationship-
>    with" check once full coverage pooled it in with entity_id-derived name matches.
> 3. **The actual fix:** `_relationship_entry_keywords()` checks each rendered relationship/
>    affiliation entry ON ITS OWN (`entity_id` + `predicate` + `label`/`note`/`blurb`, never pooled
>    with prose or with other entries) for full coverage of the fact's keywords minus the page's own
>    subject name. A negative fact is `contradicted` only when ONE SPECIFIC entry supplies both the
>    right other party AND the right relationship word together. Verified against the real run:
>    exactly the 2 genuine violations flagged, all 15 false positives cleared, confirmed both by a
>    standalone Python replay against the real `data/spice-and-wolf/05_pages/*/v02.json` files and by
>    re-running `wiki audit eval` for real. `docs/eval/gold/spice-and-wolf/baseline.json` now has
>    real `precision` numbers (mean 93%, 8/10 gold-covered characters at 100%) and a raised
>    `fact_recall` floor (mean 0.19 -> 0.338, every entity improved or held, none regressed).

### docs/vision/PHASE_24.md

Source: [PHASE_24.md](vision/PHASE_24.md). SHA-256: `cffa82705af7add220b62d78faf3adfbf84c0dccdb1ac037c1a44c3b2345511c`.

**Original line 1:**

> # PHASE_24 — Research programme: from working system to publishable contribution

**Original line 3:**

> Full entries for Phase 24. Append-only (`CLAUDE.md` §4). One-line pointers live in `VISION.md`.

**Original line 5:**

> ---

**Original line 7:**

> ## 2026-09-11 — The project becomes a research contribution; the paper's thesis and what it is not

**Original line 9:**

> **What:** `narrativewiki` is to be published at a top-tier venue (*ACL main/Findings class) within
> ~12 months, solo, on a ~$20 API budget plus one local GPU. The full strategy — feasibility
> assessment, venue ladder, engineering programme, 12-month schedule, related-work map, risk register
> — lives in `Guide to Publishing.md` at the repo root. This entry records the decisions that shape
> the code.

**Original line 15:**

> The paper's thesis is **not** "we built a pipeline and measured it." It is:

**Original line 17:**

> > Reading order is a reader-observable time axis that yields N fully-supervised knowledge states
> > from one annotation pass. That makes narrative an *instrument*: serve the same question at a
> > cutoff where it is unanswerable, and a correct answer is provably parametric memory rather than
> > retrieval.

**Original line 22:**

> Four claims: (1) the task of progressive knowledge scoping and this system as its constructor;
> (2) **Leak@t**, a metric for temporal containment, and the finding that filter-before-generate is
> necessary but *not sufficient* — implication leaks through a correctly filtered claim set;
> (3) NARRATIVEWIKI-BENCH on public-domain corpora with a graph-preserving counterfactual
> perturbation protocol; (4) the hyperlinked output as a generator of contamination-controlled
> multi-hop retrieval environments whose gold derivation chains are known by construction.

**Original line 29:**

> **Why:** the system is mature (Phases 0-23, ~700 tests) but validated on 2 volumes of 1 series, and
> its headline invariant is asserted rather than measured. Two external facts force the framing:

**Original line 32:**

> 1. **Filter-before-generate is already published.** Prior work (to verify: arXiv 2512.07474)
>    describes a "Diegetic Knowledge Graph" with a "Narrative-Present Gate" filtering spans to
>    story-time <= t before generation — i.e. `CLAUDE.md` §1. It cannot be claimed as novel. But
>    nobody has *measured* whether it works, which is where Leak@t comes from — and `CLAUDE.md` §1's
>    own reasoning ("implication leaks through redaction") is the hypothesis to test.
> 2. **The nearest agentic-retrieval environments each miss one half.** Fabricated mini-internets
>    have ground truth by construction but no real-text anchor; real-Wikipedia environments have real
>    text but are memorized. This system is the only design with both, plus a cutoff knob neither has.

**Original line 41:**

> **Implies:** seven new phases, all additive — no existing contract changes, and `graph/`, `synth/`,
> `site/`, `eval/` need no series-specific work.

**Original line 44:**

> - **Phase 24** — multi-corpus ingest + scale-out. Make `ingest/epub.py`'s chapter-heading tag
>   configurable (it hard-codes `find_all("h1")`, so a Gutenberg EPUB using `<h2>` collapses every
>   chapter into one); `corpus/package.py`; three new series configs (Sherlock, Three Kingdoms,
>   Monte Cristo); **write `tests/test_spoiler_leak.py`, which `CLAUDE.md` §1 names as the gate on
>   the one invariant that must never break and which does not exist**; full re-run of all corpora.
> - **Phase 25** — crawlable multi-page site. The reference viewer is a hash-routed SPA, so an HTML
>   crawler sees exactly one page and claim (4) cannot be evaluated. Add a `--multipage` emitter
>   beside the existing one; reuse `site/wikify.py`'s links, which already apply the cutoff filter to
>   both target and alias `first_vol`.
> - **Phase 26** — evaluation harness v2. `wiki eval` with `judge.py` (entailment), `leak.py`
>   (Leak@t), `ceiling.py` (groundedness upper bound), `kgalign.py` (triple P/R/F1, GED, centrality
>   correlation), `humaneval.py` (IAA), `report.py` (CIs, significance). The existing lexical scorer
>   stays as the cheap CI gate it was designed to be, demoted from headline metric.
> - **Phase 27** — contamination. `corpus/perturb.py` (seeded entity remap via the existing
>   Aho-Corasick automaton + paragraph paraphrase, with an alignment map so every annotation
>   transfers); `eval/contamination.py` (closed-book probing, memorization gap).
> - **Phase 28** — baselines under one fixed open-weight backbone: vanilla RAG, GraphRAG, LightRAG,
>   long-context, closed-book, plus ablations for the spoiler gate, intervals, verification and PPR.
> - **Phase 29** — the agentic environment: `eval/webtasks.py` (task generation by construction from
>   graph paths), cutoff-conditioned t1/t2 task pairs, `eval/crawler.py` (trajectory-scored harness).
> - **Phase 30** — artifact: Zenodo DOI, pinned seeds/models, **the released LLM response cache** so
>   every number reproduces with zero API spend, corpus manifests, datasheet.

**Original line 67:**

> **Rejected, with reasons** (recorded so they are not relitigated):

**Original line 69:**

> - **Event shuffling as a contamination defence** — destroys the reading-order structure that is the
>   paper's independent variable, and the mitigation literature documents a fidelity-resistance
>   tradeoff covering permutation-style strategies. The cutoff axis already provides variation
>   without incoherence.
> - **Graph isomorphism as a metric** — NP-hard and label-blind; a graph with every relation type
>   swapped is isomorphic to the correct one. Use T-F1 / G-F1 / GED / centrality correlation instead.
> - **Fandom and Wikidata as primary ground truth** — heavily memorized (incoherent as a target for a
>   contamination-controlled evaluation), whole-series scoped (punishes correct spoiler suppression),
>   and the available graphs are co-occurrence networks, not typed relations. Three-tier scheme
>   instead: human gold, derived silver with measured noise, structural correlation.
> - **A different frontier model per baseline** — confounds architecture with model budget, and is
>   unaffordable. One fixed open-weight backbone for every system, stated as a deliberate protocol.
> - **86—EIGHTY-SIX as the released corpus** — commercial EPUBs cannot be redistributed. PG corpora
>   become the benchmark; 86 and Spice and Wolf become a non-redistributable case study releasing
>   derived statistics only.
> - **Two papers (system + benchmark)** — 12 months solo is not enough for two at main-track quality,
>   and splitting weakens both. One paper, system as constructor.

**Original line 87:**

> **Status:** Planned. Phase 24 is the first implementation block.

**Original line 89:**

> ---

**Original line 91:**

> ## 2026-09-13 — Four-channel leak taxonomy replaces H1-H4; L_build measured, non-zero, zero LLM calls

**Original line 93:**

> **What:** Verified both cited papers directly (arXiv 2512.07474 full text; arXiv 2606.31946
> abstract+body). *Living the Novel*'s own architecture confirms the reframe this phase needs: "the
> system builds the Diegetic Knowledge Graph" once over the whole novel, and the Narrative-Present
> Gate is applied "at inference time" only. Their gate is a **query-time filter over a build-time
> index that already read the future.** WNM (cs.CV, different modality) asserts a "deterministic
> structural blueprint" drives its renderer and never measures obedience — the same pattern:
> *a structured control layer is asserted to constrain a generator, unverified against the channels
> that bypass the layer.*

**Original line 102:**

> `Guide to Publishing.md` §2.2's H1-H4 are replaced by a taxonomy organized by **when the future
> touched the system**, not by four unrelated hypotheses:

**Original line 105:**

> | Channel | What the future shaped | Status |
> |---|---|---|
> | L_query | which claims reach the generator | the published gate; **enforced**, see below |
> | L_artifact | page existence, `vol_end` closures, link presence (ex-H1/H2/H3) | enforced, see below |
> | **L_build** | the gazetteer, alias clusters, automaton — the index itself | **open; measured this entry** |
> | L_param | the generator's own pretraining on the source text | unaddressed; reported as a floor |

**Original line 112:**

> **H4 is retracted.** It hypothesized PPR over-selects future-important entities. Checked directly:
> `graph/ppr.py::build_subgraph` already takes only `all_edges_at(conn, upto_vol)` — the edge set is
> cutoff-correct by construction, and `tests/test_ppr.py::test_build_subgraph_filters_by_cutoff`
> already pins this. H4 as written is false. L_build (below) is what H4 was reaching for, one stage
> earlier and demonstrated with a number instead of asserted.

>   exist (R8, logged Fatal). 27 tests across L_query and L_artifact, including
>   `test_generation_input_is_independent_of_the_future`, which states §1 as a property (the
>   cutoff-t claim-set hash is a pure function of volumes <= t) rather than a procedure. All pass
>   against current behaviour: `wikify.py` and `assemble.py`'s render-time filters were already
>   correct — L_query and L_artifact are closed. `pytest -q`: 700 -> then 706 passed.

>   zero annotation); `channels/index.py` with two zero-LLM-call L_build probes:
>   `measure_candidate_mining` re-runs `entities/candidates.py::mine_candidates` restricted to
>   volumes <= t and diffs the surviving surface set against the shipped, whole-corpus-mined
>   gazetteer; `measure_vocabulary_exposure` checks whether in-scope mentions/claims rest on a

>   (`docs/probe/index_<series>.jsonl`, Part 0.3's "no paper from HTML" requirement). CLI:
>   `wiki probe run index --series <id> --volumes <range> [--json <path>]`.

**Original line 134:**

> **Found — L_build is real, and larger than expected:**

**Original line 136:**

> | Series | t | candidate_mining leak_rate | mechanism confirmed |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 86 | 1 | **0.303** (37/122 surface forms) | `min_mentions=3` and the capitalisation-ratio gate in `mine_candidates` are corpus-wide counts, computed once over whatever `--volumes` range is passed, not per-cutoff |
> | 86 | 2 | 0.190 (31/163) | closes monotonically as the cutoff approaches the range actually mined |
> | 86 | 3 | 0.050 (9/179) | |
> | 86 | 4 | 0.000 | the gazetteer's own `volumes_covered` upper bound — nothing left to leak from |
> | spice-and-wolf | 1 | 0.042 (1/24) | one surface, "Kraft Lawrence": 2 raw occurrences in v1 alone (below threshold), 4 more in v2 (6 total, clears it) — confirmed by direct text count |

**Original line 144:**

> The originally-hypothesized channel (automaton surface-form/link overlap) reads near-zero
> (`future_vocabulary_mention_rate` 0.1-0.5%, `tainted_claim_rate` 0-2.3%) because `first_vol` is
> *earliest* evidence volume, so a future entity has almost no mentions in text <= t by definition.
> `wikify.py`'s per-target, per-alias `first_vol` filter (already tested in
> `test_spoiler_leak.py::test_wikify_never_links_an_entity_introduced_after_the_cutoff`) closes that
> specific surface. **The real channel sits one stage earlier, in candidate discovery, not in link
> rendering** — `min_mentions` and word-frequency capitalisation-ratio are corpus statistics,
> computed in one `mine_candidates` call over every volume `wiki gazetteer --volumes` was given, and
> a page at cutoff 1 can carry a surface form that would never have cleared discovery from volume 1
> text alone.

> **What was actually wrong.** The 2026-09-14 (earlier) entry said render mode merges `holo`/`wisewolf`

> `wiki gazetteer --merge-epithets`, a whole-corpus LLM pass that **no `--gate=build` run has ever

> `cli.py::gazetteer`'s `--merge-epithets` branch returns at line 871, before the `--gate` branch at
> 874, so `--gate=build --merge-epithets` silently ignores `--gate` entirely — confirmed by reading
> both branches directly). The merge is an **epithet-mining artifact, not an alias-clustering one.**
> `entities/alias.py` never had the chance to unify these two identities in either gate; the epithet
> pass is what did it, and only in render mode.

**Original line 409:**

> **A sharper, second-order fact this reveals: bare `Wisewolf` (no leading "the") is not indexed to
> ANY entity in render mode**, epithets included — `the Wisewolf`-shaped patterns don't match a bare

> invisible to render-mode mention indexing. Cutoff-1 build mode, by contrast, *did* index them — as
> their own standalone `wisewolf` entity, since nothing merges it with `holo` there either.

> **Root cause of the OTHER anomaly the audit flagged — `Wisewolf` vanishing entirely at t=2, found and
> verified independently.** `entities/candidates.py::_passes_capitalisation_ratio` accepts a
> single-token candidate only if `(exact-case count) / (any-case count anywhere in the mined scope) >=
> 0.75` — a heuristic to reject sentence-initial common words that only look capitalized by accident.
> Measured directly:

**Original line 422:**

> | scope | exact `Wisewolf` | any-case `wisewolf` | ratio | passes 0.75? |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | volume 1 only (t=1's mining scope) | 17 | 20 | **0.850** | yes — candidate survives |
> | volumes 1+2 (t=2's / render's mining scope) | 34 | 49 | **0.694** | **no — candidate is dropped** |

**Original line 427:**

> Volume 2 introduces 12 additional non-exact-case occurrences (`"wisewolf"`, `"Wise Wolf"`) that
> don't exist in volume 1. Sampling them (`01_parsed/v02.jsonl`) shows a real in-narrative shift, not
> noise: volume 1 uses `Wisewolf` as a proper name the reader doesn't yet understand; by volume 2,
> now that Holo's identity is established, the text increasingly uses it as a common descriptive title
> bolted onto her name (`"Holo the Wisewolf"`, `"a canny wisewolf"`, `"the wisewolf snickered"`). **The
> candidate-mining filter is retroactively punishing volume 1's own, independently-qualifying evidence
> because of how the SAME string gets used differently once volume 2's text is added to the same
> mining pass** — the mechanism is corpus-composition-dependent, not cutoff-dependent in the sense
> the taxonomy names. This is a distinct bug/design gap from L_build (it would happen even comparing
> two render-mode runs at different corpus sizes, no cutoff filtering involved at all), not fixed
> here — flagged as a candidate for `docs/tasks/`, not fixed impulsively.

> **The pattern is systematic, not noise**: flagged-count by predicate is `ENEMY_OF` 22, `COMRADE_OF`

> against `AGE` 1, `ORIGIN` 1, `GENDER` 1, `RANK` 3, `OCCUPATION` 0. Novels show a relationship
> through scenes and dialogue rather than stating it in the predicate's own words ("comrade,"
> "rival"), so relation evidence is close to definitionally inferential; MiniCheck (built for literal
> summary-vs-source fact-checking, not narrative inference) reads that as unsupported at a much
> higher rate than attribute claims, where the source text usually states the value directly. R21's
> single confirmed win (Zheren `OCCUPATION`) is an attribute case — it was never evidence this
> generalizes to relations, and now there's a direct on-corpus measurement showing it does not, at
> least not at a flat threshold.

> **Item 4 (quote quality).** Pulled every quote already extracted for v1-2 from `events.db` and
> read them: alongside real dialogue, several were narrator prose the model mistook for a spoken
> line ("It was a common technique for buying up a commodity in advance of a higher price." —
> Marheit's business exposition, not anyone's quoted speech), and one had a narrator attribution tag
> leak into the quote text itself (`"Why do you want me to?" she shot back` extracted verbatim,
> tag included). Root cause: `ingest/epub.py`'s per-paragraph `speech` classification
> (dialogue/narration/para_raid/machine, CLAUDE.md §3 trap 4) is computed at ingest and read by
> nothing downstream (`audit/reports.py`'s stats aside) — exactly the gap this phase's own scope
> note named. Fix: `extract/scenes.py::_build_quote` now drops a quote cited from a `speech ==
> "narration"` paragraph (a hallucinated attribution, not a verbatim-check failure — the substring
> genuinely is in the paragraph, it's just not something anyone said); the extraction prompt now
> explicitly says the quote text excludes narrator attribution. Deliberately NOT applied to
> epithets/state_changes, which are legitimately narration-sourced by design (the worked example
> itself, "the wisewolf smiled," is narration).

**Original line 231:**

> **Item 6 (sarcasm/lies).** Spice and Wolf's Holo is built around teasing, boasting, and
> suspected lying, so the real corpus is a strong stress test. Checked the polarity distribution
> across all 947 v1-2 claims: `presumed`/`denied` are already used (43 of 947) and handle narrator
> hedging well ("Lawrence guessed," "was said to," explicit negation) — the existing machinery
> (`polarity_prefixed` rendering, arbitration handling) is mature. The actual gap: nothing in either
> extraction prompt (`claims.py`, `scenes.py`) ever told the model that a CHARACTER'S OWN sincere-
> sounding statement could itself be insincere (a boast, a joke, a lie) — the polarity guidance only
> covered secondhand/uncertain narration, never in-character insincerity. Fix: extended both
> prompts' polarity instruction to mark such a line `presumed` too (narration cues like "she
> teased," "he lied," "in jest" as the signal) — deliberately reuses the existing `Polarity` literal
> and downstream handling rather than adding a new schema field or a fourth polarity value, since
> the semantics ("not confirmed, take with a grain of salt") already match exactly.

**Original line 244:**

> **Item 7 (prose verbosity).** Read Holo's actual generated v2 prose: `appearance` (config cap: 4
> sentences) had 5 real sentences; `history` (cap: 12) had 15 — both comfortably under their
> `max_sentences * 280`-char validation budget, so both passed silently. The character-count check
> was a proxy for a sentence cap, not a real one. User's explicit call on the fix (asked, not
> assumed, given real design trade-offs): (1) keep `history` as a narrative chronology, tightened to
> major turning points rather than scene-by-scene transaction detail, over reverting to a
> background-only bio; (2) replace the char-count proxy with a real sentence-boundary count as the
> actual enforced ceiling, over just lowering the chars-per-sentence budget. Implemented both:
> `synth/prose.py::_count_sentences` (regex sentence-boundary count) backs `_prose_schema_for`'s
> Pydantic validator, which now rejects a response over `max_sentences` directly; only the ceiling
> is a hard gate (`min_sentences` stays a prompt instruction — undershooting is a quality nit, not
> the runaway-verbosity bug this closes). `_chronology_system_prompt` (shared by `generate_history`
> and the older `source: "events"`-dispatched `generate_chronology` path) now explicitly asks for
> major turning points and says to omit a scene's incidental logistics (exact sums, side-character
> errands, transaction place names) unless the detail IS the turning point.

> and Wolf EPUBs are 4.5× sparser, at roughly one anchor per 65 paragraphs. Print page is a usable
> *label*, not a usable *anchor*, for this series.

**Original line 50:**

> **Second trap, new:** `ingest/epub.py` stores only the `<section id>` of a chapter's *first* XHTML
> document (`:215`, `:226`), but a chapter absorbs continuation spine docs (`:218`, `:230`). v02
> chapter 0 is `chapter002.xhtml` (191 paras) + `chapter004.xhtml` (339 paras), all recorded as
> `chapter002`. Any scheme that maps a `para_id` back onto a source file by `chapter_id` is wrong for
> the majority of paragraphs. The spine href is computed at `:146` and discarded at `:147`.

**Original line 56:**

> **Decision: render a source view from `data/<series>/01_parsed/vNN.jsonl`**, one Markdown page per
> chapter per cutoff dir, each paragraph stamped `{: #nw-<para_id> }` via the `attr_list` extension
> the emitter already enables. The anchor is correct by construction because it addresses the exact
> normalized text the extractor saw — no EPUB re-parsing, no continuation-file ambiguity, no new
> dependency, and it composes with the existing cutoff filtering so `vNN/source/` can only hold
> volumes ≤ NN.

> converter binary, page-level precision only, page numbers drift with converter settings). The

> correctly-extracted, well-evidenced `MENTOR_OF` scoring 0.038.

> | stage | calls (v1-2) | shape |

**Original line 313:**

> against a model whose context is an order of magnitude larger than what each one uses.

**Original line 322:**

> **Decision:** pack several windows into one request (`windows.pack_windows`, config
> `extraction.window.max_windows_per_request`). Windows are already disjoint passages; packed ones

> every downstream check is untouched — `normalize_para_id`, the verbatim-quote test and
> `passes_evidence_adequacy` all still resolve each fact against the one real paragraph it cites.
> Measured offline against the real v1-2 corpus: **359 requests → 101 at 4 per request.**

**Original line 329:**

> The batch is bounded by a window COUNT, not only by the input budget, because the binding
> constraint is the OUTPUT cap (4096 on the free profile): facts scale with passages, p99 output is
> already 2386 tokens for a single window, and a truncated JSON costs a repair retry — spending the
> call the packing just saved. The input budget is the profile's own usable context where it
> declares one (so a local run never builds a request it cannot send) and `max_request_tokens`
> otherwise.

> - The girl at the tavern`. That is plausibly this model's own documented weakness at this stage
> rather than the packing, but plausibly is not measured, and this repo's own standing lesson is
> that a config flip is not verified until it has been smoke-tested against the model that will
> actually run it.

**Original line 345:**

**Original line 348:**

> claims, drops = claims_mod.extract_character_volume(
>     entity, vol, records, mentions, entities_by_id, settings, client, max_windows=6)
> ```

**Original line 354:**
