> `subject_must_be_named` exists precisely because chapter-major resolution is where subject
> attribution goes wrong. Packing keeps one subject per call and takes most of the win.

**Original line 360:**

**Original line 363:**

> beat and detail passes into one call (113 → 56); batch `codex_summary`, which is one *sentence*
> per call for 67 calls and is the most obviously batchable stage in the pipeline; then `verify`.
> And the standing one that costs nothing: the LLM cache is keyed on the exact prompt, so batch
> prompt-affecting config edits together — every edit to a predicate's `note:` invalidates the whole
> `claim_extract` cache, because the vocabulary block is in every prompt. Three of the four
> extraction re-runs on 2026-09-20 were full-price for exactly that reason.

**Original line 371:**

> ## 2026-09-21 — Standing rule: quality is never traded for call count

**Original line 373:**

> Maintainer instruction, in response to the packing analysis above: *"do not make any modification
> that might sacrifice quality of the output. if keeping separate multiple prompts is better then do
> that."*

**Original line 377:**

> So `max_windows_per_request` stays at **1** — one window per `claim_extract` call — and the packing
> mechanism stays as an off-by-default lever rather than something to reach for when the cap bites.
> The bar for ever turning it on is a real A/B against the routed model showing equal claim yield and
> no rise in `quote_not_verbatim`; absent that measurement, the separate prompts win by default. The
> same bar now applies to the other call-saving ideas listed above: merging `scene_extract`'s
> beat+detail passes and batching `codex_summary` are both quality-affecting and neither is to be
> done on cost grounds alone.

**Original line 385:**

> Cost savings that cannot touch quality remain fair game and are the preferred response to the cap:
> reusing the prompt-keyed LLM cache, batching prompt-affecting config edits so the cache is
> invalidated once rather than four times, running `--volumes N` in daily slices, and simply waiting
> for the 00:00 UTC reset. The cap is an operational annoyance; a quality regression is baked into
> the artifact and is far more expensive to find and undo.

> ## 2026-09-21 — `audit eval` fact recall conflates three different failures

**Original line 393:**

> Chasing the jakob/norah-arendt drops in the nex-pro prose re-run (LOG 2026-09-21) showed the metric
> is measuring three unrelated things at once, which is why it is a poor gate and why chasing a
> single number was pointing at the wrong layer each time.

**Original line 397:**

> **1. Extraction coverage (jakob — a real gap, worth fixing).** Jakob has **9** trait claims. The
> nex-pro prose used essentially all of them (formidable, cunning, crisis-seasoned, consoling,
> grand speeches, sharp-eyed, lie-detecting). The gold facts it "missed" — *"very friendly man,
> usually with a smile"*, *"treats guild members like his own sons"* — have **no claim at all**, yet
> the corpus plainly supports them: `v02:c02:p0191` "Jakob broke into a grin", `p0195` "Jakob's laugh
> rang out again", `p0229` "Jakob smiling pleasantly", `p0184` "harsh edge and warmth". 14 paragraphs
> pair Jakob with a warmth cue; extraction produced zero traits from any of them. The pattern: these
> are **narrated behaviour**, not dispositional statements, and the trait extractor only fires on the
> latter. Recall here is bounded by extraction, and no prose model can recover it.

**Original line 407:**

> **2. Prose length cap (norah-arendt — working as designed).** The opposite case: **68** claims,
> including `MOTIVATION: to become a dressmaker` (x3) and `join a tailors guild`, `formerly lived in
> an almshouse`, `watched by The Church`. The gold facts scored "not recalled" are *in the graph*.
> They are absent from the page only because `background`/`personality` prose is capped at 2-4
> sentences (CLAUDE.md §2) — a deliberate constraint. Fact recall against a full Fandom page is
> therefore **structurally bounded well under 100%**, and pushing it up would mean breaking the cap.

**Original line 414:**

> **3. Lexical synonym blindness (both).** Gold *"dreams of becoming a tailor"* vs the page's
> "dressmaker" is a miss by keyword overlap alone. Same class as the liebert case in LOG.

**Original line 417:**

> **Consequence, not yet acted on:** a single `fact_recall` float gating pass/fail cannot separate
> "we never extracted it" from "we deliberately did not print it". The gate should be split, or at
> minimum the report should mark, per missed fact, whether a supporting claim exists in the graph —
> that one bit turns the metric from a score into a diagnosis and is computable with no LLM call.
> Left as a named next step rather than built, since it changes what `audit eval` asserts.

> MiniCheck over **all 206** arbitration-scope v1-2 claims with a hypothesis template, not the five

**Original line 431:**

**Original line 436:**

> **The fork resolves against the threshold.** A separate relation cutoff would only work if the
> score separated good relations from bad ones. It does not:

**Original line 439:**

>   predicate: `ENEMY_OF` median 0.065 / p90 0.917, `FRIEND_OF` median 0.040 / p90 0.900. No cutoff
>   splits that into "correct" and "incorrect"; it only chooses how many to discard.

>   `rel:MENTOR_OF` median at **0.039** — the known-good claim sits *at its predicate's median*, so
>   for that predicate the score carries no information about correctness at all.
> - Lowering to 0.02 makes relations and attributes flag at an identical 7% — i.e. the only cutoff
>   that stops over-flagging relations is one that stops flagging almost anything.
> - MiniCheck score vs the extractor's own confidence: Spearman **+0.25** for relations (low-scorers
>   and high-scorers share an identical 0.99 median confidence). Weak evidence, since confidence is
>   near-constant across this corpus, but it points the same way.

> which is a hypothesis-template problem, not a classifier one.

**Original line 503:**

> ## 2026-09-21 — CORRECTION: the "16% sampling variance" was a window-budget bug, not sampling

**Original line 505:**

> The entry above ("The stored graph is not reproducible to within 16%") is **wrong in its cause**
> and is retracted here rather than edited, per this file's append-only rule. The numbers in it are
> real; the explanation is not. Chasing it to the bottom found a live bug.

**Original line 509:**

> **What actually happened.** Re-extracting Holo "on the byte-identical prompt" was not
> byte-identical at all, and the cache proved it: zero of the 80 new prompts matched any of the 361
> stored ones. Two separate causes, found by diffing `calls.jsonl` between runs:

**Original line 513:**

> 1. **The system prompt is identical (sha `b92cbedd`, 8788 chars), but the USER prompt changed.**
>    Commit 46e7029 (packing, shipped OFF) rewrote the per-request header unconditionally —
>    "Passage (each paragraph labeled with its id)" became "Passages (… a passage break means …)"
>    — so it invalidated the entire `claim_extract` cache for a feature that never activates.
>    Verified: 0 actual `PASSAGE_BREAK` separators in any of the 80 prompts.
> 2. **The real cause of the claim drop: `extract_volume` sized the window pool over the FILTERED
>    character list.** `allocate_window_caps` sets `total_pool = base_cap * len(mention_counts)`,
>    so passing only the targeted characters collapses the whole pool to fit them. Measured:

**Original line 522:**

>    | Holo's window cap | v1 | v2 |
>    |---|---|---|
>    | full run | 105 | 116 |
>    | `--entities "Holo"` | **40** | **40** |

**Original line 527:**

>    That is where `window_cap_truncated: 36` came from: 36 evidence windows built and then thrown
>    away before the model ever saw them. Not sampling — **a targeted top-up was reading a
>    quarter of the evidence a full run reads.**

**Original line 531:**

> **Why this one stings.** `wiki audit eval`'s own low-recall hint recommends
> `wiki extract --entities "<name>"` as the remedy. The remedy was starving the character it was
> meant to help, and it silently invalidated every targeted-vs-stored comparison made this phase —
> including the trait A/B, whose "control" was run with `--entities "Holo"` and so was never a
> control at all.

**Original line 537:**

> **Fixed** (`extract/claims.py`): the pool is sized over every CHARACTER in `all_entities`, which
> is already in scope, so a narrowed run gets the same per-entity budget as a full one. Regression
> test asserts the targeted cap equals the full-run cap; it fails `40 == 70` without the fix.

**Original line 541:**

> **What remains true from the retracted entry:** a stored baseline is still not a control, because
> prompt edits invalidate the cache and re-run costs real calls. But the reason is bookkeeping, not
> irreducible sampling noise, and the honest position now is that **run-to-run extraction variance
> at fixed inputs has not been measured at all** — the one experiment that looked like it measured
> variance was measuring this bug.

**Original line 547:**

> ### Allocation policy: researched, deliberately NOT changed

**Original line 549:**

> The cap that truncates is top-k by `mention_count`, a pointwise density score with no
> redundancy term. Three papers verified against the arXiv API and added to
> `docs/fetch_reference_pdfs.py` (section B):

**Original line 553:**

> - **BEAR** (2601.18116) frames exactly this as *budgeted evidence allocation* across items under
>   a query-time budget, via coarse-to-fine hierarchical access rather than a per-item quota.
> - **Budget-Aware Routing for Long Clinical Text** (2605.00336) compares positional, frequency and
>   diversity-aware (MMR) selection under a fixed budget and proposes RCD, a monotone submodular
>   relevance/coverage/diversity objective — the direct comparison point for top-k-by-density.
> - **EviRerank** (2411.06254) does information-density-aware adaptive budgeting per document.

**Original line 560:**

> **Not adopted, for two reasons that are measurements rather than taste.** First, 2605.00336
> reports positional heuristics beating diversity-aware selection specifically on *low-budget
> extractive* tasks, which is what this stage is; the paper does not endorse MMR here. Second and
> decisive: with the allocation bug fixed, **0 of 359 windows are discarded corpus-wide** at two
> volumes. The truncation branch never executes, so swapping its policy would be optimising a path
> that does not run. Revisit if `window_cap_truncated` becomes non-zero as volumes are added.

**Original line 172:**

> `chapter002.xhtml` (191 paras) + `chapter004.xhtml` (339 paras), all recorded as `chapter002`.
> The spine href is computed at `:146` and discarded at `:147`.

> ### 5.2 Why `audit eval` still FAILs, and why the baseline was not lowered

**Original line 262:**

> Fact recall conflates **three unrelated failures**, which is why chasing the single number kept
> pointing at the wrong layer. Diagnosed 2026-09-21 (`docs/vision/PHASE_26.md`):

**Original line 265:**

> - **Extraction coverage** — real, and the only one worth fixing. Jakob has 9 trait claims; the
>   prose used essentially all of them. The gold facts it misses ("very friendly", "treats guild
>   members like his own sons") have **no claim at all**, though the corpus plainly supports them:
>   14 paragraphs pair Jakob with a warmth cue (`v02:c02:p0191` "broke into a grin", `p0229`
>   "smiling pleasantly"). The extractor fires on *dispositional statements* and not on *narrated
>   behaviour*. No prose model can recover this.
> - **The prose cap** — working as designed. Norah has **68** claims; the "missed" gold facts are
>   in the graph and off the page only because prose is capped at 2-4 sentences (CLAUDE.md §2).
>   Recall against a full Fandom page is therefore structurally bounded well under 100%.
> - **Lexical synonym blindness** — gold "tailor" vs the graph's "tailors"/"dressmaker".

**Original line 276:**

> `wiki audit eval` now prints, per missed fact, **`in graph`** vs **`no lexical match in graph`**,
> by running the *same* matcher against the volume-filtered `claims` table instead of the page — so
> the one varying thing is page-vs-graph. The two directions are **not** equally trustworthy and the
> report says so: `in graph` is reliable; its negation over-reports (a 14-keyword gold sentence
> scores 5 against a threshold of 6 while three matching almshouse claims exist). It is deliberately
> not "fixed" by lowering that threshold, because the same rule computes the gated recall number —
> that would be tuning the metric to the desired answer. The top-up hint now fires only when some
> miss has no graph match, so it no longer recommends a full re-extract for a page bounded by the
> prose cap.

**Original line 87:**

> ### The one design decision worth not repeating by accident

**Original line 89:**

> MiniCheck is a *stricter* judge than keyword overlap, not a better one, so it is unioned in, never
> substituted. Scoring by entailment alone measured **worse** than lexical on 3 of 5 characters: it
> refuses compound gold sentences that keyword overlap passes, because entailment demands the whole
> proposition. And it is acutely chunking-sensitive — the score is a MAX over documents, so
> `liebert`'s "tense and nervous during the gold-smuggling job" scored **0.797** as one whole-page
> document and **0.059** sentence-chunked, because no single sentence entails both halves. Hence
> `gold.page_chunks`' three shapes: structured fields, each prose section (name-prefixed, since
> sections are full of pronouns), and a truncated whole-page chunk so cross-section facts still have
> one document that spans them.

> ## 3. The trap in the semantic recall pass — do not "simplify" this

**Original line 65:**

> MiniCheck is a **stricter** judge than keyword overlap, not a better one. Two measurements that
> will look like over-engineering until you re-derive them the hard way:

**Original line 68:**

> 1. **It is unioned in, never substituted.** Scoring by entailment *alone* measured WORSE than
>    lexical on 3 of 5 gold characters: it refuses compound gold sentences that keyword overlap
>    passes, because entailment demands the whole proposition.
> 2. **`page_chunks` has three shapes on purpose.** The score is a MAX over documents. One
>    whole-page document truncates at MiniCheck's 512-token window and loses the tail; fine chunks
>    break any fact needing two sections. `liebert`'s "tense and nervous during the gold-smuggling
>    job" scores **0.797** whole-page and **0.059** sentence-chunked. Hence: structured fields,
>    each prose section (name-prefixed, because sections are full of pronouns an entailment check
>    cannot resolve), and a truncated whole-page chunk.

**Original line 78:**

> Gain: `kraft-lawrence` 44→56%, `marheit` 17→33%, `norah-arendt` 30→40%, every one a genuine
> paraphrase. Cost: **0 OpenRouter requests.**

**Original line 35:**

> Two facts worth writing down because they are not obvious:

**Original line 37:**

> 1. **The gemini-3.x family is not served from `us-central1`** — it 404s. `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`
>    must be `global`.
> 2. **Thinking tokens bill at the OUTPUT rate and are drawn from `max_output_tokens`.** A 3.x flash
>    model asked for JSON under a small cap can spend the whole cap thinking and return an empty
>    string. `llm/providers/google.py` now counts them into `out_tokens` (the budget was
>    under-reporting) and accepts a `thinking_budget` profile option.

**Original line 44:**

> ### Guardrails: relaxed in number, unchanged in kind

**Original line 46:**

> - `tier: frontier` + `max_volumes: 2` still refuses any call once a run's volume scope passes 2,
>   before the provider is contacted. This is what keeps "Spice and Wolf volumes 1–2 only"
>   mechanical.
> - `max_calls_per_run` raised 20 → 2000. At 20, no real run could start; the dollar ceilings are
>   what bound spend.
> - `budget.lifetime_cap_usd` 5 → 20, `hard_stop_usd` 25 → 10 (per run), `warn_usd` 5 → 2.
> - `tests/test_config.py` kept its cost-strategy guard but changed its shape: a routed profile must
>   be either $0 **or** `tier: frontier` with a `max_volumes` cap. "Paid model, no interlock" still
>   fails the suite.

**Original line 56:**

> **Actual spend for everything in this entry, including four scene re-runs and three extraction
> re-runs: $3.13.** A single clean v1–2 pass measures ~$1.65.

**Original line 59:**

> ## 2026-09-23 (later) — Three gates were deleting good extraction, and one check had failed open

**Original line 61:**

> Switching model exposed four defects that had nothing to do with which model was routed. Each was
> found by comparing `yield.json` drop counters between runs, not by reading output.

**Original line 64:**

> 1. **`Profile.is_callable`.** Vertex authenticates with ADC and a project, never an `api_key`, so
>    `resolve_role`'s "no key → use the fallback" rule silently routed every Vertex stage back to the
>    free tier. Nothing failed; it just quietly did not happen. `fallback:` may now be a list
>    (Vertex → OpenRouter free → local), because one entry could not preserve both "prefer the free
>    tier over local" and "a machine with no keys at all still runs".

**Original line 70:**

> 2. **A gate the model was never told about.** `min_quote_words: 6` and `requires_qualifier` were
>    enforced silently: 106 facts dropped for a short quote, 163 for a bare `FRIEND_OF`. Worse,
>    `subject_must_be_named` contradicted the prompt outright — the prompt said a fact carried by a
>    pronoun "still counts … do not require the character's own name to appear", and the gate threw
>    exactly those away (342 of them). `extract/adequacy.py::prompt_rules` now generates an EVIDENCE
>    REQUIREMENTS block from the same config the gates read, so a config edit cannot leave the prompt
>    lying, and both extraction prompts include it.

**Original line 78:**

> 3. **`subject_must_be_named` was too strict to be right.** Prose carries a subject across
>    paragraph breaks with pronouns constantly. New config `subject_named_within_paragraphs: 1`
>    widens the check to the cited paragraph's immediate neighbours *within the window the model was
>    shown* (0 restores the old behaviour). The misattribution it exists to catch is still caught: a
>    neighbourhood that never names the character is not about them. Effect, replayed from cache at
>    zero cost: v01 127 → 170 claims, v02 218 → 269.

**Original line 85:**

> 4. **`wiki verify` had been failing open.** The prompt asked in prose to "list the index of every
>    fact…", so models answered with the shape the prose described — a bare array, or
>    `{"bad_facts": [6, 12, …]}`. That last one validates perfectly against `flags: []`: unknown key
>    ignored, default empty. **49 flagged facts read as "nothing flagged" and nothing raised.** The
>    prompt now states the exact JSON shape and `VerificationResult` coerces every observed variant.
>    First real run after the fix: 23 flagged facts across 11 of 15 characters.

**Original line 92:**

> Also: the scene detail prompt asked for "notable dialogue" and a literal-minded model returned 6
> quotes per span where the passage held ~40 — volume 1 kept quotes for 4 of its 11 speaking
> characters. It now asks for every line, selection being a downstream deterministic job
> (`quotes.max_quotes`). And `_DETAIL_GENERATION_OPTIONS` num_predict 8192 → 24576, because once the
> answer got long, 6 of 42 detail responses were truncated mid-JSON — and the truncated tail is
> always `participant_facts`, the last key in the response.

**Original line 99:**

> ## 2026-09-23 (later still) — Optimisations, all measured, none trading accuracy

**Original line 101:**

> - **The pipeline was entirely serial**; `concurrency:` in `config/models.yaml` was read by nothing.
>   `llm/parallel.py::map_calls` runs a stage's independent calls a few at a time, in input order.
>   Wired into candidate classification, per-character claim extraction and per-chapter scene
>   extraction. Spans inside a chapter stay serial — their quote dedup and claim merge are
>   order-dependent. Measured: a volume of scene extraction 8.5 min → 33s; `wiki extract` on two
>   volumes ~9 min.
> - **`RunContext.frontier_call_count()` was O(n²)** — it re-parsed the whole of `calls.jsonl`, full
>   prompts included, on every frontier call. Now seeded once, counted in memory.
> - **One Gemini SDK client per endpoint**, not per call: construction measured 0.6s and the first
>   request on a fresh client another ~1.5s.
> - **A 429 is "not yet", not a failure.** Vertex's shared quota answers one for minutes under a
>   parallel stage, and three attempts on a 2s ladder crashed `wiki scenes` mid-volume twice.
>   Rate-limited attempts now have their own budget (`rate_limit_retries: 8`) and their own ladder
>   (20s, 40s, …). Concurrency on `vertex_flash` settled at 4; 8 tripped the quota.

**Original line 116:**

> **Result, `wiki audit eval`, mean fact recall over the ten gold characters: 39.8% → 43.9%**, with
> precision still 1.0 everywhere and all eleven audits OK. Four floors raised in
> `baseline.json`; `yarei` left at 0.25 although it now scores 0.0, because the one fact it used to
> recall is conditional in the corpus ("Now Yarei *would be* locked in a granary … close to a week")
> and gold states it as fact — the extractor declining to assert a hypothetical is correct, so the
> WARN stays visible instead of being tuned away.

**Original line 123:**

> ## 2026-09-23 (last) — Sampling variance made this phase's own comparisons argue with themselves

**Original line 125:**

> Two prompt experiments ran after the numbers above were recorded, and together they produced the
> most useful finding of the phase — about the measurement, not the prompt.

**Original line 128:**

> **Experiment: does telling the model to work through every named character raise fact yield?**
> A/B on eight real stored detail prompts, same model, same temperature: participant_facts 17 → 24
> (subject groups 14 → 17) with quote output unchanged (469 vs 462). A clean win on its own terms.

**Original line 132:**

> **Then the full pipeline measured WORSE with it: mean gold fact recall 43.9% → 36.7%**, five
> characters regressing against the floors recorded an hour earlier.

**Original line 135:**

> **Reverting the prompt did not restore 43.9%.** The reverted run scored the same 36.7%, and its
> own cache told us why: 53 of 112 scene calls were fresh, not replays. `wiki gazetteer
> --merge-epithets` had run in between, which is the documented order (scenes → merge → extract), and
> it grows the "Known entities in this chapter" list that both scene prompts are built from. So the
> comparison was never model-vs-model at all — and at temperature 0.4 the scene pass was free to
> answer differently anyway.

**Original line 142:**

> **Conclusion, and the change that follows from it:** in structured extraction, sampling variance is
> not creativity, it is an unreproducible deliverable and a measurement that cannot be trusted to
> ±7 points. `temperature: 0.1` is now pinned in the extraction call options
> (`claims.py::_GENERATION_OPTIONS`, `scenes.py::_BEAT/_DETAIL_GENERATION_OPTIONS`); the prose stages
> keep the profile's 0.4, where a little variation genuinely reads better. The per-character-sweep
> prompt is NOT shipped: it measured better in isolation and worse end to end, and this phase has
> already learned what happens when you ship on the isolated number.

**Original line 150:**

> This is the same lesson as the 2026-09-21 "16% variance" entry in `PHASE_26.md`, one layer along:
> that one turned out to be a window-budget bug, this one is real sampling plus a prompt input that
> legitimately changes between stages. Both say the same thing — **a before/after on this pipeline is
> only valid if the whole sequence is re-run from the same starting artifacts.**

**Original line 15:**

> ## 1. What changed, in one paragraph

**Original line 17:**

> Vertex AI became available, so the maintainer authorised paid routing and asked for the project to
> be finished, cheaply, without trading accuracy. Every generative stage now defaults to
> `vertex_flash` (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) with the old defaults kept as an ordered fallback chain.
> Switching model then exposed four defects that were never about the model — a routing fallback that
> skipped Vertex entirely, three evidence gates the prompts never mentioned, and a verification pass
> that had been silently approving everything. Fixing those, plus parallelising the pipeline, took
> mean gold fact recall from 39.8% to 45.9% with precision unchanged at 1.0.

**Original line 25:**

> ## 2. The routing chain (and the trap inside it)

**Original line 27:**

> ```
> vertex_flash (gemini-3.1-flash-lite, Vertex, paid)
>   -> openrouter_free / openrouter_free_nex_pro ($0)
>      -> local_fast / local_prose / local_best (Ollama, $0)
> ```

**Original line 33:**

> `resolve_role` walks that chain and takes the first rung whose credential exists. Three things
> about it:

**Original line 36:**

> - **`fallback:` may now be a LIST.** A single value could not preserve both "prefer the free tier
>   over local" and "a machine with no keys at all still runs". The last entry is the answer when
>   none are callable.
> - **`Profile.is_callable`, not `profile.api_key`, decides each hop.** Vertex authenticates with
>   Application Default Credentials plus `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`; it has no api_key. Before this
>   property existed, the "no key → use the fallback" rule silently routed every Vertex stage
>   straight back to the free tier and nothing failed or warned. If you add another
>   credential-by-environment provider, extend `is_callable` or you will reintroduce this exactly.
> - **`GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` must be `global`.** The gemini-3.x family 404s on `us-central1`. The
>   2.5 family works at both, so a location mistake looks like "the new models don't exist".

**Original line 47:**

> `wiki doctor` prints the resolved model per stage — that is the fastest way to confirm what a run
> will actually call.

**Original line 50:**

> Measured on eight real stored `claim_extract` prompts, eight calls in parallel, same day:

**Original line 54:**

> |---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | 8/8 | 6.0s | **6.8** | none | chosen |
> | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | 8/8 | 2.3s | 2.4 | none | terser, measurably worse yield |
> | `gemini-3.5-flash` | 7/8 | 31.9s | 6.4 | 2.6k tok/call | one 429; thinking bills as output |
> | `gemini-3.8-flash` | 1 then 429 | 48s | — | — | unusable at ~700 calls/run |

**Original line 61:**

> On three sentences of wiki prose from fixed facts, all four plus `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` were
> indistinguishable. **Do not "upgrade" this profile on model-name recency.** Newer Gemini tiers in
> this project are slower, quota-starved, and pay for thinking tokens the work does not need.
> `vertex_pro` exists, unrouted, for `--model <stage>=vertex_pro` when an audit shows flash-lite is

> ### 4.1 A gate the model was never told about deletes good work

> `subject_must_be_named` while the prompts said nothing about them. Measured on one real v1–2 run:

**Original line 82:**

> `adequacy.py::prompt_rules(settings)` now generates an EVIDENCE REQUIREMENTS block from the same
> config the gates read, and both extraction prompts render it. **It is generated, not hand-written,
> so a config edit cannot leave the prompt lying.** If you add a gate, add it there too.

**Original line 86:**

> ### 4.2 `subject_must_be_named` was too strict to be correct

**Original line 88:**

> New config: `extraction.evidence_adequacy.subject_named_within_paragraphs: 1`. The name may appear
> in the cited paragraph *or its immediate neighbours inside the window the model was shown*; `0`
> restores the old single-paragraph behaviour. Prose carries a subject across paragraph breaks with
> pronouns constantly, and the strict form dropped more facts than it kept. The misattribution the
> gate exists to catch is still caught — a neighbourhood that never names the character is not about
> them. Replayed from cache at zero cost: v01 127 → 170 claims, v02 218 → 269.

**Original line 95:**

> ### 4.3 `wiki verify` had been failing OPEN

**Original line 97:**

> The prompt asked in prose to "list the index of every fact…", so models answered in the shape the
> prose described: a bare JSON array, or `{"bad_facts": [6, 12, …]}`. That second shape **validates
> perfectly** against `flags: []` — unknown key ignored, default empty — so a response flagging 49
> facts was read as "nothing wrong" and nothing raised anywhere. How long this had been true is
> unknown; the stored response proving it is in
> `data/spice-and-wolf/_runs/20260921T064854-verify-upto2/calls.jsonl`.

**Original line 104:**

> Fixed at both ends: the prompt states the exact JSON shape, and `VerificationResult` has a
> `mode="before"` validator coercing every observed variant (bare list, `bad_facts`/`flagged`/
> `indices` aliases, `index`/`i` item keys, bare ints). First run after the fix: 23 flagged facts
> across 11 of 15 characters (14 in the final clean run). `tests/test_graph_verify.py` pins it. **A check that fails open is
> worse than one that crashes** — keep the validator.

**Original line 110:**

> ### 4.4 Two prompt/budget interactions in scene extraction

**Original line 112:**

> - "QUOTES: notable dialogue" → a literal-minded model returned 6 quotes per span where the passage
>   held ~40, and volume 1 kept quotes for 4 of its 11 speaking characters. Now it asks for every
>   line; selection is downstream and deterministic (`quotes.max_quotes`). Volume 1 went 133 → 1037
>   quotes, 4 → 7 named speakers.
> - Once answers got that long, 6 of 42 detail responses were truncated mid-JSON — and the truncated
>   tail is always `participant_facts`, the last key in the response, i.e. the cap was silently
>   deleting the facts the call exists to produce. `_DETAIL_GENERATION_OPTIONS` num_predict 8192 →
>   24576. Output tokens bill only when generated.

**Original line 121:**

> ## 5. Optimisations (and the one that is a correctness fix in disguise)

**Original line 123:**

> - **`llm/parallel.py::map_calls`** — a stage's independent calls, `Profile.concurrency` at a time,
>   results in input order. `concurrency:` had been in `config/models.yaml` for months and was read
>   by nothing; the whole pipeline was serial. Wired into `entities/classify.py`,
>   `extract/claims.py` (per character) and `extract/scenes.py` (per chapter). **Spans inside a
>   chapter stay serial on purpose** — quote/epithet dedup and claim merging are order-dependent.
>   Thread-safety already existed where the shared state is (Budget's lock, RunContext's lock); the
>   disk cache needed a per-thread temp filename. A volume of scene extraction: 8.5 min → 33s.
> - **`RunContext.frontier_call_count()` was O(n²)** — re-parsing all of `calls.jsonl`, full prompts
>   included, on every frontier call. Seeded once from the file, then counted in memory.
> - **One Gemini SDK client per endpoint**, not per call (0.6s to construct, ~1.5s more for the first
>   request on a fresh one).
> - **Extraction temperature is pinned to 0.1** (`claims.py::_GENERATION_OPTIONS`,
>   `scenes.py::_BEAT/_DETAIL_GENERATION_OPTIONS`; prose stages keep the profile's 0.4). This is the
>   most important thing in this handover for anyone about to measure a change: at 0.4, **re-running
>   only the scene pass moved mean gold fact recall by 7 points in both directions with no code
>   change**, which made two of this phase's own A/Bs argue with themselves. A per-character-sweep
>   prompt that measured +41% facts in isolation shipped and then measured 7 points WORSE end to end;
>   reverting it did not restore the old number either, because `gazetteer --merge-epithets` had run
>   in between and legitimately changes the scene prompts. It is not shipped. **A before/after on
>   this pipeline is only valid if the whole sequence is re-run from the same starting artifacts.**
> - **A 429 is "not yet", not a failure.** It now has its own retry budget (`rate_limit_retries: 8`)
>   and its own ladder (20s, 40s, …), separate from `max_retries` (3) for real failures. Vertex's
>   shared quota refuses for minutes under a parallel stage; the old shared 3-attempt/14-second
>   ladder crashed `wiki scenes` mid-volume twice. `vertex_flash` concurrency settled at 4 — 8
>   tripped the quota.

**Original line 149:**

> ## 8. What is NOT done

**Original line 205:**

> - **`yarei` recall is 0.0 against a floor of 0.25, deliberately unfixed.** The fact it used to
>   recall is "held in the barn for a week"; the corpus sentence is conditional — "Now Yarei *would
>   be* locked in a granary … close to a week". An extractor that declines to assert a hypothetical
>   is behaving correctly and gold states it as fact. Fix gold's side, then re-record the floor.
>   Do not tune the floor to make the WARN disappear.
> - **`docs/REFERENCES.md` is still stale** (51 rows against 54 PDFs). Diagnosis advanced: arXiv
>   returns 200 for an API URL it has already served and 406 for every uncached one, so this is
>   server-side refusal, not a bad id and not batch size (correcting this file's earlier guess). The
>   script writes nothing on a partial fetch, which is right. Re-run
>   `python docs/fetch_reference_pdfs.py --check` on a day arXiv is answering.
> - **Scene-pass fact yield is low on this model** — roughly 60-80 raw participant_facts per volume
>   against a free-tier model's several hundred, of which ~20 per volume survive the gates. The
>   window pass (`extract/claims.py`) carries claim recall today. The obvious prompt fix was tried
>   and rejected on the end-to-end number (§5); if you try again, measure the whole sequence, twice.

>   visible on purpose.
> - **Gold still covers one series**, and the NLI hybrid from `PHASE_26.md` §5.1 is still
>   unimplemented and still the maintainer's call, for the same reason: it changes what readers see.
> - **`synthesize` and `verify` are still serial.** Both share one SQLite connection across the loop,
>   so parallelising them is not the two-line change the other three stages were. `synthesize` is
>   ~2.5 min for two volumes, so this is not urgent.

> ### The target

**Original line 38:**

> > *"the target is for the final output to have enough structurally well balanced well connected
> > information that rivals a professional wiki-fandom page."*

**Original line 41:**

> Written into `CLAUDE.md` as a new §2b. What it means concretely, and why each of these is a
> separate thing from recall:

**Original line 44:**

> - **Balanced.** Every character page carries the same sections filled to a comparable depth. A
>   page that is correct but 70 words next to one of 1,497 does not read as the same wiki.
> - **Connected.** Every named entity on a page is reachable by a link, in both directions. A
>   one-way edge — Holo's page links to Pasloe, Pasloe names Holo in plain text — is the failure
>   mode that is easiest to miss, because `wiki audit links` only checks that emitted links
>   *resolve*, never that a name that should be a link is one.
> - **Honest.** No page asserts something the text or the art does not support. This is where the
>   images work landed: a caption naming a character is a claim about the picture, and nothing in
>   this pipeline can see a picture.

**Original line 54:**

> **Decision: measure the target before improving it.** `docs/MEASUREMENTS.md` §3 is the structural
> baseline — page-length spread, per-section fill rate, link count, portrait coverage — taken today,
> before any of the changes below. Without it "rivals a fandom page" stays an opinion.

**Original line 58:**

> ### Rejected, with reasons

**Original line 60:**

> - **Giving locations and factions their own pages** (the obvious fandom-wiki move). Rejected:
>   `CLAUDE.md` §2 says only characters get unique pages, and that rule exists because a page per
>   entity multiplies the spoiler surface and the synthesis cost by the entity count. The codex
>   anchor (`/codex/<kind>#<slug>`) is already a real link target; connectivity does not require a
>   file per entity.
> - **Category pages** (`categories:` is already in every page's front matter and rendered by
>   nothing). Deferred, not rejected — it is the cheapest remaining fandom affordance, but it is
>   additive and the imbalance in §3 is the larger gap. Note that `categories` is currently `[]`
>   for Holo, so the field would need populating first.
> - **An infobox table.** Rejected as cosmetics: the `Overview` bullet strip already carries exactly
>   the structured fields an infobox would, deterministically from graph rows.
> - **Filling the short pages with prose.** Rejected outright — it is the one thing that would break
>   `CLAUDE.md` §2's "zero evidence means `null`, never an invented sentence". A 70-word page is
>   short because the corpus says little about that character, and that is the correct output. The
>   fix for imbalance, if there is one, is more *evidence* reaching synthesis, not more words.

**Original line 76:**

> ### Shipped today (all of it zero-cost — see `docs/MEASUREMENTS.md` §5)

**Original line 78:**

> Four defects, each a case where the emitter said something the data did not support:

>    Kraft Lawrence, Marheit" directly above "Adversaries: Kraft Lawrence, Yarei". Both intervals
>    are real (an employee who is also betrayed), but the reader sees a contradiction. Membership
>    now wins, in `site/bundle.py::_members_and_related` — one place, every caller.
> 2. **Codex roster names were plain text.** Now links, via a new `_entity_link`. This was the
>    one-way edge described above.
> 3. **The codex `related` bucket was information-free.** Every place and faction alike listed the
>    same four globally-central entities, because that is what personalized PageRank returns on a
>    2-volume graph. No longer rendered; still computed, still in the bundle, still in CONTRACTS
>    §6.1. Re-render it if a bigger graph makes the neighbour sets differ per entry.
> 4. **An art plate was the "portrait" of up to three different characters at once.** The v01
>    frontispiece ran at the top of Holo's, Lawrence's and Yarei's pages, captioned with each of
>    their names. `cover_image_for_entity` can only answer "which plate is nearest this character's
>    debut" — nothing here can see the image — so the fix is a cap, not a better guess:
>    front-matter plates only for the volume's two leads, and any plate on at most two pages.

> **What:** A new additive stage, `wiki infobox` (`extract/infobox.py`), fills GENDER, AGE and ORIGIN:

> depth". Before this, GENDER rendered on 2 of 14 pages, ORIGIN on 1 and AGE on 2, the fields every
> fandom infobox carries. The windowed pass misses them structurally: no single 4k window *states* a
> character's gender. Recent work points the same way. Long-context models locate scattered
> literary evidence across a whole novel far better than retrieval over fragments (Literary Evidence
> Retrieval via Long-Context LMs, ACL 2025: Gemini 2.5 Pro 62.5% vs embedding retrieval 4.5%), and
> evidence-bound extraction (Evidence-Bound Persona Extraction with LLMs, NLPIR 2025) is the
> attribution discipline this pipeline already enforces.

> ## 1. What this phase was

**Original line 9:**

> It began (2026-09-23) as a change of metric: the measure is whether the information a
> professional fandom page conveys is present **and carried in a structured form** — with the
> standing clarification that the fandom page is a *quality bar*, not a template to mimic ("a fandom
> page has X" is not by itself an argument for X; no redundancy, no dead ends, every claim
> traceable). Under that metric it went on to:

**Original line 15:**

> - restructure the repo (`STRUCTURE.md`; plans in `docs/vision/plans/`, EPUBs in `corpus/<id>/`);
> - fill infobox fields and backstory with long-context passes (`wiki infobox`, `--pass backstory`)
>   and keep verifier-withheld facts out of prose;
> - **widen from one corpus to three** at the maintainer's direction — Overlord v1–2, then
>   Ascendance of a Bookworm v1–2 — plus a public-domain Gutenberg probe;
> - make the pipeline take **any generic novel** with a three-line config;
> - build the output as **browsable HTML sites** and fix what reading them turned up.

**Original line 23:**

> ## 2. The things you must know before touching anything

**Original line 25:**

> 1. **Scope** (`AGENTS.md` §3, maintainer instructions): `--volumes 1-2` only, for exactly three
>    series — `spice-and-wolf`, `overlord`, `bookworm`. *86* is retired. **Mushoku Tensei** is
>    being downloaded into `corpus/` but is **not in scope until the maintainer says so**. A plan or
>    a handover recommending a wider run is not authorisation.
> 2. **Money.** Lifetime spend is **$12.79 of the $20 cap** (Spice and Wolf $7.13, Overlord $3.08,
>    Bookworm $2.59) — **$7.21 left**. Until 2026-09-25 the lifetime cap silently started every
>    process at $0 (it read a ledger nothing writes); it now sums every `data/<series>/budget.json`
>    (`llm/budget.py::lifetime_spent`). Earlier handovers/LOG entries quoting "$7.13 lifetime" were
>    Spice and Wolf alone. A full v1–2 pass for a new series costs **~$2.5**.
> 3. **Replay for free first.** `NARRATIVEWIKI_CACHE_ONLY=1` makes any cache miss raise instead of
>    bill. Run every rebuild under it first; only the calls it names need money. `wiki site build`
>    and `wiki synthesize` over an unchanged graph are $0.
> 4. **How to run commands on this machine.** `wiki` is not on PATH: use
>    `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m narrativewiki.cli <command> --series <id>`. Set
>    `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` (the console is cp1252; names like "Éclair" and "◆" crash prints).
>    **Always pass `--volumes 1-2` to `ingest`** — without it, it parses every volume in the folder
>    (it did once this session; cleaned up, see §4).
> 5. **Routing** is Vertex `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` → OpenRouter free → local Ollama
>    (`config/models.yaml`). A Gemini content refusal (`PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, not configurable) is no
>    longer retried: the next rung answers that one call (`llm/client.py::_call`).

> ## 4. Traps worth remembering

**Original line 64:**

> - **Silent failures were the theme.** Three of this session's bugs made no noise: the lifetime cap
>   at $0, canonicalization switching itself off after one NaN, and the eval undercounting
>   possessive facts. When a number looks too good or a stage too quiet, count the calls in
>   `data/<s>/_runs/<id>/calls.jsonl` against another series.
> - **A lexical eval cannot read direction.** Gold negative facts are matched by keywords;
>   "Myne is not Tuuli's older sister" fired on a correct page saying "Tuuli is Myne's older
>   sister". Write negatives whose words never co-occur on a correct page.
> - **Extracted qualifiers mix perspectives** ("daughter" on Myne's entry *for Effa*). Never render
>   a role from the qualifier; take it from the predicate (`family:` values in the taxonomy).
> - **First-person narrators** name people by relation: Bookworm's "Mom" (342) and "Dad" were
>   characters until a config merge; ~6 "Mom" mentions refer to other characters' mothers.
> - **The fandom wiki returns HTTP 402** to fetches. Gold facts came from search summaries and were
>   grep-verified against the text; every gold file cites the evidence paragraph.
> - **Bash heredocs on this Windows setup mangle escapes** in embedded Python (`\n`, `\b` became
>   real newline/backspace characters in written files twice). Use the Edit tool for any edit
>   containing a backslash.
> - **An `ingest` without `--volumes`** wrote every volume of Spice and Wolf (24) and Overlord (16).
>   It was cleaned (files, images, manifests back to v1–2, md5-verified) — but `ingest` records no
>   provenance run, so `wiki rollback` cannot undo it.

**Original line 19:**

> **Novelty, checked against the literature on 2026-09-25:**
> - Renaming entities to defeat memorisation is **established method, not a contribution**
>   (WHODUNIT 2502.07747; ∞Bench; name-cloze memorisation, Chang et al. 2023; OWL 2505.22945).
> - Rephrased samples evade n-gram contamination checks (2311.04850). Paraphrase is therefore a
>   treatment whose effect has to be measured, not assumed.
> - *Living the Novel* (2512.07474) reports near-perfect timeline coherence on *Twenty Thousand
>   Leagues Under the Sea*: one book, one cutoff, 100 questions, an LLM judge, and **no control for
>   the base model having memorised the book**.
> - TimeChara (2405.18027) shows LLMs leak future knowledge in point-in-time role-play. That is
>   parametric-only: no retrieval gate, no decontamination.

**Original line 30:**

> **Candidate central claim (proposed, awaiting maintainer pick):** a filter-before-generate gate
> closes retrieval leakage but not parametric leakage. On a memorised classic, the residual leak
> is the generator's own memory. Decontamination is the treatment, and it is measured, not assumed.
> The design is a 2×2: {original, decontaminated} × {gated pipeline, ungated/long-context}, with
> Leak@t across all cutoffs, plus memorisation probes (name-cloze, title identification) run before
> and after remapping, which show how much recognition survives. Supporting contributions: a
> spoiler-scoped QA set built from the claim graph's `first_vol` labels, and an agent that browses
> the cutoff-t site. Full reasoning is in the 2026-09-25 session reply.

**Original line 41:**

> **First novel: *Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea*** (Gutenberg #164). It is the book
> *Living the Novel* evaluated on, so the comparison is on the same text. Its two Parts give a

**Original line 45:**

> - **Cutoff unit = the book's own Parts**, via `source.volume_breaks` (regexes on chapter
>   titles). Rejected: chapter-level cutoffs, because they would need the volume axis re-plumbed
>   through every stage and the interlock. Rejected: splitting the EPUB file, which is fiddly and
>   loses provenance to the Gutenberg original.
> - **Decontamination runs on parsed records, not EPUBs.** A decontaminated series has the same
>   `para_id`s as its source, so every measurement is paired paragraph by paragraph (CONTRACTS
>   §1.6). `wiki ingest` refuses such a series, because parsing its EPUB would write the original text.
> - **Three conditions, not two.** Adding a remap-only series (`paraphrase: false`) tests the
>   prior practice directly and costs $0.
> - **Remap before paraphrase, and again after.** The paraphraser never sees an original name,
>   so it cannot anchor on the book, and a name it restores from memory is caught.
> - **The entity map is hand-reviewed config**, seeded from `mine_candidates` (174 surfaces →
>   22 entries). Real places and historical people are story facts and stay. Rejected: generating
>   the map from the gazetteer, because a wrong automatic entry silently changes a fact.
> - **Memorisation probe = Chang et al.'s name cloze plus title identification**, aligned by
>   `para_id`. Its key number is *source recall*: the original name given for a decontaminated
>   passage. The remap-only cloze is unscored because its masked passage equals the original's.
>   Title answers are scored book-level and author-level, because wrong-book Verne answers are common.

> ## 4. Findings so far (hand-verified; MEASUREMENTS §43–45)

**Original line 61:**

> - **Renaming does not stop recognition.** A book is identified from name-remapped passages 55.7%
>   (Gemini) / 67.0% (Qwen 14B); after remap + paraphrase, 34.7% / 30.7% (paired 101 items). Gemini
>   still gives the original character name for 48.5% of paraphrased, renamed cloze passages
>   (majority-guess baseline 21.7%).
> - **Fact transfer is what decontamination stops.** Part Two facts on a name-only page: 32% on the
>   original (Gemini and Nemotron alike), 0% on renamed text. With Part One in context the
>   generator barely leaks: 0–4%, one Atlantis witness.
> - **The gated pipeline leaks 0/25** Part Two facts on its v01 pages (control recall 87.5%).
> - **Identity disclosure is a second channel, and it is model-dependent.** Nemotron writes the real
>   identity on 4/12 remap and 4/12 decon pages ("In the original French text, this character is
>   **Ned Land**"), even when told to use only the text. Gemini: 0/24.
> - **Instrument limits.** MiniCheck errs both ways on page-level leak detection, and it cannot
>   judge paraphrase fidelity (E0b read 46.5% on faithful pairs). Every positive above was read
>   by hand. Memorisation item sets differ slightly per condition; compare on the paired
>   intersection.

**Original line 43:**

> - `measure_future_fact_leak(series_id: str, upto_vol: int) -> dict[str, Any]`
>   - Connect via `graph.store.connect()` (default `graph_db()` path — no `db_path` override needed,
>     `paths.set_active_series`/the caller already points `paths.graph_db()` at the right series).
>   - `future_claims = probe.futureset.future_claims_at(conn, upto_vol)`. If `graph.db` does not
>     exist, let the resulting `sqlite3` error propagate (same "let FileNotFoundError/equivalent
>     propagate, the caller decides what to do with it" contract `measure_candidate_mining` already
>     follows — see `probe/channels/index.py`).
>   - For each future claim, the "leaked value" to search for is:
>     - attribute/trait kind (`claim["value"]` is not null): the literal `value` string.
>     - relation kind (`claim["object"]` is not null): the OBJECT entity's `canonical` name — look
>       it up from the `entities` table (`SELECT canonical FROM entities WHERE entity_id = ?`).
>       Skip (do not count in the denominator) a claim whose object entity_id has no `entities` row
>       — should not happen in practice, but do not crash if it does.
>   - Build one big search corpus: for every `data/<series>/05_pages/*/v*.json` file with a cutoff
>     `<= upto_vol` (use `synth.cache.previous_page` semantics — the file exactly AT `upto_vol` if
>     `paths.page_json(entity_id, upto_vol)` exists, else the nearest cutoff below it via
>     `synth.cache.previous_page(entity_id, upto_vol)` — read that function before reimplementing
>     it, it already does the "walk downward to the nearest real file" logic you need for the
>     fallback half), concatenate these fields into one search string per character (skip a
>     character with no page file at or below this cutoff — nothing to search):
>     - `page.get("lead")`
>     - every `page["prose"][key]["text"]`
>     - every scalar `fields` entry's `["value"]` (the `age`/`status`/`rank`/`origin`/`occupation`/
>       `gender`-shaped single-valued ones) — CONTRACTS §5's example
>     - every list-valued `fields` entry's items' `["value"]` (`title`/`nickname`/`appearance`-shaped)
>     - `fields["relationships"][]["blurb"]`
>     - `fields["affiliations"][]["role"]`
>   - `leaked_count` = number of future claims whose search string is found as an exact (case-
>     sensitive) substring anywhere in the concatenated corpus. Case-sensitive, matching this
>     project's existing verbatim-search convention (`scripts/probe/reanalysis_first_occurrence.py`'s
>     Tier A) — do not add fuzzy/case-insensitive matching, that is Tier B territory this task does
>     not need.
>   - Return a dict shaped like `channels/index.py`'s probe rows (read one of those functions'
>     return statements for the exact convention) with these keys: `channel: "L_query"`,
>     `probe: "future_fact_leak"`, `series`, `upto_vol`, `future_claims_total` (the denominator —
>     count of future claims that had a searchable value/object, per the skip rule above),
>     `leaked_count`, `future_fact_leak_rate` (`leaked_count / future_claims_total`, or `0.0` when
>     the denominator is `0` — do not raise a `ZeroDivisionError`; `upto_vol == max volume` on a
>     2-volume corpus has no future claims at all, and that is an expected, valid input, not an
>     error).

**Original line 13:**

> ## 1. Why this task exists

**Original line 15:**

> `docs/vision/PHASE_24.md`'s 2026-09-14 (late pm) entry root-caused why bare `Wisewolf` (17
> occurrences in v1, well clear of `min_mentions=3`) is its own candidate entity at cutoff `@t01` but
> **vanishes entirely** — not merged into `holo`, just gone — once volume 2 is added to the same
> mining pass (`@t02` and render mode both). The entry explicitly left the fix undecided: "flagged as
> a candidate for `docs/vision/plans/`, not fixed impulsively." This task files that.

**Original line 21:**

> ## 2. The mechanism (verified against `entities/candidates.py::mine_candidates`, not re-derived)

**Original line 23:**

> `_passes_capitalisation_ratio` accepts a single-token candidate only if
> `(exact-case count) / (any-case count anywhere in the mining scope) >= _ALWAYS_CAPITALISED_RATIO`
> (0.75). Both the numerator (`agg[surface]["count"]`) and denominator (`word_freq[surface.lower()]`)
> are accumulated in one pass over every volume in the `volumes` dict the caller passes in — there is
> no per-volume reset. Measured directly:

**Original line 29:**

> | mining scope | exact `Wisewolf` | any-case `wisewolf` | ratio | passes 0.75? |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | volume 1 only | 17 | 20 | **0.850** | yes |
> | volumes 1+2 | 34 | 49 | **0.694** | **no** |

**Original line 34:**

> Volume 2 adds 12 non-exact-case occurrences (`"wisewolf"`, `"Wise Wolf"`) that don't exist in volume
> 1 — a real in-narrative shift (v1 uses `Wisewolf` as a proper name the reader doesn't yet understand;
> by v2, now that Holo's identity is established, it increasingly reads as a common descriptive title:
> `"Holo the Wisewolf"`, `"a canny wisewolf"`). The filter retroactively drops volume 1's own,
> independently-qualifying evidence because of how the same string gets used once more text joins the
> same mining pass. This is corpus-composition-dependent, not cutoff-dependent — it would reproduce
> comparing two render-mode runs at different corpus sizes, no `--gate=build` involved at all.

**Original line 42:**

> **Not a leak.** This does not put a future fact in front of a cutoff-`t` reader; if anything it
> removes an entity a reader legitimately could infer, so it is a recall/completeness defect, not a
> `tests/test_spoiler_leak.py`-class safety defect. It does, however, make the entity set
> **non-monotonic across cutoffs** (present at `@t01`, absent at `@t02`), which nothing in the design
> predicts and which complicates every future `--gate=build` vs. render comparison — see
> `docs/vision/PHASE_24.md` 2026-09-15 for the one channel (`measure_candidate_mining`'s `leak_rate`)
> already confirmed structurally immune to this.

**Original line 50:**

> ## 3. The decision — two options, not resolved here

**Original line 52:**

> **Option A — per-volume-OR-across-volumes.** Compute the ratio within each volume separately;
> keep the candidate if it clears 0.75 in *any single volume* it appears in, even if the pooled
> corpus-wide ratio would fail it. Rationale: once a word has independently earned proper-noun status
> from one volume's own text, later volumes using it more loosely shouldn't erase that evidence.
> Risk: a word that is a common noun everywhere except one biased paragraph (e.g. three consecutive
> sentence-initial "Wolf/Wolf/Wolf" in one action scene) could pass on weak grounds it currently fails
> on correctly, pending the sentence-initial safeguards (`agg`'s `signals` set) actually catching it.

**Original line 60:**

> **Option B — leave it corpus-wide, treat non-monotonicity as a documented, named property of the
> taxonomy** (a reader's own sense of what's a proper noun really is corpus-dependent — that's not
> obviously wrong) rather than a bug. Add a `wiki audit gazetteer` warning when a `@tN` cutoff's
> candidate set loses a surface a smaller cutoff had, so it's visible instead of silent, and cite the
> behavior explicitly in `docs/vision/PHASE_24.md` as an accepted taxonomy dimension for the paper
> (a fifth leak-adjacent phenomenon, distinct from L_build/L_extract/etc.) rather than something to
> suppress.

**Original line 68:**

> **Recommendation (not a decision — the maintainer's, since it changes candidate-mining behavior and
> every already-published `docs/probe/*.jsonl` number derived from it): Option A.** A reader who has
> finished volume 1 does not un-learn that `Wisewolf` is Holo's name because volume 2 exists; an index
> that can is measurably wrong in a way Option A directly fixes, and Option B mostly just accepts a
> recall regression instead of fixing it. But Option A is a behavior change to a function three
> already-recorded headline numbers (0.303→0.033, 0.982→0.954-class corrections, this task's own
> 0.042→0.000) were measured against, so re-running the zero-cost probes after the change and
> diffing against `docs/probe/*.jsonl` is mandatory before calling it done, not optional cleanup.

> | Priority / issue | Evidence and cause | Consequence / direction |
> |---|---|---|
> | P0: evaluation measures the wrong universe | `eval/gold.py::_page_text` reads fields/prose/quotes but omits `traits`; `score_fact_precision` counts selected gold hits against selected forbidden relations. Synthetic ability recall is missed; an extra unjudged assertion does not reduce precision. | Add semantic fact-level and publication-level coverage; keep legacy metrics clearly labeled. Source-ground the evaluation set. |
> | P0: polarity is lost or strengthened | Invalid `ExtractedFact` polarity defaults to asserted. Pair and codex projection do not share character-page polarity handling. Live Zheren/Lawrence pair loses the presumed label while retaining a “suspected” qualifier. | Quarantine invalid modality; share one publication policy for every surface. Preserve presumed/denied semantics in data. |
> | P0: temporal reads disagree | `temporal.relations_at` does not filter interval ends, while `relations_between` does. `_relation_entries_between` copies future ends into public bundle metadata. Synthetic witnesses reproduce both. | Separate current/history APIs and scrub future endpoints centrally, including JSON and indexes. |
> | P0: verification is not a shared, versioned publication decision | `_is_renderable` permits absent verdicts and ignores verdict cutoff. Stored historical verdict cutoffs are null. Character, trait, related, codex and pair readers implement separate checks. | Key review decisions to assertion/evidence/policy/cutoff; distinguish unreviewed from supported; test every public consumer. |
> | P1: claim identity conflates different observations | `make_claim_id` excludes polarity, qualifier and occurrence; `_merge_claim` unions evidence but retains the first semantic fields. | Preserve source observations, then derive assertions with explicit equivalence. Do not let deduplication choose truth. |
> | P1: volume is too coarse for narrative change | `_resolve_single_valued` groups by volume; the standing rule treats same-volume disagreement as extraction error and cross-volume disagreement as change. | A character can move, learn or change allegiance within one volume; a later passage can disclose an earlier event. Propose source-order and disclosure-aware state handling. This changes a standing semantic rule and needs explicit acceptance before implementation. |
> | P1: ontology pressures incorrect assignments | Existing dev fixture includes INFLUENCE, REPUTATION, DEPICTION, NAMESAKE and PATRONAGE gaps. BACKGROUND can carry text but does not solve typed assignment. Traits expose SKILL/PERSONALITY overlap. | Add only witness-justified predicates, type/cardinality rules and explicit unmapped candidates; keep unsupported interpretations out of published fields. |
> | P1: ambiguity is resolved too early | The mention automaton keeps the alphabetically first exact-surface claimant. `resolve_surface` can abstain, but cannot recover a discarded candidate upstream. Global alias grouping can carry future identity knowledge. | Preserve candidate sets and scope identity/alias evidence; resolve locally or abstain. Measure actual collision/misattribution cases before adopting a large coreference model. |
> | P1: prose/event summaries have weaker evidence contracts | `graph/events.py` documents `beat_summary` as ungated; generated prose uses pooled citations. A verified graph does not verify a newly generated sentence. | Attach sentence/atom-to-evidence links and explicit support status; build progression from validated event/state records. |
> | P2: deduplication is not semantic equivalence | The ledger's Holo skill comparison shows no cosine threshold separating duplicates from meaningful sound/scent differences. | Embeddings may propose candidate pairs; entailment/review must decide equivalence, directionality and preserved qualifiers. |
> | P2: presentation heuristics can assert more than evidence | Image proximity and reuse caps do not identify depicted characters. Roster precedence can hide coexistence of roles/conflict. | Use only reviewed depiction links for portraits; keep association types and episode context in structured data. Do not invent connectivity. |

> ## 5. Research-informed choices

**Original line 149:**

> The exact paper-to-work-package mapping is in the research record; these are bounded adaptations,
> not claims to have implemented or reproduced the papers.

**Original line 152:**

> - **CHIRON (2024), §4–5:** character/category questions can help discover nuanced facts, followed
>   by validation. Adapt only as a targeted top-up after proving a source-supported gap. Its
>   narrative-specific validation motivates calibrating our verifier; do not copy its ontology or
>   train a model by default.
> - **STAGE v9 (2026), §3.1.2, §3.2.1, §3.3:** preserve evidence-linked state developments and
>   evaluate checkpoint changes separately from current state. Adapt progression and no-change
>   controls; do not import its movie corpus or role-playing scope.
> - **EvolvTrip v1 (2025), §3.3–3.4:** distinguish attributed mental states and their evolution.
>   Adapt explicit belief/report qualifiers; its own limitations argue against treating inferred
>   psychology as exhaustive factual triples.
> - **E²RAG v1 (2025), §4:** keep context-specific entity occurrences connected to events. Adapt
>   occurrence-to-event provenance within existing SQLite stores, not its complete retrieval stack
>   or name-in-generated-summary linking heuristic.
> - **MiniCheck (2024), §2 and Limitations:** evidence support is useful but does not establish
>   absolute truth or distinguish every contradiction. Calibrate the existing local support path
>   on attribution, negation, temporal and narrative context; retain human review for ambiguity.

**Original line 169:**

> No paper's headline performance is a target or a measurement of this project.

**Original line 171:**

> ## 6. Order of work and success criteria

**Original line 173:**

> 1. **Establish trustworthy measurement and regression witnesses.** Freeze current artifacts;
>    evaluate extraction, classification, assignment, temporal interpretation, publication and
>    citations separately. Extend task 0006's existing witness report instead of restarting it.
> 2. **Repair shared publication semantics.** Fix polarity, expired relations, future metadata and
>    verdict reuse. Add tests across all consumers and future-input invariance tests.
> 3. **Preserve observations and model changes correctly.** Introduce schema versions, semantic
>    identity and evidence-bound review records; trial within-volume changes in a shadow database.
> 4. **Repair taxonomy and entity resolution where witnesses justify it.** Classify, resolve and
>    deduplicate existing evidence before paying to extract more.
> 5. **Recover genuinely missing supported information.** Run isolated prompt/top-up experiments
>    on stored passages, following task 0006's existing holdout and approval boundaries.
> 6. **Publish coherent progression and provenance.** Derive per-volume change records and concise
>    supported prose from the safe dataset; independently validate generated event summaries.
> 7. **Confirm once end to end on the authorized corpus.** Promote only after focused tests,
>    reviewed precision/coverage comparison and cutoff checks pass.

**Original line 189:**

> Release gates are distinct: zero known high-severity attribution/polarity/spoiler failures in the
> reviewed regression set; all published structured assertions have eligible evidence and review
> status; missed source-supported facts and unresolved cases remain counted; no gains created by
> duplicate paraphrases or relabeling unknowns. Report coverage and support with denominators,
> sample scope and reviewer agreement. Passing a finite set is never a proof of universal safety.

**Original line 195:**

> ## 7. Boundaries and decisions still needed

**Original line 197:**

> - This is an implementation plan, not authorization to expand beyond the existing series/volumes.
> - Explicit acceptance is needed before replacing the standing contradiction semantics or changing
>   default release handling of unreviewed facts. Fixtures and a shadow implementation can be
>   prepared first; leave the conflict recorded rather than silently shipping a reinterpretation.
> - Task 0006's passage-transfer approval remains separate from downloading public papers. This
>   review neither spends it nor bypasses it. No new paid run is needed to begin the plan.
> - Larger models, a new vector database, graph database migration, full-corpus coreference,
>   multi-agent extraction, more volumes, more website sections and model training are deferred
>   unless the measured bottleneck warrants them.

**Original line 207:**

> The first deliverable is an honest diagnostic and a shared publication boundary. Once those are
> reliable, improvements in structured coverage will mean better information rather than a more
> convincing presentation of the same errors.

> ## 1.1 What it is actually doing

**Original line 27:**

> `entities/automaton.py` is multi-pattern exact string matching over an **enumerable, finite pattern
> set** — every `surface_forms[].text` in `gazetteer.json` — with two project-specific rules bolted on
> (`_is_boundary_match`, so `Shin` never fires inside `Shining`; `_resolve_overlaps`, longest-match-wins).
> It has four consumers, not one:

**Original line 32:**

> | Consumer | What it needs from the automaton |
> |---|---|
> | `index_mentions` → `mentions.jsonl` → `extract/windows.py` | exact `(para_id, start, end, surface, entity_id)` offsets |
> | `site/wikify.py` (via `site/bundle.py`) | the same, over already-generated prose, to place links |
> | `probe/channels/index.py::measure_vocabulary_exposure` | per-surface `first_vol` over an enumerable vocabulary |
> | **Planned** `corpus/perturb.py` (Phase 27, `PHASE_24.md` 2026-09-11) | a **reversible** entity remap with an alignment map so every annotation transfers |

**Original line 39:**

> It costs $0 and runs one linear pass per gazetteer build. Current scale: 86 has 163 entities /
> 211 surfaces at 4 volumes; extrapolating linearly, ~500 entities / ~700 surfaces at 13. That is
> three orders of magnitude below where any AC implementation starts to care.

**Original line 43:**

> ## 1.2 The five properties the research programme is resting on it for

**Original line 45:**

> 1. **Enumerability.** "What does the index know at cutoff *t*" is a finite, printable set of strings.
>    This is what makes `probe/channels/index.py` a *diff* rather than an estimate.
> 2. **Decidability of the counterfactual.** "Could a cutoff-*t* reader have seen this string?" is
>    answerable by verbatim search over `01_parsed` — literally what
>    `scripts/probe/reanalysis_first_occurrence.py` does, and the only reason the 0.303 → 0.033 correction
>    was possible. This works *because* matching is exact-string. Under any approximate matcher the
>    question becomes "is cos-sim above τ", which is not a fact about the text.
> 3. **Determinism.** Same gazetteer + same corpus → byte-identical `mentions.jsonl`. No seed, no
>    temperature, no model version. This is what makes the Phase 30 artifact claim ("a reviewer
>    reproduces every number with zero API spend and no GPU", `docs/archive/GUIDE_TO_PUBLISHING.md` §3.2) true for
>    this stage.
> 4. **Zero marginal cost.** §3.3 already names GPU wall-clock as the binding constraint at
>    150k–200k local calls. Anything that adds calls here multiplies by (corpora × variants × cutoffs).
> 5. **Invertibility.** A match is an exact offset span. Substitution is reversible; an alignment map
>    is trivially derivable.

**Original line 61:**

> ## 1.3 The alternatives, against those constraints

**Original line 63:**

> | Alternative | Auditability | Cost | At 13 vols / new series | Verdict |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | **Pure-LLM mention detection per window** | Destroys all five. The index's knowledge becomes model weights — unenumerable, and the detector has read the whole series in pretraining, so L_build becomes L_param by construction | Adds O(windows) calls per cutoff per corpus; under `--gate=build` × 13 cutoffs × 3 corpora × 2 variants this is the single largest line item in the whole programme | worse, superlinearly | **Reject outright.** This would end Claim 2. |
> | **Embedding / ANN fuzzy matching** (`ollama.py::embed()` already exists, so it *is* cheap) | Loses 1, 2, 5. The similarity threshold τ is itself a corpus-wide statistic — i.e. it reintroduces the exact `min_mentions` bug the probe just spent two sessions locating, one level up and harder to see | cheap-ish but non-zero; embeddings must be recomputed per cutoff under Mode B | threshold needs recalibration per series → a new unaudited free parameter per corpus | **Reject as a replacement.** Correct as a *separate retriever arm* — see §1.5. |
> | **Plain trie, hand-rolled** | identical | identical | identical, slower | No gain. This is roughly what the existing pure-Python fallback branch already is. |
> | **`regex` / `re` alternation over ~700 literals** | identical | identical | degrades with pattern count; no native longest-match-wins across alternatives without ordering hacks; escaping is a new failure surface | No gain, strictly more fragile. |
> | **FlashText** | identical | identical | AC-equivalent trie, pure Python (slower than the C ext), effectively unmaintained, and it bakes in *its own* word-boundary notion — replacing `_is_boundary_match` is a silent behaviour change for zero benefit | No gain. |
> | **spaCy `PhraseMatcher`** | **worse.** Requires tokenization that must agree with this corpus's quirks (para-RAID spans, `<<…>>` machine voice, em-dash-as-image). That inserts a new, corpus-dependent, version-pinned component *into the auditable path* | new ~50MB+ dependency and a model download | a tokenizer trained on newswire on a translated LN corpus is an unmeasured error source per series | **Reject.** Moves backwards on the one axis being published. |

**Original line 78:**

>    a citable, shippable file rather than something recomputed from the gazetteer each time. ~15

> 3. **Stop silently dropping ambiguous surfaces.** `build_automaton` adds a colliding surface to
>    whichever entity comes first under `sorted(entities, key=entity_id)` — an alphabetical,
>    silent, unmeasured loss. At 13 volumes and three new series, collisions rise. Minimum fix:

>   a different thing entirely. A diary study would cost months and buy nothing at the target venue.
> - **Dual-level (low/high keyword) query decomposition via a 4B LLM.** A conversational-retrieval
>   trick. Narrativewiki renders pages; it does not serve queries. Only becomes relevant if Claim 4
>   (the agentic environment) is revived — and that is explicitly deferred to paper 2.
> - **The Narrative-Present Gate itself.** Already implemented, and the entire premise of Phase 24 is

### docs/vision/plans/0009-parametric-leakage-gutenberg.md

Source: [0009-parametric-leakage-gutenberg.md](vision/plans/0009-parametric-leakage-gutenberg.md). SHA-256: `3961ce91abff70e30c1af1c315f6114467441f63e10a252c22c23111a619a1d8`.

**Original line 1:**

> # PLAN 0009 — Parametric spoiler leakage on decontaminated Gutenberg novels

**Original line 3:**

> **Status:** living plan, opened 2026-09-25 (Phase 31). Decision record: `docs/vision/PHASE_31.md`.
> Papers: `docs/papers/PAPERS.md` §G. Every number lands in `docs/MEASUREMENTS.md` first.

**Original line 6:**

> ## Claim the paper is built around

**Original line 8:**

> A filter-before-generate spoiler gate stops future facts the system *retrieves*. It does not stop
> future facts the generator *remembers*. On a memorised classic, the leak that remains is
> parametric. Renaming the characters, the standard fix (WHODUNIT, InfiniteBench), is a treatment
> whose effect has to be measured. We measure it, and paraphrase on top of it, per cutoff.

**Original line 13:**

> Closest prior work: *Living the Novel* (2512.07474), 90.8% timeline coherence on *Twenty Thousand
> Leagues*, with one cutoff, 100 questions, an LLM judge and no memorisation control. TimeChara
> (2405.18027) shows parametric future-knowledge leakage in role-play, with no gate and no
> decontamination.

**Original line 18:**

> ## What the first novel says (2026-09-25, MEASUREMENTS §43)

**Original line 20:**

> | gemini-3.1-flash-lite, t = 1 | Original | Names remapped | Names + paraphrase |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Book identified from a passage | 99.1% | 55.7% (Qwen 14B: 67.0%) | 33.9% |
> | Original name recalled for a masked stand-in | 57.4% (cloze) | n/a (same passage) | **51.3%** |
> | Part-Two facts on a name-only page (hand-verified) | **32%** | 0% | 0% |
> | Part-Two facts on a Part-One-context page, unguarded / guarded | 4% / 0% | 0% / 0% | 0% / 0% |

**Original line 27:**

> **The sharper claim this suggests: recognition is not leakage.** Contamination work measures
> recognition (cloze, title identification), and by that measure standard decontamination
> fails: the model still recalls "Nemo" for 51% of renamed, paraphrased passages. The harm that
> matters for a spoiler-safe system is fact transfer, and on these pages it drops to zero once
> names change, even though recognition survives. Full-text context also anchors the model on
> the original text (0–4%). What is left untested is the one place memory has room: the gated
> pipeline's claim-to-prose prompts, where a sparse character gets a few claims and a name (E2).
> That run decides whether the paper says "gates suffice once names are remapped" or "gates leak
> through thin prompts, and remapping is what closes it".

**Original line 37:**

> ### Update 2026-09-26: a second model changes the story (MEASUREMENTS §45)

**Original line 39:**

> | Hand-verified, t = 1 | Gemini flash-lite | Nemotron-3-ultra (free) |
> |---|---|---|
> | Part Two facts on a name-only page, original | 32% | 32% |
> | Part Two facts on a context page, original (guarded / unguarded) | 0% / 4% | 4% (implication) / 0% |
> | Part Two facts, remap or decon, any mode | 0% | 0% |
> | Pages naming the **original book or characters**, remap / decon | 0/12 / 0/12 | **4/12 / 4/12** |
> | Gated pipeline v01 pages, original (E2) | 0/25 | not run |

**Original line 47:**

> **Two leak channels, not one.** *Fact transfer* (future plot facts) is what decontamination
> removes, and it did for both models. *Identity disclosure* is new: a strong model de-anonymises
> renamed and paraphrased text and writes the real identity on the page ("In the original French
> text, this character is Ned Land"), even when told to use only the text. For a spoiler-safe
> wiki that is a leak in itself, because a reader who learns the source can look up its ending.
> It is **model-dependent**, which is the argument for a multi-model protocol. The paper's claim
> becomes: *decontamination suppresses fact transfer but not recognition; whether recognition
> reaches the page depends on the generator, so it must be measured per model.*

**Original line 56:**

> ## Conditions (one series each, same `para_id`s — CONTRACTS §1.6)

**Original line 58:**

> | Condition | Series | Built by | Cost |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Original | `leagues` | `ingest --volumes 1-2` (Part Two = v2 via `volume_breaks`) | $0 |
> | Names remapped (prior practice) | `leagues-remap` | `decontaminate` with `paraphrase: false` | $0 |
> | Remapped + paraphrased | `leagues-decon` | `decontaminate` (stage `decon_paraphrase`) | ~$0.30 |

**Original line 64:**
